issues.body:
## Security context

Strata automatically parses attacker-controlled files while browsing directories. Thumbnail and preview generation currently runs with the user's full privileges and filesystem/network access.

Relevant code:
- `src/ui/thumbnail.rs:199-289`
- `src/adapters/local_preview.rs:104-148`
- `src/ui/preview.rs:382-410`

The parser attack surface includes GdkPixbuf, Poppler, GStreamer, ImageMagick, dcraw, and ffmpegthumbnailer. A malicious file in Downloads or an archive extraction directory can reach some of these parsers merely by becoming visible.

## Proposed work

- Move untrusted thumbnail/preview parsing into a separate helper process.
- Sandbox the helper (for example with bubblewrap/landlock/seccomp):
  - no network access;
  - read-only access to only the selected input;
  - writable access only to a private output location;
  - no access to user configuration, secrets, or unrelated files.
- Apply CPU, memory, output-size, and wall-clock limits.
- Kill the complete helper process group on timeout/cancellation.
- Treat parser crashes as a failed preview without crashing Strata.
- Document which formats/providers run in the sandbox.

## Acceptance criteria

- Opening a directory cannot invoke an untrusted native parser in the main Strata process where avoidable.
- External thumbnail tools and media/PDF/image parsers have no network access or broad home-directory access.
- Malformed files, crashes, and timeouts degrade to a fallback icon/message.
- Security tests cover sandbox permissions and failure handling.
issues.title: Sandbox thumbnail and preview parsing of untrusted files

issues.body:
## Supply-chain concern

CI and release workflows reference mutable action tags such as `actions/checkout@v7`, `Swatinem/rust-cache@v2`, and `dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable`. The release job eventually receives `contents: write`, so a compromised mutable dependency could modify releases or the repository.

Relevant files:
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`
- `.github/workflows/release.yml`

## Proposed work

- Pin every third-party action to a full commit SHA, retaining the release tag in a comment.
- Pin the Rust toolchain version used for release builds.
- Configure Dependabot/Renovate to update action SHAs.
- Add artifact attestations and cryptographic signing where practical.
- Use a protected GitHub release environment with required approval.
- Minimize permissions per job and ensure write credentials are unavailable to build jobs.

## Acceptance criteria

- No workflow `uses:` entry references a mutable tag or branch.
- Release artifacts are tied to the exact source commit and have verifiable provenance.
- Only the final approved publishing job receives write permissions.

issues.body:
## Problem

New-folder creation does not apply the validation used by rename.

Relevant code:
- `src/ui/browser.rs:703-719`
- `src/adapters/local_operations.rs:172-180`

GIO resolves names such as `../escaped` outside the selected parent and treats `nested/child` as a path. A file-manager "New Folder" operation should be confined to one child of the displayed directory.

## Proposed work

- Centralize basename validation and use it for rename and folder creation.
- Reject:
  - empty names;
  - `.` and `..`;
  - `/` and any multi-component path;
  - NUL or values the backend cannot represent.
- Validate again in the operation provider, not only in the UI.
- Display the validation error inline without starting an operation.

## Acceptance criteria

- `../escaped`, `nested/child`, `/tmp/absolute`, `.`, and `..` are rejected.
- A folder can only be created as a direct child of the requested parent.
- Unit tests cover native and URI-backed locations where supported.

author: l0gicgate
body:
## Summary
- track replace/fail-if-exists decisions per transfer item
- stage local replacements in unique sibling paths and atomically exchange them with destinations
- preserve existing destinations when staging, cancellation, remote backends, or atomic exchange cannot complete safely
- replace directories without merging and clean staged files after failures

## Testing
- `./scripts/check.sh`
- injected disk-full and cancellation coverage verifies destination preservation and staging cleanup
- multi-item conflict coverage verifies late destinations are not overwritten

Closes #7

issues.body:
## Security/data-integrity problem

Replacement currently permanently deletes the destination before the new copy or move has succeeded.

Relevant code: `src/adapters/local_operations.rs:208-249`.

A failed, cancelled, disk-full, or disconnected transfer can destroy the original destination and leave an incomplete or absent replacement. In addition, the request-wide `overwrite_existing` flag can apply replacement behavior to an item whose destination appeared after the UI performed its collision check.

## Proposed work

- Track the user's replace/skip decision per source item rather than with one request-wide boolean.
- For local files, copy to a uniquely named temporary sibling first.
- Flush/close the staged output as appropriate, then atomically rename/exchange it into place.
- Do not remove the prior destination until staging succeeds.
- Define safe behavior for directory replacement/merge and remote GIO backends where atomic replacement is unavailable.
- Preserve the original destination and report a failure when safe replacement cannot be guaranteed.
- Clean up abandoned staging files after failures/cancellation.

## Acceptance criteria

- Injected copy/move failures do not lose or modify the original destination.
- Disk-full and cancellation tests verify preservation of the destination.
- A destination created after collision confirmation is not silently overwritten.
- Multi-item transfers honor each item's explicit conflict decision.

author: mrocha-montes
body:
Found this while testing something else, but it is not specific to that scenario, it reproduces for a plain local New Folder too.

## The bug

`update_basename_validation` runs on every text change, including the programmatic clears that happen when a New Folder/File prompt opens, cancels, or succeeds after creating. Since `validate_basename("")` treats an empty name as invalid, any of those routine clears can leave the field styled red before the user has typed anything wrong, or anything at all.

Repro:
1. Open New Folder, type an invalid name (for example one with a `/`), press Enter. It gets rejected in place, no dialog, field turns red. So far expected.
2. Press Escape, then open New Folder again.
3. The field is already red and empty, nothing has been typed yet.

Confirmed present on the current `main` (v0.4.0).

## The fix

Treat an empty field as the normal, unstyled starting state rather than an error state. Submission is still blocked (the function still returns `false` for an empty name), only the alarming red border for a field nobody has touched yet is gone.

Added a unit test constructing a real `gtk::Entry` and driving `update_basename_validation` directly, `check.sh` passes (142 tests).
title: Don't flag an empty name field as an error

author: mrocha-montes
body:
## Summary

- "Network" sidebar entry backed by GVfs discovery, same pattern as Trash.
- `Ctrl+L` accepts any well-formed `scheme://` URI, not just `trash:///`, so `smb://`, `sftp://`, `ftp://`, `dav://`, etc. all reach GIO instead of being rejected as "not an absolute path."
- Async auto-mount flow using a native `GtkMountOperation` for credentials. Correctly dispatches to `mount_enclosing_volume` vs `mount_mountable` depending on the GVfs entry type (they are not interchangeable).
- UNC (`\\host\share`) and SCP-style (`user@host:path`) shorthand rejected with a clear message instead of being misread as a local path, per this issue's own product decisions.
- A URI with an embedded password is rejected outright; a bare username is still accepted and prompts normally.
- A missing GVfs backend reports which package to install (e.g. `gvfs-smb`) instead of a raw GIO error.
- Cancelling the credential prompt returns quietly to the prior state, no alarming error.

Closes #5: GVfs mounts now stay URI-native everywhere a `Location` is derived from a `gio::File` (sidebar, volumes, click-to-navigate, and every child entry produced while enumerating a remote directory), instead of leaking the opaque `/run/user/$UID/gvfs/...` FUSE path.

Two more bugs found and fixed while testing against a real SMB share:
- A background directory-batch refresh could steal keyboard focus from an open New Folder/File prompt on slow network shares that stream many batches (local directories load in one fast batch, so this never showed up there).
- Creating an item on a remote location never appeared in the view until navigating away and back, since remote locations have no live directory monitor.

Also improved: Trash on a backend that doesn't support it (SMB has none) now explains that and suggests permanent delete, instead of surfacing a raw GIO error.

## Not included

Left for later slices per this issue's own scope: SFTP/FTP/WebDAV-specific testing (the code is protocol-agnostic through GIO, but only verified against SMB), saved Connections UI/persistence, a Disconnect action, and capability-gated hiding of unsupported operations like Trash.

## Testing

161 automated tests (`./scripts/check.sh` clean), plus manual end-to-end testing against a real SMB share on my LAN. Recording attached in a follow-up comment.

---

One more thing: I'll be away from this for a bit starting tomorrow, work week kicking off. No rush reviewing, take your time. Good luck with everything!

issues.body:
## Context

While experimenting locally with SMB/network location support (not yet submitted — still WIP), I noticed that once a GVfs network mount actually succeeds (e.g. via `gio::File::mount_enclosing_volume`/`mount_mountable` on an `smb://` location), it shows up automatically in the sidebar's "DEVICES" section through the existing mounted-volumes code, and it's presented very differently from how the rest of the app treats network locations.

## Where

`src/ui/window.rs`, both in `SidebarState::rebuild` (the `mounts` mapping around line 692) and in `append_volume` (around line 911):

```rust
let root = mount.root();
let location = root
    .path()
    .map(Location::local)
    .unwrap_or_else(|| Location::uri(root.uri()));
```

## Problem

For local/removable-device mounts, `root.path()` is the right thing to prefer. But for a GVfs network backend (smb, sftp, dav, ...), the automounter also exposes the mount through a FUSE bind path (`/run/user/$UID/gvfs/smb-share:server=...,share=...`), so `root.path()` succeeds too — just with that opaque FUSE path instead of `None`. The `unwrap_or_else` never gets a chance to prefer the clean `smb://host/share` URI in that case.

Concretely, once such a mount is registered:

- The sidebar entry's location, breadcrumb, and any further navigation happen through the `/run/user/1000/gvfs/smb-share:server=192.168.1.220,share=music`-style native path rather than `smb://192.168.1.220/music` — inconsistent with how the rest of the app models network locations as explicit URIs (see the "Native paths stay native" boundary in `docs/architecture.md`).
- Descending further from that FUSE-path breadcrumb misbehaved in my testing — one subfolder click surfaced "Unable to open directory: That location does not exist." I haven't dug into why; it may be specific to how that particular path was constructed, but the FUSE-path presentation itself seems like the wrong thing to be navigating through by design, regardless.

## Ask

Decide and document the intended convention for GVfs network mounts appearing in this sidebar list — I'd expect preferring the mount's URI (`root.uri()`) over its FUSE path whenever the mount isn't a plain local/removable device — before network location support (SMB/SFTP) lands, so the "mounted volumes" sidebar feature and network browsing agree on one presentation instead of drifting into two different (and differently-buggy) code paths.

I don't have a concrete fix in mind yet since I haven't decided the right way to distinguish "local device mount" from "GVfs network mount" at this call site — happy to discuss approaches.

## Problem

PR #30 prevents the new-entry field from appearing invalid when it is cleared programmatically, but it also suppresses empty-name feedback after a user explicitly submits or clears the field. Submission silently fails with no error style or `Enter a name` tooltip.

## Proposed fix

## Summary

Persist the selected sorting field and direction across application restarts. The saved sorting preference is shared by all three browser presentations: **List**, **Grid**, and **Explorer**.

## Investigation

List mode already retains sorting, but only in memory:

- `ViewPreferences` carries `sort_key` and `sort_direction` through `NavigationState`.
- Commit [`de2330c`](https://github.com/lgse/strata/commit/de2330ceea01308388e7e5f4a9f7d4aa608a28c9) made changed sorting preferences flow to newly opened columns and remain consistent when switching browser modes.
- All three mode controls ultimately update the same `Browser`/`NavigationState` sorting preferences.
- On every launch, `Browser::new` and `NavigationState::default` start from `ViewPreferences::default()` (`Name`, ascending).
- The persisted preferences in `src/ui/theme.rs` currently include browser mode and density, but no sorting field or direction.

So the earlier work covered navigation and mode switches during one run, not app restarts.

## Requirements

- Store the sorting field (`Name`, `Size`, `Modified`, or `Type`) and direction (`Ascending` or `Descending`) in the existing application preferences.
- Load them before the initial directory is populated so the first rendered results use the restored ordering without a visible default-order pass.
- Use one shared persisted sorting pair across List, Grid, and Explorer. A change made in any mode must be reflected after switching modes and after restarting in any mode.
- Keep backward compatibility with existing preference files. Missing or unrecognized values must safely fall back to `Name` ascending rather than preventing startup.
- Keep this issue scoped to sorting field and direction; persistence of “Folders first” and “Hidden files” is not included.
- Add tests for preference serialization/defaulting and applying restored sorting to initial navigation. Follow #15 for settings-write hardening rather than expanding this issue into a persistence-layer rewrite.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Select a non-default field and direction in List, restart Strata, and see the same ordering and control state in List, Grid, and Explorer.
- [ ] Repeat from Grid and Explorer; each mode updates the same durable preference.
- [ ] The initial directory load after restart is sorted with the restored values.
- [ ] All supported fields and both directions round-trip through the preferences file.
- [ ] Legacy, missing, and invalid sorting preference values fall back to `Name` ascending without startup failure.
- [ ] Automated tests cover serialization compatibility and restored initial sorting behavior.

Closes #38.

## Summary

- attempt VA-API acceleration across discovered render nodes;
- fall back to Vulkan across visible GPU devices;
- retain #37's bounded VP8/WebM software fallback;
- expose selected GPU devices and read-only `/sys` only to media previews;
- produce H.264/AAC MP4 from hardware paths and VP8/Opus WebM from software;
- validate bounded MP4/WebM signatures before passing output to GTK;
- document the sandbox tradeoff and required GStreamer packages.

The backend order is intentionally fixed as:

1. VA-API
2. Vulkan
3. software

Hardware failures and unsupported codecs advance to the next backend. The first successful command stops the sequence.

## Preserved limits

This builds on #37 and preserves:

- first 30 seconds;
- maximum 1280 pixels on either axis;
- maximum 30 fps;
- 30-second media wall limit;
- 1.25 GiB address-space limit;
- 32 MiB output limit;
- cancellation and namespace isolation.

Image, PDF, and thumbnail helpers retain their existing 12-second wall and 10-second CPU limits and receive no GPU or sysfs access.

## Benchmarks

Environment:

- CPU: AMD Ryzen 7 7800X3D
- GPUs: AMD Raphael iGPU and NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4080
- FFmpeg: n9.0.1
- Kernel: Linux 7.1.9-arch1-2
- release build through the actual bubblewrap path
- three-run median wall time

| Input | AMD VA-API | NVIDIA Vulkan | Forced software |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 960×400 | 1.784s | 1.000s | 4.239s |
| 2560×1440 | 3.282s | 2.050s | 5.540s |
| 3840×2160 | 4.833s | 3.456s | 10.000s |
| 1080×1920 H.264/60 | 4.252s | 2.584s | 4.486s |

The Vulkan route used a sandbox exposing only the NVIDIA-compatible nodes, so its measurement includes the expected failed NVIDIA VA-API attempt before Vulkan succeeds.

For the 1080×1920 H.264/60 fps reproducer, every route produced the full bounded preview:

- hardware: 720×1280 at 30 fps, H.264/AAC MP4;
- software: 720×1280 at 30 fps, VP8/Opus WebM.

All outputs passed FFprobe and GStreamer discovery.

## Validation

- `cargo fmt --all --check`
- `cargo check --all-targets --all-features`
- `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test --all-targets --all-features` — 158 passed
- 36 sandboxed benchmark runs across VA-API, Vulkan, and forced software
- GTK media playback verified locally

issues.body:
## Performance problem

Video previews currently normalize up to the first 30 seconds using a CPU-only FFmpeg/libvpx pipeline before playback. High-resolution videos can consume substantial CPU time and approach the 12-second wall timeout, especially on slower machines, even when hardware video acceleration is available.

Relevant code:

* `src/sandbox_helper.rs`
* `src/sandbox.rs`

## Proposed work

* Attempt VA-API acceleration first across available `/dev/dri/renderD*` devices.
* Fall back to Vulkan when VA-API is unavailable or unsupported.
* Retain the existing software VP8/WebM pipeline as the guaranteed fallback.
* Expose GPU devices and required read-only system information only for media preview operations.
* Produce a bounded GTK/GStreamer-compatible hardware output, expected to use H.264/MP4.
* Preserve the existing duration, output-size, memory, and wall-time limits.
* Document the additional sandbox permissions and GPU-driver exposure.

## Acceptance criteria

* Supported VA-API and Vulkan systems use hardware-accelerated video transcoding.
* Unsupported or failing hardware paths fall back automatically without breaking previews.
* Hardware output plays correctly through the existing GTK media preview.
* GPU device access is limited to media previews; image, PDF, and thumbnail operations remain unchanged.
* The 30-second duration, 32 MiB output, and 12-second wall-time limits remain enforced.
* Benchmarks show reduced wall time and CPU usage on representative HD and 4K videos.
* Tests cover backend ordering, sandbox scoping, and software fallback without requiring GPU hardware in CI.

## Summary

Extend the updater to present release notes before a user consents to an upgrade, and make release notes available later from Settings for both the installed release and an available newer release.

Move the existing update controls out of **General** into a dedicated **Updates** settings page so update status, actions, and release notes have enough space and a clear home.

## Current behavior

- The latest-release request keeps the version, release URL, and matching archive URL, but discards the GitHub release body.
- The upgrade dialog shows the target version and immediately offers **Download update** without explaining what changed.
- Settings contains update controls under **General → Updates**, but no way to revisit release notes.

## Proposed behavior

### Upgrade dialog

- Include the available release's notes in the confirmation state, before any download or installation begins.
- Clearly identify the installed and target versions.
- Keep the primary update action below the notes so the user can review the changes before consenting.
- Make long notes scroll without pushing the dialog actions off-screen or breaking compact layouts.
- Preserve the existing download, verification, installation, failure, and restart states after consent.

### Settings

- Add a first-class **Updates** page to the Settings navigation and move the automatic-check toggle, status, manual check, install, progress, and restart controls there.
- Provide release-note views for:
  - **Current release** — the exact release matching `CARGO_PKG_VERSION`.
  - **Available release** — the newer release found by the update check.
- When Strata is up to date, avoid presenting duplicate current/latest content; clearly indicate that the current release is the latest.
- Refresh the available-release notes when a manual or automatic update check produces a different result.

## Release metadata and rendering

- Extend release metadata handling to retain the GitHub release body and fetch the installed version's release by its exact tag when needed.
- Continue to ignore draft releases and follow the existing latest-release/prerelease policy.
- Render the subset of GitHub Markdown needed by generated release notes (at minimum headings, paragraphs, bulleted lists, emphasis/code, and links) in a readable, themed layout.
- Treat release content as untrusted: do not interpret raw HTML or execute/embed active content. Open links through the normal external URI handler and avoid automatic remote image loading.
- Keep network and parsing work off GTK's main thread.
- Show useful loading, empty-notes, offline/API-error, and unavailable-tag states. A notes-fetch failure must not be reported as “up to date” and should offer the canonical GitHub release page when known.
- A release-notes fetch failure should not make an otherwise eligible update impossible; show the failure explicitly and retain the release-page fallback so the user can review notes externally before choosing to continue.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Opening the update dialog for a newer release shows that release's notes before **Download update** can start.
- [ ] The dialog names both installed and target versions, remains usable with long notes, and keeps actions visible on compact window sizes.
- [ ] Settings has a dedicated **Updates** page containing all controls currently under **General → Updates**.
- [ ] Users can view notes for the installed release and, when one exists, the available newer release from Settings.
- [ ] An up-to-date installation clearly identifies the current release as latest without duplicate note panels.
- [ ] Manual and automatic checks update the displayed version, notes, sidebar notice, and install action consistently.
- [ ] Generated GitHub release notes render headings, lists, text formatting, and links readably; raw HTML/active or remote embedded content is not rendered.
- [ ] Loading, missing/empty notes, rate limiting, offline failures, and a missing current-version tag have distinct, non-blocking states with a GitHub fallback where possible.
- [ ] Existing update download, progress, verification, installation, and restart behavior remains intact.
- [ ] New controls and all visual states are keyboard accessible, expose accessible names, use semantic theme colors, and update live with theme changes.
- [ ] Tests cover release-body deserialization, exact-tag/current-version lookup, empty or malformed notes, safe Markdown handling, up-to-date versus available presentation, and failed notes requests.

Follow-up to #24 and the update-check work in #22.

author: spandan11106
body:
Fixes #54.

`--fsize=33554432` mirrored `MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES` in order to cap the output PNG, but `RLIMIT_FSIZE` is process-wide and also covers the memfd glycin sizes to `width * height * channels` while decoding. Since gdk-pixbuf routes decoding through glycin, any image over roughly 11 MP made the loader exceed the limit and get killed with SIGXFSZ, so previews and thumbnails failed for most phone photos and left a core dump behind.

This decouples the two caps:

- `FILE_SIZE_LIMIT_BYTES` is now 512 MiB, comfortably above a full-resolution frame while staying under `ADDRESS_SPACE_LIMIT_BYTES`, which remains the real memory guard.
- `MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES` is unchanged and still bounds the output host-side after the run, which is where that check belongs.

## Testing

- `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --all-targets --all-features`.
- Verified against the underlying loader directly: with the old limit, `prlimit --as=2147483648 --cpu=10 --fsize=33554432 -- glycin-thumbnailer -i file://<12MP.jpg> -o out.png -s 256` kills the loader, and raising only `--fsize` lets the same command succeed.

Note that CI runs on `ubuntu-24.04`, whose gdk-pixbuf 2.42.10 predates the glycin loader and decodes in-process, so it cannot exercise this path. The added unit test pins the invariant that the limit must clear a full-resolution decoded frame, to stop the value being tightened back into the same failure.

issues.body:
Previews and thumbnails fail with "The sandboxed preview renderer failed" for any image above roughly 11 megapixels, which covers most phone photos. Each attempt also leaves a core dump behind.

## Cause

`src/sandbox.rs:235` passes `--fsize=33554432` (32 MiB) to `prlimit`, mirroring `MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES`. The intent is to cap the output PNG, but `RLIMIT_FSIZE` is process-wide and applies to every file any descendant writes.

Since gdk-pixbuf 2.43.2, `Pixbuf::from_file_at_scale` (`render_pixbuf` in `src/sandbox_helper.rs`) routes decoding through glycin, which spawns `glycin-image-rs` and `ftruncate`s a memfd to `width * height * channels` to hold the full-resolution frame before scaling. For a 3024x4032 JPEG that is 36,578,304 bytes, over the 32 MiB cap, so the kernel kills the loader with SIGXFSZ.

The requested thumbnail size does not help, since the full frame is materialised first. The threshold is `W * H * 3 > 32 MiB`, about 11.2 MP, or about 8.4 MP when an RGBA format is selected.

## Reproduction

```
prlimit --as=1342177280 --cpu=10 --fsize=33554432 -- \
  glycin-thumbnailer -i file:///path/to/12MP.jpg -o out.png -s 256
# Glycin Thumbnailer: Remote error: org.freedesktop.zbus.Error: i/o error
```

Raising only `--fsize` to 512 MiB makes the same command succeed, so `--as` and `--cpu` are not involved. `coredumpctl` shows `glycin-image-rs` terminated with signal 25 (XFSZ), crashing in `SharedMemory::new` -> `nix::unistd::ftruncate`.

## Affected systems

Any distribution whose gdk-pixbuf is built against glycin: Arch (2.44.7), Fedora (2.44.5), Debian trixie/sid, Ubuntu 25.04+. It does not reproduce on gdk-pixbuf 2.42.x, which decodes in-process. That includes `ubuntu-24.04`, which CI runs on, so CI cannot catch this today. `src/sandbox/tests.rs:32` asserts the current value, which locks it in.

## Suggested fix

Decouple the two caps. `--as=1342177280` is already the memory guard, and `MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES` is enforced host-side after the run, so `--fsize` can be raised well above any plausible decoded frame.

issues.body:
## Bug

When `gvfsd` is hung/unresponsive, Strata hangs indefinitely during startup with no window appearing and no error message. The process stays alive but never shows a UI.

## Reproduction

1. Kill or hang `gvfsd`: `killall gvfsd`
2. Launch strata
3. Observe: process starts, `activate` is called, `window.present()` is reached, but the window never appears on screen
4. stderr shows repeated `(strata:PID): GVFS-WARNING **: Error: Timeout was reached` every ~25 seconds
5. The app never recovers — it waits forever on GIO calls

## Expected behavior

Strata should either:

1. **Fall back to direct `std::fs` access for local paths** when GVFS is unresponsive (local files don't need a virtual filesystem daemon), or
2. **Timeout after 2-3 seconds** and show an error state ("Filesystem daemon unresponsive") with a retry option, or
3. **At minimum**, show a loading/error window instead of silently hanging with no UI

## Actual behavior

The app hangs silently. No window, no error, no timeout. A non-technical user would assume the app is broken and force-quit it.

## Environment

- Arch Linux / Omarchy / Hyprland (Wayland)
- GTK 4.22.4
- gvfs 1.60.2-1
- Rust 1.98.0
- Strata 0.4.0 (built from `main`, commit 035d6d6)

## Workaround

Restarting `gvfsd` before launching strata fixes the issue:
```bash
killall gvfsd && /usr/lib/gvfsd &
```

But this is not something a non-technical user would know to do.

## Root cause

Strata uses GIO/GVFS for file operations. When `gvfsd` is unresponsive, every GIO call blocks indefinitely with no timeout. This affects window creation because the initial directory load happens during `BrowserView::new()`, which blocks the GTK main loop.

Local file access via `std::fs` would not have this dependency — GVFS is only needed for virtual locations (trash://, network mounts, etc.), not for browsing local directories.

## Summary

Closes #9.

- Limit thumbnail rendering to one worker with at most 64 queued unique requests.
- Deduplicate identical requests and retry live requests deferred by queue saturation.
- Generate search thumbnails only for rows intersecting the viewport.
- Cancel work when rows leave the viewport, are rebound, replaced, or hidden.
- Cache failed renders for 30 seconds to prevent retry loops.
- Limit raster and PDF inputs to 512 MiB and validate decoded PNG dimensions.
- Bound provider output, discard stderr, and enforce sandbox runtime and memory limits.
- Terminate renderer process groups and descendants on cancellation or timeout.

## Testing

issues.body:
## Security/availability problem

Thumbnail jobs currently have no global concurrency limit or timeout. External providers use `Command::output()`, which buffers stdout without a bound.

Relevant code: `src/ui/thumbnail.rs:202-289`.

A malicious file or directory containing many expensive files can consume excessive processes, threads, memory, or CPU. The final thumbnail cache limit does not constrain in-flight decoder memory or subprocess output.

## Proposed work

- Add a small bounded thumbnail worker queue.
- Cancel jobs for rows that are no longer visible/current.
- Enforce per-job wall-clock timeouts and terminate timed-out process groups.
- Stream and cap stdout/stderr rather than using unbounded `Command::output()`.
- Apply input file-size and decoded-dimension/pixel limits where possible.
- Cache failed/unsupported results for a bounded period to prevent retry loops.
- Coordinate these controls with the preview sandbox work.

## Acceptance criteria

- At most a configured small number of thumbnail jobs run concurrently.
- Provider output, stderr, runtime, and decoded image dimensions are bounded.
- A directory full of malformed/slow files leaves the UI responsive.
- Tests cover oversized output, timeout, cancellation, and queue saturation.

## Summary

This extends the existing file-list keyboard controls into a complete focus flow for column headers, nested folders, the sidebar, menus, and delete confirmation. Existing item-level `h/j/k/l` and arrow behavior remains unchanged.

## New navigation behavior

### Nested columns

- `Enter`, `l`, or Right on a folder opens its child column and selects the first item, allowing another press to continue immediately.
- Activating a folder whose child column is already open moves focus into that column instead of doing nothing.
- Backspace closes the focused nested column and its descendants. From the root column, it navigates to the filesystem parent.
- Returning to a parent or already-open child column restores that column's selection.

### Column headers

- `k` or Up from the first visible file moves focus into the column-header controls.
- `h/l` and Left/Right move between the sort-direction, sort-menu, filter, and close controls.
- `j` or Down returns focus to the selected file.
- `h` or Left from the first header control continues outward to the parent column or sidebar.
- Enter and Space activate the focused header control instead of activating the previously selected file.

### Sidebar

- `h` or Left from the first file column focuses the active sidebar row.
- `l` or Right returns from the sidebar to the active file column.
- Sidebar rows now receive native Up/Down and Enter handling instead of those keys affecting the file list.
- `j/k` mirror native Down/Up navigation within the sidebar.
- `Ctrl+Shift+B` moves focus to the sidebar and restores the exact previous control when pressed again.

### Filters, sorting, and deletion

- Backspace closes an empty focused filter while preserving normal text deletion when the filter contains text.
- The Sort By dropdown supports `h/j/k/l`, and Backspace closes it.
- Delete confirmation supports `h`/Left for Cancel and `l`/Right for Confirm.
- The initially selected delete action now receives a reliable visible focus ring.

## Focus presentation

- The active column header receives a complete accent border.
- Keyboard focus rings are shown consistently on header controls.
- Background directory batches, sorting, and filesystem refreshes no longer steal focus from controls.

## Testing

- `./scripts/check.sh` — 207 tests passed
- `git diff --check`
- Manually validated nested-column, header, sidebar, filter, sorting, and delete-dialog keyboard flows
- Manually validated focus visibility and persistence during directory loading and refreshes

body:
## Description

Search indexing and trash summarization each walked (and, for search, retained) an entire tree with no bound, so an adversarial or unexpectedly large tree could cause excessive memory use, I/O, or long-running work.

- Add entry, depth, and wall-clock time budgets to search indexing (`src/services/search.rs`), and surface a `truncated` flag through to the search UI (a footer hint) when a budget is hit.
- Add the same budget shape to trash summarization (`src/ui/browser.rs`), surfaced via the empty-trash confirmation dialog and the trash-root properties size ("At least N items" / "≥ size").
- Make the confirmation-dialog measurement fully decoupled from deletion: `summarize_trash` never retains an entry list and stays strictly bounded regardless of trash size, while "Empty Trash" does its own fresh, unbounded, non-recursive top-level listing at the moment it's clicked, so it always empties everything and can't go stale.
- Make trash measurement cancellable end-to-end: a `LoadHandle` (aborts a superseded request) plus a "Measuring Trash…" indicator with Cancel/Escape while the walk runs.
- Degrade gracefully instead of failing outright when a trash subdirectory becomes unreadable or disappears mid-walk: treat it as a truncated branch rather than aborting the whole measurement.
- Add `tracing` instrumentation for truncation, completion, and cancellation, matching the existing convention in `adapters/local_files.rs`.

Deliberately left out: a disk-backed/incremental index for search, which the issue marks as "consider" rather than required, and which is a large enough change to warrant its own discussion first.

## Visual evidence

N/A for the primary logic (bounding/cancellation of background work has no visual surface). Two small UI additions exist — a "Measuring Trash…" loading indicator with Cancel, and a search-results footer hint shown only once the entry/time budget is hit on an adversarially large tree — but I don't have a way to drive this native GTK app's mouse input to capture that specific dialog (no click-simulation tooling available in my environment). I did manually verify the surrounding trash browsing flow end-to-end: navigated to `trash:///`, populated it with real files, confirmed they render correctly, then emptied it.

## How to test

1. `./scripts/generate-fixture.sh target/fixtures` to build a large synthetic tree, then open Strata's search on `target/fixtures` and type a query. Search remains responsive; on an even larger tree (or with the budget constants temporarily lowered) a "search limited" hint appears in the footer.
2. Move a large number of files/folders to Trash, then use the sidebar's Trash entry or the "Empty Trash" action. The confirmation dialog appears after a bounded measurement (never longer than ~5s), shows "At least N items" if truncated, and "Empty Trash" always deletes everything regardless of how large the trash is.

**Expected result:** search and trash summarization stay responsive and bounded on very large or adversarial trees, trash deletion is always complete, and none of this blocks the UI or the confirmation dialog from appearing.

## Related issue

Closes #13

## Availability problem

Search indexing retains an entry for the complete tree, and trash summarization recursively walks all entries. Adversarial or unexpectedly large trees can cause excessive memory usage, I/O, and long-running work.

Relevant code:
- `src/services/search.rs`
- `src/ui/browser.rs:4108-4175`

## Proposed work

- Establish explicit entry, memory, depth, and runtime budgets.
- Keep search result storage bounded and consider a disk-backed/incremental index for large trees.
- Make indexing and trash measurement cancellable end-to-end.
- Detect cycles/backend anomalies and cap recursive depth.
- Surface partial/estimated results rather than blocking indefinitely.

## Acceptance criteria

- Search and trash measurement remain responsive on very large synthetic trees.
- Memory use has a documented bound or graceful degradation behavior.
- Cancellation promptly stops traversal.
- Tests cover deep, broad, inaccessible, and changing trees.

issues.body:
## Data-integrity problem

Cancelling a delete, restore, copy, or move cannot undo items that already completed, and recursive work may stop midway. The current task-abort model can make cancellation appear cleaner or more transactional than it is.

Relevant code:
- `src/app/browser.rs:710-725`
- `src/adapters/local_operations.rs:264-309`

## Proposed work

- Use explicit cancellables and define cancellation semantics for every operation type.
- Track and report completed, failed, and not-attempted items.
- Refresh every affected source and destination after cancellation.
- For recursive copy, remove only known-incomplete staging output; never remove pre-existing data.
- Make the progress UI state that cancellation may leave completed changes in place.
- Return a distinct cancelled/partially-completed event instead of silently dropping callbacks.

## Acceptance criteria

- Cancellation produces a final result describing partial completion.
- The UI does not claim that already completed destructive changes were reverted.
- Source/destination views converge to actual filesystem state.
- Tests cancel between items and during recursive copy/delete/restore.

comments.author: l0gicgate
comments.body:
## Implementation and manual verification update

PR #75 is up to date with `main` and now includes the cancellation-accounting fix plus the performance and reconciliation fixes found during staged manual testing.

### Testing methodology

We tested one operation at a time using large, uniquely named fixture sets so the on-disk state could be compared directly with Strata's reported totals. For each scenario we:

1. created or staged a known set of files/directories;
2. started the operation from Strata and cancelled it after measurable progress;
3. compared **completed**, **failed**, and **not attempted** counts in the result UI;
4. verified the source and destination contents on disk;
5. checked that affected panes refreshed to the same state;
6. checked responsiveness while progress, cancellation, context menus, and reconciliation were active;
7. checked for leaked Strata-owned staging artifacts (`.strata-*`).

The restore case used 3,000 uniquely named Trash entries and a dedicated restore destination. We also restarted the debug build between iterations and repeated scenarios after each performance/UI change rather than relying only on automated tests.

### Scenarios exercised

- recursive copy cancellation;
- same-filesystem bulk move cancellation;
- permanent recursive-delete cancellation;
- large Trash restore cancellation;
- large selection/context-menu behavior during these workflows;
- post-cancellation model and filesystem reconciliation.

### Confirmed behavior and fixes

- Cancellation now reports partial results accurately: completed work remains completed, failures remain failures, and untouched items are reported as not attempted.
- Completion wins a cancellation race when GIO has already completed the item.
- Recursive copy/replacement uses Strata-owned staging and cancellation removes only the incomplete staging output, preserving existing destinations.
- Completed move sources are removed from the cut clipboard while uncompleted sources remain available.
- Affected local/remote roots and open descendants are refreshed after partial operations.
- Copy cancellation left the expected partial destination state and no `.strata-*` artifacts.
- Same-filesystem move cancellation remained responsive and reconciled to the reported result.
- Permanent recursive-delete cancellation preserved the unfinished root and matched the reported partial state.
- Large restore cancellation matched the reported completed/not-attempted split at both the Trash and restore destination.
- Large operation progress no longer performs expensive per-item GTK model reconciliation.
- Bulk transfer checks, selection synchronization, cut styling, and context-menu summaries were changed from quadratic behavior to linear/set-based lookups.
- Large filesystem-monitor bursts now collapse into one rescan instead of starving the UI with thousands of notifications.
- Context menus remain responsive for large selections, and summaries are width-bounded with a 60-character truncation limit.
- Cancellation statistics are shown before the slower Trash reconciliation begins; refresh starts after the result dialog closes.
- Column, grid, and explorer reloads now retain a loading skeleton until `LoadFinished`, avoiding the previous several-second blank pane.
- Filtered/selection views are detached while backing models reload and reconnected once at completion, avoiding repeated filtered-view recalculation.
- Skeleton padding was aligned more closely with loaded rows to reduce the visible layout shift.

### Additional defects discovered

These are separate from cancellation accounting and were filed independently:

- #149 — expand `~/...` paths entered in the address bar.
- #150 — support moving directories across filesystems (currently fails with `Can’t recursively copy directory`).

### Remaining visual limitation

In the largest filtered Trash reconciliation case, the loading skeleton is visible but the small header spinner can still appear stationary. The results and final filesystem/model state remain correct, and the previously blank loading period is now represented by the skeleton. Given that this is an edge-case visual limitation rather than a correctness failure, we are not blocking the cancellation fix on it.

### Automated verification

Latest branch verification:

- `cargo fmt`
- `cargo test` — **282 passed**
- `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `git diff --check`

Branch head: `a84b006` (`perf(ui): reconnect filtered views after reload`).

issues.body:
## Summary

Pressing `Delete` on a selected **file** correctly moves it to Trash. Pressing `Delete` on a selected **folder** does nothing: no filesystem change, no Trash entry, no error dialog, and no log output at any level — a silent no-op.

## Environment

- Strata `v0.5.0`, installed from the official release archive (`strata-0.5.0-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz`), `SOURCE_COMMIT` `c57ec3e1ae44aa4ffeb171f66cfaaa99d2c9253f`
- Arch-based (CachyOS), glibc 2.44
- GTK 4.22.4, GLib 2.88.3
- Wayland, `niri` compositor
- Test location: a folder on the real home filesystem (`btrfs`, confirmed via `findmnt`) that fully supports XDG Trash — ruling out the "this location doesn't support Trash" case entirely.

## Repro steps

1. In a directory on a Trash-capable filesystem, create an empty subfolder and a plain file alongside it.
2. Select the file, press `Delete`. Confirm it lands in `~/.local/share/Trash/files/`.
3. Select the folder, press `Delete`.
4. Observe: nothing happens. The folder remains on disk, untouched, with no entry created in `~/.local/share/Trash/`.

## Evidence / ruled-out causes

Reproduced directly, in the same running Strata session, with the file case succeeding immediately beforehand:

- **Not a Trash-unsupported-filesystem issue**: confirmed via `findmnt` that the test directory is on `btrfs`, and the file delete in the same session produced a real Trash entry.
- **Not a focus issue**: the file delete succeeded in the same window immediately before/after the folder attempt.
- **Not a permission or "not empty" error**: no dialog appeared at all (contrast with a genuinely Trash-unsupported location, e.g. tmpfs, which does surface a "This location doesn't support Trash" dialog — so Strata's error-reporting path does work when it has something to report).
- Ran Strata with `RUST_LOG=debug` for the whole session: no trash/delete-related log line appears anywhere around the folder deletion attempt, despite the log being otherwise verbose (directory loads, selection changes, preview pipeline, etc. are all logged).
- `docs/todo.md` lists "Trash and permanently delete selected files" and "Bind `Delete` and `Shift+Delete` to confirmed trash and permanent-delete actions" as done, with no file/folder distinction, and the underlying GVfs trash mechanism (`g_file_trash`) supports directories natively — so this doesn't look like an intentional scope limitation.

## Expected behavior

Pressing `Delete` on a selected folder should trash it (with the same confirmation behavior as a file), matching the behavior already implemented for files.

## Description

Let `GtkListView` exclusively handle double-click activation in Miller columns. The row gesture now handles only selection and single-click previews, preventing the gesture and the list's `activate` signal from both opening the same file.

Adds regression coverage ensuring the preview gesture ignores double-clicks and modified/group-preserving clicks.

## Visual evidence

N/A — this changes launch behavior without changing the interface.

## How to test

1. Set a non-single-instance application such as Gwenview as the default image handler.
2. Double-click an image in Strata's Miller columns, then select it and press Enter.

**Expected result:** Each action opens exactly one application window.

## Related issue

issues.body:
## Summary

Double-clicking a file in the browser view (Miller columns / Grid / Explorer) launches the default application **twice**, producing two separate windows/processes. Pressing **Enter** on the same file opens it correctly as a single instance. A full restart of Strata (and re-login) does not resolve it.

For apps with a client/daemon single-instance architecture (e.g. Zed), the duplicate launch is silently masked — the second client process hands off to the existing daemon and exits. For apps without that (e.g. Gwenview), two full windows open.

## Environment

- Strata `v0.5.0`, installed from the official release archive (`strata-0.5.0-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz`), `SOURCE_COMMIT` `c57ec3e1ae44aa4ffeb171f66cfaaa99d2c9253f`
- Arch-based (CachyOS), glibc 2.44
- GTK 4.22.4, GLib 2.88.3
- Wayland, `niri` compositor
- Default app for the tested image type: `org.kde.gwenview.desktop` (Gwenview 26.08.0), set via a correct `~/.config/mimeapps.list`

## Repro steps

1. Set a non-daemonized app (e.g. Gwenview) as the default handler for an image MIME type.
2. In Strata, double-click an image file.
3. Observe two Gwenview windows/processes open for the same file.
4. Press Enter on a file instead — only one instance opens, as expected.

## Evidence

Traced the running Strata process with `strace -f -tt -e trace=execve,clone,fork,vfork` while double-clicking an image. The **same Strata PID (40435)** issues two separate `clone()` calls ~5ms apart, each independently launching the default app on the identical file:

```
40435 21:04:14.600486 clone(...) = 41457
41457 21:04:14.602105 clone(...) = 41458
41458 21:04:14.603538 execve("/usr/lib/gio-launch-desktop", ["/usr/lib/gio-launch-desktop", "/usr/bin/gwenview", "/home/<user>/example.png"], ...)
41458 21:04:14.605261 execve("/usr/bin/gwenview", ["/usr/bin/gwenview", "/home/<user>/example.png"], ...)

40435 21:04:14.605354 clone(...) = 41460
41460 21:04:14.606464 clone(...) = 41461
41461 21:04:14.607675 execve("/usr/lib/gio-launch-desktop", ["/usr/lib/gio-launch-desktop", "/usr/bin/gwenview", "/home/<user>/example.png"], ...)
41461 21:04:14.609266 execve("/usr/bin/gwenview", ["/usr/bin/gwenview", "/home/<user>/example.png"], ...)
```

Both process chains fork from the same Strata PID for a single double-click on a single file. This points to the double-click handler invoking the "open with default app" action twice (e.g. a click-gesture handler and a row/item-activate signal both firing an open call), rather than anything in GIO, Gwenview, or the system's MIME configuration:

- Confirmed a single `g_app_info_launch_default_for_uri()` call reliably spawns exactly one process (tested directly via PyGObject).
- Confirmed the system's double-click timing threshold is a standard 400ms, not misconfigured.
- Confirmed `~/.config/mimeapps.list` correctly resolves the file's content type to Gwenview.
- Confirmed the bug persists after a full application restart and user re-login.

## Expected behavior

Double-clicking a file should invoke the default-application launch exactly once, matching the behavior of the Enter key.

author: l0gicgate
body: ## Description Adds a curated catalog of 88 Tinted Theming palettes plus the contributed 0x96f theme, bringing Strata to 95 alphabetically ordered bundled themes. The Theme & appearance page now provides search, All/Light/Dark filtering, and a bounded scrolling gallery so the larger offline catalog remains easy to browse. The catalog records its upstream revision, semantic Base16 mapping, and MIT attribution. Settings is also treated as a modal layer so text-editing shortcuts do not trigger Miller column actions behind the dialog. ## Visual evidence ## How to test 1. Open **Settings → Theme & appearance** and browse the scrolling theme gallery. 2. Search for themes by name, clear the query with the X button, and switch between **All**, **Light**, and **Dark**. 3. Select several themes, including **0x96f**, and confirm each applies immediately. 4. Focus the search field and press Ctrl+A. **Expected result:** Bundled themes appear alphabetically, search and appearance filters combine correctly, selecting a card applies it, and Ctrl+A selects the query without changing the background file selection. ## Related issue Closes #82

issues.body:
### Problem or use case

Strata currently ships a small set of built-in themes and supports custom themes through its nine-token TOML format. There are hundreds or thousands of established color schemes in projects such as Tinted Theming, but adding each theme manually does not scale and makes it difficult for users to reuse a theme they already use elsewhere.

Bundling many palettes is technically plausible: the seven current TOML files contain about 1.4 KB of theme data, so roughly 100 similarly sized themes would be around 20 KB and 1,001 would be around 200 KB before packaging overhead. The harder questions are discovery in Settings, palette conversion quality, ongoing maintenance, provenance, and license attribution.

### Proposed solution

Investigate a scalable way to offer a broad theme catalog without committing to a specific implementation yet. A useful first milestone could support around 100 well-known themes while establishing an approach that can grow further.

Possible solutions:

1. **Curated built-in catalog**
   - Generate Strata theme files from a reviewed list of popular schemes at build or release time.
   - Keep themes available offline with no additional user setup.
   - Add search, filtering, and possibly light/dark or family grouping to Settings so a large catalog remains usable.
   - Record each source, upstream revision, and license; review generated semantic mappings before release.

2. **Import a standardized palette format**
   - Add an importer for Base16/Base24 (Tinted Theming) YAML, mapping source colors into Strata's nine semantic tokens.
   - Preview the mapped result before saving it under **Your themes**.
   - This provides access to a large existing ecosystem without permanently bundling every palette.
   - Start with a declarative format rather than Vim colorschemes, which may contain executable Vimscript/Lua, editor-specific highlight groups, and no unambiguous mapping to Strata's UI roles.

3. **Import common terminal/editor theme files**
   - Support a small set of declarative formats with predictable colors, such as Alacritty, Kitty, or another widely used palette schema.
   - Require an explicit preview and allow users to adjust the generated tokens because these formats often lack equivalents for surface, muted, border, danger, and dim text.
   - Avoid executing editor configuration or theme code.

4. **Optional downloadable catalog**
   - Keep a small core set built in and provide an installable catalog in Settings.
   - This reduces the default list and allows catalog updates independently, but introduces networking, caching, integrity/versioning, offline behavior, and trust requirements.

A phased approach may be best: first add searchable curated built-ins and a Base16/Base24 file importer, then evaluate whether a remote catalog or more source formats are justified by demand.

### Alternatives considered

- Continue accepting one built-in theme per pull request. This is simple but creates repetitive review work and inconsistent provenance/mapping quality.
- Ask users to manually translate every palette into Strata TOML. This already works but is inconvenient and makes sharing/discovery poor.
- Import Vim themes directly. This has broad reach, but Vim themes are not a single declarative palette format and can include code, making conversion unreliable and execution unsafe.
- Bundle all known themes immediately. Storage is unlikely to be the limiting factor, but the Settings UI, licensing, duplicate variants, quality control, and update policy need a design first.

### Visual examples

N/A — this issue is for design and feasibility exploration. Any implementation that exposes a large catalog should include mockups for theme search/filtering and import preview before development.

### Strata version

0.5.0

### Additional context

- Existing Strata themes use nine semantic tokens: `background`, `surface`, `text`, `accent`, `danger`, `muted`, `highlight`, `border`, and `dim_text`.
- Tinted Theming schemes are a promising declarative source: https://github.com/tinted-theming/schemes
- Decisions needed before implementation:
  - Which source formats and licenses are acceptable?
  - Should generated themes be bundled, imported locally, or downloaded on demand?
  - How are incomplete source palettes mapped and reviewed for contrast/accessibility?
  - How should variants, duplicates, attribution, upstream revisions, and updates be tracked?
  - At what catalog size do search, tags, favorites, or pagination become necessary?
issues.title: Support a scalable theme catalog and theme imports

author: spandan11106
body:
Closes #61.

Adds an opt-in preview release channel to the updater, an RC publication mode to the release workflow, and a "Return to stable" path back off a prerelease.

## Root fix

`parse_version` read three `u64` segments and zero-filled anything unparseable, so `0.5.0-rc.1` parsed as `(0, 5, 0)` — indistinguishable from final `0.5.0`. It is replaced by a `Version` type implementing real semver §11 precedence, where `Version::parse` returns `Option` and is the single place any tag is interpreted anywhere in the codebase.

## Architecture

A new pure module `src/services/release_channel.rs` owns every channel, version, eligibility, and ordering decision — no I/O, no serde, no GitHub types. `update_check.rs` is now GitHub transport only and delegates all judgement to it. That boundary is what makes the "a Stable user never sees a prerelease" guarantee provable in unit tests with no network access.

## Channel isolation

Stable and preview use separate fetch paths, so a Stable user's process never enumerates prereleases at all. Stable results are *additionally* filtered through `is_eligible`, which requires both that the parsed tag carries no prerelease and that GitHub's own `prerelease` flag is false — the defensive redundancy the issue asks for. Everything fails closed to Stable: unknown config values, a missing config key, unparseable build metadata.

## Prerelease identity

Travels via `STRATA_RELEASE_TAG` / `STRATA_BUILD_KIND`, injected by `build.rs` exactly as `STRATA_BUILD_COMMIT` already is. An RC run tags the source commit and never pushes a version bump to the default branch, so a prerelease cannot poison the stable version line. `--prerelease` on the GitHub release keeps `/releases/latest` pointing at the last final release, which is the endpoint Stable users poll.

## Design decisions made where the issue left them open

- **RC outranks nightly** at equal core version, matching semver's alphanumeric ordering of prerelease identifiers (`"nightly"` sorts before `"rc"`). Once an RC is cut, that line has stabilized; pulling a preview user onto a same-core nightly would be a stability regression.
- **Preview = stable ∪ prereleases**, newest by semver precedence, so a user on `0.5.0-rc.2` is offered final `0.5.0` as an ordinary update instead of being stranded on a stale RC. "Return to stable" remains the separate explicit channel switch, and is gated on the *running build* being a prerelease rather than on the selected channel — otherwise a user who already switched their preference back to Stable would be stranded on an RC with no exit.

## Scoped out

The issue's "both executables" wording came from #59, which is deferred — this repo ships one binary (`src/main.rs` dispatches `--preview-helper` as `argv[1]`). The installer takes a *list* of binaries to place, so #59 becomes a small change rather than a rewrite if it lands.

## Partially met

The **"workflow tests"** acceptance criterion. There is no workflow test harness in this repo. The version-calculation logic is extracted to `scripts/release_version.py` with 18 tests wired into CI as a `release-scripts` job, but the workflow wiring itself is only verifiable by a manual `rc` dry run. Flagging rather than papering over.

## Verification

`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets`, `cargo test` (235 passed, up from a 176 baseline), and `python3 scripts/test_release_version.py` (18 passed) are all clean.

The GTK wiring for the channel selector and rollback row is not unit-testable and has not been visually confirmed — worth an eyeball before merge.

## Known follow-ups

Non-blocking, found in review and left deliberately:

- A hard-killed install now leaks a uniquely-named staging directory with no sweep (previously the pid-named directory was reused).
- The install-in-progress guard is per-window rather than per-process; with unique staging paths the worst case is two complete verified binaries installed in sequence, not corruption.
- A channel toggle during an install causes cosmetic status churn in the update row; the guard holds and no second install starts.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

issues.body:
## Problem

The updater currently follows the stable GitHub release only. We need a safe opt-in path for users who want preview builds, while ensuring stable users never see release candidates or nightly update prompts. Preview users must also have an obvious way back to the latest stable release.

## Goals

### 1. Publish RC builds from GitHub Actions

- Extend the release workflow with an RC release mode.
- Produce semver prerelease tags such as `v0.5.0-rc.1`.
- Mark RC GitHub releases as **prerelease**, never as `latest`.
- Build and publish both supported architectures and both Strata executables.
- Publish checksums, provenance attestations, source commit metadata, and release notes using the same security controls as stable releases.
- Keep stable and prerelease version/tag generation deterministic and prevent accidental replacement of a stable release.

### 2. Add an opt-in preview/nightly update channel

In **Settings → Updates**, add a release-channel preference with clear language:

- **Stable** (default): final releases only.
- **Nightly / preview** (explicit opt-in): nightly builds and eligible RC prereleases.

The selected channel must persist. Opting in should immediately check the preview feed and clearly identify the offered build, channel, version/tag, source commit, and publication date before installation. Existing checksum and provenance expectations must continue to apply.

### 3. Support rollback to stable

While running a nightly or RC build, the Updates page must offer **Return to stable** even when the stable semantic version compares lower than the installed prerelease/nightly version.

Rollback must:

- fetch the latest final stable release explicitly;
- show the target version and confirmation before replacing binaries;
- install both `strata` and `strata-preview-helper`;
- switch the persisted channel back to Stable after a successful rollback;
- preserve user preferences and data;
- report download, verification, installation, and restart failures clearly.

## Channel isolation requirements

- Users on Stable must not receive, see, or be notified about RC/nightly releases.
- Stable checks must use a final-release-only source such as GitHub’s `/releases/latest` endpoint and defensively reject prerelease/draft metadata.
- Preview checks may enumerate prereleases, but must ignore drafts, unsupported artifacts, malformed tags, and releases for other channels.
- An RC/nightly must never update a stable user merely because its version sorts newer.
- Automatic checks and the sidebar update notice must respect the selected channel.
- Release notes and update dialogs must visibly label prerelease software.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A maintainer can publish an RC through a protected GitHub Actions workflow without changing the stable `latest` release.
- [ ] Stable remains the default for new and existing installations.
- [ ] Stable users cannot see RC/nightly builds anywhere in the update UI.
- [ ] A user can explicitly opt into the preview/nightly channel and install an eligible build.
- [ ] A preview user can update between eligible preview builds.
- [ ] A preview/RC installation can downgrade to the latest stable build.
- [ ] Channel choice survives restart and automatic checks obey it.
- [ ] Both executables, checksums, and provenance are handled for upgrade and rollback.
- [ ] Unit tests cover channel filtering, prerelease ordering, stable isolation, persisted preferences, downgrade selection, malformed metadata, and unsupported assets.
- [ ] Workflow tests/documentation cover stable, RC, and nightly publication behavior.

## Design note

Define the relationship between “nightly” and “RC” explicitly during implementation. The proposed UI uses one opt-in preview channel that may consume both, but metadata should retain their distinct labels so a user always knows what they are installing.

comments.author: spandan11106
comments.body:
The issue asks for "both supported architectures and both Strata executables", and rollback must "install both strata and strata-preview-helper". As far as I can tell the repo ships a single executable today — src/main.rs dispatches on --preview-helper as argv[1] into sandbox_helper::run, and Cargo.toml has no [[bin]] targets, so release.yml packages exactly one file (dist/$package/strata).

Which did you have in mind?

1. The single binary already satisfies it — replacing strata replaces the preview helper too, since they're the same file. Upgrade and rollback stay single-file atomic renames, and I'd just document that when checking the criterion off.
2. Split out a real second binary — add a [[bin]] strata-preview-helper target, package and checksum both, and make upgrade/rollback replace two files transactionally (staging both, undoing the first rename if the second fails). That's a meaningfully larger change and touches the sandbox spawn path, so I'd want it confirmed as in scope before building it.

Happy either way — just don't want to guess on the packaging contract.

comments.author: l0gicgate
comments.body:
@spandan11106 I created this ticket while I was not on main (a different perf PR that proposes shipping 2 executables) I'm not sure if I want to follow through with this as it makes things more ergonomically difficult to ship stuff.

See #59 for context. I still have to give it more thought. let me know what you think.

comments.author: spandan11106
comments.body:
I'd suggest not coupling them. Most of #61 does not care how many binaries ship. I can build it against single-binary main now and have the installer take a list of binaries instead of a hardcoded name; then if #59 lands it's a one-line change plus packaging.

On #59: the thing I'd weigh isn't packaging friction but version skew. Right now sandbox.rs:98 spawns current_exe --preview-helper, so main and helper are identical by construction. Split them and a partially-applied update leaves a new strata talking to an old helper across the sandbox boundary. Fixable (versioned dir + symlink flip, version handshake on spawn), just worth deciding deliberately.

Also, #59 bundles the split and the deferred settings construction. Only the split costs you anything in packaging. Might be worth measuring them separately.

Happy to start #61 on the single-binary assumption unless you'd rather hold.

comments.author: l0gicgate
comments.body:
@spandan11106 agreed, you can start #61. I was going to ship #59 with the next release but need to give it more thought.

Assigned the task to you! Thank you for taking this on.

## Description

Reduce CI runner startups to three repository-managed jobs while preserving the security boundary between trusted PR metadata and untrusted repository content. Title and Claude-attribution validation now share a trusted metadata job; dependency and spelling checks share a repository policy job; format, lint, and tests remain together.

The metadata job reads commit information through GitHub's API and never checks out or executes pull request code.

## Visual evidence

N/A — this changes repository policy only.

## How to test

1. Open a test PR with an invalid title or a commit containing `Co-authored-by: Claude Sonnet <noreply@anthropic.com>` and observe the metadata policy fail.
2. Correct the title and rewrite the commit without the attribution metadata.
3. Confirm that CI presents one metadata policy job, one dependency and spelling policy job, and one format, lint, and test job.

**Expected result:** Corrected PR metadata passes, prohibited attribution fails with the affected commit SHA, and repository checks use three runners.

## Related issue

Closes #103
Part of #101

issues.body:
### Problem or use case

Several quick pull request checks each start a dedicated runner. Runner startup takes as long as or longer than checks such as title validation and spelling, wasting CI capacity and adding avoidable overhead.

### Proposed solution

Consolidate the checks into three jobs while preserving the security boundary between trusted pull request metadata and untrusted repository content:

1. A trusted pull request policy job for title and commit-attribution validation.
2. A repository policy job for dependency and spelling checks.
3. The existing format, lint, and test job.

### Alternatives considered

Combining every check into one job would execute pull request content in the privileged `pull_request_target` context or make the metadata policy editable by the pull request. Keeping the trusted metadata job separate avoids that security risk. Keeping all checks separate provides more parallel feedback but incurs unnecessary runner startup overhead.

### Visual examples

N/A — CI-only change.

### Strata version

Current `main`

### Additional context

Cursor Bugbot and `[code]smith` are external integrations and cannot be consolidated into these GitHub Actions jobs.

### Strata version

0.6.0 (source build at commit `a6c872105a33a8857776e9fe44ca3cf55636f255`).

### Installation method

Built from source.

### Linux distribution and desktop environment

Arch Linux, Hyprland (Omarchy), Wayland.

### What happened?

Confirmation and prompt dialogs (delete, replace, empty trash, rename, connect-to-server, etc.) are rendered as custom modal layers with a blurred backdrop. Clicking on the backdrop outside the dialog does nothing — the dialog stays open. The only ways to dismiss are the Cancel/Close buttons or pressing Escape. This is inconsistent with the popover/menu behavior users expect, where an outside click dismisses the surface.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open Strata and select a file.
2. Press Delete to open the delete-confirmation dialog.
3. Click anywhere on the blurred backdrop outside the dialog.
4. Observe that the dialog remains open.

### Expected behavior

Clicking the backdrop (the area outside the dialog content) should dismiss the modal the same way the Cancel button does, without triggering the confirm action.

### Screenshots or video

N/A — interaction issue, not visible in a static screenshot.

### Relevant logs

N/A — no errors observed.

### Additional context

The modals are built by `modal_layer` in `src/ui/browser.rs`, which composes a fullscreen `gtk::Box` with `top`/`bottom` spacer boxes around the content. The spacers act as the backdrop but have no click gesture attached. There are ~20 call sites that wire Cancel/Close/Escape to `dismiss_modal_layer`; the backdrop click should reuse the same dismiss path.

author: JoeJoeflyn
body:
## Summary

### Modal animation rewrite (commit 1)

**What:** Removed the manual `allocate()`/`gsk::Transform` timer-based animation and replaced it with CSS class toggles (`animate_in`/`animate_out` add/remove a `modal-hidden` class that CSS transitions on opacity and transform). Added a `dismissing` guard to `dismiss_modal_layer`, search `hide`, and settings `hide`.

**Why:** The timer approach had three root causes of bugs:
1. `allocate()` from a 16ms timer overrides GTK's own layout allocation — the dialog jumped/startled and broke centering because GTK re-layouts and our timer re-allocates in conflict
2. `connect_map` handlers stacked up on persistent search/settings layers each time they were reopened, producing duplicate competing animations
3. No re-entry guard meant rapid outside clicks scheduled multiple fade-out callbacks before the first finished, leaving stale overlays stuck (the "double modal" bug)

CSS transitions run in GTK's render thread, don't conflict with layout, and handle timing internally. The `dismissing` class + `set_sensitive(false)` prevents any second dismissal from scheduling.

### Design polish (commit 2)

**What:** Added `transform: scale(0.97)` on `:active` and CSS transitions to 12 interactive elements (breadcrumb, location-action, dropdown, column-header-action, column-menu-option, preview-header-action, segmented-control-option, transfer-suggestion, properties-action, release-notes-fallback, theme-color-picker button, grid-thumbnail-menu button). Added transitions to switch, switch slider, and form-check. Replaced all dark `#000000` shadows on modals and popovers with one reused accent glow (`0 0 14px alpha(@theme_accent, 0.24)`). Unified border-radius to 9px and border to `alpha(@theme_border, 0.6)`. Added `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)`.

**Why:**
- Pressable elements without `:active` scale feel dead — no feedback that the UI heard the press (Apple: respond on pointer-down; Emil: buttons must feel responsive)
- State changes without transitions snap instantly instead of animating — feels broken (Emil: every state change needs a transition)
- Dark shadows on floating surfaces were inconsistent (some `#000000`, some `@theme_bg` which is invisible in light themes) and didn't match the accent-tinted design language; one reused accent glow provides identity and consistency with a single value
- Mixed border-radius (7px/9px) and border colors across surfaces looked unpolished
- Reduced-motion users get motion sickness from transforms; the media query keeps opacity cross-fades but removes movement (Apple: reduced motion means gentler, not zero)

Stacked on top of #107 — merge #107 first, then this one.

#### Manual verification

- [ ] Open/close confirmation dialogs repeatedly — no startle, no double modal
- [ ] Click outside dialog rapidly — dismisses once, no stuck overlay
- [ ] Open/close search repeatedly — smooth fade, no duplicate animation
- [ ] Open/close settings repeatedly — smooth fade, no duplicate animation
- [ ] Press any button — visible scale-down feedback on press
- [ ] Toggle switch — smooth background transition
- [ ] Open popovers (peek, column, appearance, context menu) — accent glow, no dark shadow
- [ ] Enable reduced motion in OS settings — modals cross-fade without scaling
title: fix(ui): modal animation and design polish

author: kallupx
body:
## Description

Validate every archive entry as a non-empty relative path before conflict resolution, with additional format-specific checks for ZIP and 7z archives. Extraction now creates directories and files relative to a single open destination descriptor, preventing path traversal and symlink redirection outside the selected folder.

Preserves nested extraction, password handling, progress reporting, and conflict suffixing for ZIP, TAR, TAR.GZ, and 7z archives. Adds regression coverage for traversal attempts, dangling and intermediate symlinks, normal nested extraction, and existing-name conflicts.

## Visual evidence

N/A - this is an archive extraction security fix without interface changes.

## How to test

1. Extract ZIP, TAR, TAR.GZ, and 7z archives containing nested files.
2. Extract an archive when a regular file or directory with the same name already exists.
3. Attempt to extract archives containing `../` or absolute entry paths.
4. Attempt extraction over a dangling symlink or through a symlinked directory.
5. Run `cargo test adapters::local_operations::tests` and `./scripts/check.sh`.

**Expected result:** Normal archives extract successfully, existing regular names receive numbered suffixes, and traversal or symlink-based extraction fails without writing outside the selected destination.

## Related issue

Closes #109

issues.body:
### Strata version

0.6.1 (source build at commit `e00117a79f1ab3d9ee2150a53b87a94300397d8c`).

### Installation method

Built from source.

### Linux distribution and desktop environment

Omarchy 4.0.2 (Arch Linux), Hyprland 0.56.2, Wayland.

### What happened?

Archive extraction can create files outside the destination selected by the user. The shared path check joins an archive-controlled name to the destination and performs a lexical `starts_with` comparison. A name such as `folder/../../escaped.txt` still begins with the destination lexically, but filesystem resolution writes it beside that destination.

Isolated tests using Strata's production extraction functions confirmed the escape for ZIP, TAR, and 7z. TAR.GZ uses the same extraction function as TAR after wrapping the input in a gzip decoder. A separate test confirmed that an existing dangling symlink at the destination is followed by `File::create`, allowing a nominally in-destination filename to redirect the write outside it.

Opening an untrusted archive can therefore create attacker-chosen files outside the selected destination at locations writable by the user.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create an isolated root with an empty `destination/` directory.
2. Create a ZIP, TAR, or 7z archive containing a regular-file entry named `folder/../../escaped.txt`.
3. Extract the archive into `destination/` using Strata.
4. Observe that `escaped.txt` is created in the isolated root, outside `destination/`.
5. Separately, create `destination/victim.txt` as a dangling symlink to `../escaped-via-link.txt`, then extract an archive entry named `victim.txt`.
6. Observe that the symlink target outside the destination is created.

### Expected behavior

Every extracted object must remain beneath the selected destination even when entry names contain traversal components or destination path components are symlinks. Unsafe entries should fail the extraction without creating out-of-tree files.

### Screenshots or video

N/A — no screenshot was captured; filesystem assertions provide deterministic evidence.

### Relevant logs

N/A — extraction completes without reporting an error.

### Additional context

- `safe_extract_path` performs the insufficient lexical check at `src/adapters/local_operations.rs:831-836`.
- `ExtractNameResolver::resolve` preserves inner `..` components at `src/adapters/local_operations.rs:948-966`.
- Raw entry names reach the shared resolver and filesystem writers for ZIP (`984-1001`), TAR (`1023-1043`), and 7z (`1115-1141`).
- Temporary adjacent unit tests called the production ZIP, TAR, and 7z extraction paths and asserted that each created its marker outside the destination; all three passed. A fourth test confirmed the dangling-symlink redirect. The diagnostic tests were removed after the audit.
- Archive support was introduced by `d3e5847`; PR #81 stated that extraction included path-traversal protection.
- Open issue #8 tracks descriptor-relative hardening for pre-existing recursive operations. This archive-specific deterministic traversal was introduced later and needs explicit format coverage.

#### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Reject absolute paths, prefixes, root components, and every parent-directory component before conflict-name rewriting.
- [ ] Use archive-native enclosed-path helpers where available, but keep one shared invariant for all formats.
- [ ] Create directories/files descriptor-relatively with no-follow/beneath guarantees so pre-existing or swapped symlinks cannot redirect output.
- [ ] Tests cover ZIP, TAR, TAR.GZ, and 7z traversal names plus dangling and intermediate destination symlinks.
- [ ] A failure leaves no files outside the destination.
issues.title: Archive extraction can write outside the selected destination

title: fix(archive): confine extraction to destination
