## Description

Adds `Ctrl+Up` and `Ctrl+Down` to jump the keyboard focus straight to the first or last visible entry in the active pane/Miller column, instead of stepping one item or one page at a time. It reuses the existing page-selection clamping logic (`NavigationState::page_selection`) with an unbounded page size so the jump lands exactly on the edge entry, respecting hidden-file visibility the same way `Page Up`/`Page Down` already do. The pane scrolls all the way to that edge to match. Also adds the shortcut to the Settings keybindings reference.

## Visual evidence

N/A — keyboard-only navigation behavior, no visual change to the UI besides the new Settings reference row.

## How to test

1. Open a folder with more entries than fit in one pane (or shrink the window).
2. Click into the file list and press `Ctrl+Down`.
   **Expected result:** focus and selection jump directly to the last entry, and the pane scrolls to the bottom.
3. Press `Ctrl+Up`.
   **Expected result:** focus and selection jump directly to the first entry, and the pane scrolls to the top.
4. Repeat in a Miller column and with hidden files toggled on/off to confirm hidden entries are skipped/included correctly.
5. Open Settings → Keybindings and confirm "Jump to top / bottom" is listed under Navigation.

## Related issue

Closes #357

issues.body:
## Problem or use case

There is no keyboard shortcut to jump directly to the first or last entry in the active pane/column. Getting to the top or bottom of a long directory listing currently means holding an arrow key, repeated `j`/`k`, or several `Page Up`/`Page Down` presses. This was called out explicitly in the keyboard-workflow feedback in #291 ("top/bottom navigation" listed among the missing common jumps).

## Proposed solution

Add `Ctrl+Up` to jump the focus to the first visible entry in the active pane, and `Ctrl+Down` to jump to the last visible entry, mirroring the existing `Page Up`/`Page Down` behavior (scoped to the focused pane or Miller column, respecting hidden-file visibility) but going all the way to the edge instead of one page at a time. Update the in-app keybindings reference in Settings to document the new shortcut.

## Alternatives considered

- `Home`/`End`: conflicts with the existing `Alt+Home` "go to home directory" shortcut and with in-line text field editing (filter/rename fields use Home/End for cursor movement).
- `gg`/`G` (Vim-style): inconsistent with Strata's existing single-key `h`/`j`/`k`/`l` bindings and would require sequence/leader-key handling not currently present.

## Strata version

0.9.1 development version.

## Additional context

Related to #291 (keyboard-first workflow audit), which lists first/last-item navigation as one of the missing jumps.

author: pdwaldrop
body:
## Description

The last piece of #8's acceptance criteria: move's primary path called GIO's `move_async` directly -- plain path-based, only guarding the final path component from being a symlink. Every ordinary move (cut/paste, drag/drop, undo, restore from trash) went through this, unlike copy (#254) and delete (#253), which already route through a descriptor-relative walk.

Moves between two native local paths now resolve with a single `renameat2`, opening each side's parent directory fresh (walking from the filesystem root with `RESOLVE_BENEATH`/`RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS`) right before the call, so a symlink or path-component swap can't redirect it, and `NOREPLACE` fails closed instead of silently overwriting whatever a race put at the destination name. A rename the kernel can't do atomically -- into the source's own subtree, or across filesystems -- reports the same `WouldRecurse` signal GIO's move would, so the existing copy-then-delete fallback (added in an earlier PR) still handles it unchanged.

While building this I found two related gaps in the same area and folded them in rather than opening two more PRs for the same acceptance criteria:

- The parent-directory helper this reuses (previously delete-only, `open_local_delete_parent`) is now shared and renamed `open_local_parent_directory`. Copy's own parent-open was weaker than delete's -- a single `O_NOFOLLOW` open that only protects the immediate parent's own name, not an ancestor further up the path. `copy_rejects_a_symlink_higher_in_the_sources_parent_path` demonstrates a symlink swap one level higher than the immediate parent was not caught before this change.
- `replace_local`'s single-file staging copy now goes through `copy_recursively` like the directory case already did, instead of a separate raw GIO copy call. This is mostly a consistency cleanup -- `replace_local_with` already re-validates the source's identity (via the same hardened helper) before either branch runs, so a static-symlink test can't distinguish old from new behavior here. The real effect is narrowing the window between that upfront check and the actual read. I've been explicit about this in the test's doc comment rather than overselling it as newly-demonstrated coverage.

## Visual evidence

N/A -- this is internal file-operation plumbing with no UI surface. Verified manually in a running instance instead: cut/paste of both a file and a directory between two real folders, confirming correct content, an empty source afterward, and (via `ls`) that mtimes were preserved (a real rename, not a copy).

## How to test

Automated coverage (all in `src/adapters/local_operations/tests.rs`):
- `a_plain_move_relocates_the_entry_via_the_hardened_rename_path` -- ordinary move via the new fast path
- `moving_a_directory_into_its_own_child_fails_instead_of_deleting_it` -- the kernel's `EINVAL` correctly triggers the fallback, and the (equally impossible) fallback fails without deleting the original
- `move_rejects_a_symlink_in_the_destinations_parent_path` -- new protection; fails against the pre-fix implementation

author: l0gicgate
body:
## Description

Track copy and move progress from GIO byte callbacks instead of advancing only after each item completes. Aggregate bytes across multi-item and recursive transfers, preserve truthful indeterminate progress when totals are unavailable, and keep the preparing animation active while remote trees are sized.

Zero-byte transfers fall back to item progress so an empty tree no longer appears complete before its entries are copied.

Remote file copies are written to a private sibling stage before publication. Cancelling or failing a copy removes the incomplete stage without touching the final destination, and publication fails safely when the backend cannot perform a native move.

## Visual evidence


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/348f7e04-db10-4a07-a4dc-45df740777db



## How to test

1. Copy a large file to a network share and watch the transfer dialog while bytes are being written.
2. Copy a directory containing multiple files, then copy a tree containing only empty files/directories.
3. Cancel a large file copy to a network share before it finishes, then inspect the destination directory.

**Expected result:** The bar advances during transfers with known byte totals, pulses continuously while a total is unavailable, and does not show 100% for a zero-byte tree until all requested items complete. A cancelled remote file copy leaves neither a partial final file nor a private `.strata-copy-*` stage.

## Related issue

Fixes #249

issues.body:
## Problem or use case

During a large file copy or move, the transfer progress indicator stays at **0%** for the entire operation. The destination entry’s size in the file list / transfer UI does update as bytes land on disk, so work is clearly happening. When the transfer finishes, the bar jumps (or completes) without having reflected intermediate progress.

That makes long transfers look stalled and removes any useful ETA / percent feedback.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Copy or move a large file (hundreds of MB or more) within Strata.
2. Watch the transfer progress UI and the destination item’s reported size.
3. Observe the progress value remaining at 0% while the destination size increases.
4. When the operation completes, note that progress only then reflects completion.

## Expected behavior

Progress should track bytes transferred (or an equivalent reliable signal) throughout the operation:

- Percent / bar advances as the destination grows or as the backend reports transferred bytes.
- Multi-file transfers aggregate completed bytes + current-file bytes over total planned bytes.
- Cancellation, conflicts, and failures still leave the progress UI in a truthful state.

If exact total size is unknown (some remote backends), show determinate progress when size is known and a clear indeterminate / byte-count mode otherwise — never a frozen 0% while bytes are visibly writing.

## Proposed solution

Wire the transfer progress widget to the same byte counters already driving destination size updates (or to GIO / local operation progress callbacks). Update on a reasonable cadence (e.g. on progress signals or throttled size polls), not only on operation completion.

## Alternatives considered

- Indeterminate spinner for all large transfers: hides the false 0%, but throws away useful percent when size is known.
- Relying on destination size alone in the list without a progress bar: already partially works, but the dedicated progress UI still lies.

## Strata version

0.9.0

## Additional context

Related but not duplicates: updater download progress (#24 / #48 / #148), cross-volume DnD defaults (#248), partial-result messaging on cancel (#11).

author: ogarza
body:
## Description

Extract Grid's 80ms adjustment settle into a shared `install_scroll_settle` and attach it to Explorer's inner `ListView` scroller.

While `value-changed` is firing, Explorer bind still writes the five column strings (and skips `set_label` when the text is unchanged) so recycled rows keep the right name/size/date. It no longer starts `set_thumbnail_or_icon`, `request_metadata_fill`, cut CSS, `set_modified_date` timer registration, or `file-appear`. Those run once on the bound pool after the timeout via `refresh_explorer_section`. Placeholder / new-item bind stays on the unfiltered branch and is not gated.

Row chrome is built by `assemble_explorer_row`; bind, settle refresh, and metadata updates share `explorer_row_parts` so that walk cannot drift. `.explorer-fast-scroll` disables row transitions the same way `.grid-fast-scroll` does.

A clamp from hiding files near the bottom of the list can trip the same settle flag as a fling; icons catch up on the timeout. Clipboard, undo, and rename stay on the model/selection path.

## Visual evidence

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/74170168-f8f3-4b90-816e-cc73e96f569f

## How to test

1. Open a large listing and fling / thumb-drag in List, then the same motion in Grid.
2. Stop scrolling and confirm icons, cut fade, and live dates fill in on the visible rows.
3. Create a file, rename, copy/paste, undo, and toggle hidden files while scrolled near the bottom.

**Expected result:** List bind stays on text during movement; expensive work runs after settle. New-item field still appears. Hidden toggle may pop icons in ~80ms if the scrollbar clamped.

## Related issue

Closes #368

author: ogarza
body:
## Description

Grouped Grid stacked one `GtkGridView` per file type inside a single scroller. GTK then sized rows as `content_height / 30`, so cards grew viewport-tall, almost nothing bound, and wheel scroll could abort with `bounds.y == 0`.

Use one scrollable `GridView` and cluster with `SortListModel`, the same path as ungrouped Grid and Explorer. GridView has no `header_factory`, so a sticky type heading sits above the grid. Heading updates wait for idle and the existing scroll-settle path so a fling does not walk bound cards on every wheel tick.

## Visual evidence

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/feec2047-e9be-4964-8f68-981b3889e7fd

## How to test

1. Enable **Group by file type** (Settings → appearance).
2. Switch to **Grid**.
3. Open a large local folder (the 100k fixture, or any directory with more than a few hundred files of one type).
4. Confirm card height and that a full viewport of tiles is visible.
5. Scroll with the mouse wheel up and down several times.
6. Switch grouping off and confirm ungrouped Grid still behaves as before.
7. Switch to Explorer with grouping on and confirm section headings still work.

**Expected result:** Grouped Grid keeps normal card size, fills the viewport, and wheel scrolling does not abort GTK. The sticky heading updates after scroll settles. Ungrouped Grid and Explorer grouping are unchanged.

## Related issue

Closes #372

issues.body:
**Strata version**

0.10.0 (present on main; not a regression from the Explorer settle work)


**Installation method**

Built from source


**Linux distribution and desktop environment**

Omarchy, Hyprland


**What happened?**

With “Group by file type” on, Grid works in small folders and breaks in large ones.

Cards become extremely tall, only a handful of items are visible (it looks like a partial listing), many icons never appear, and using the scroll wheel can abort GTK:
```
  Gtk:ERROR: gtklistbase.c:2131 gtk_list_base_update_adjustments: assertion failed: (bounds.y == 0)
```
Ungrouped Grid in the same folder is fine. Explorer with grouping is also fine.


**Steps to reproduce**

1. Enable Group by file type (Settings → appearance).
2. Switch to Grid.
3. Open a large local folder (the 100k fixture, or any directory with more than a few hundred files of one type, I see it in a directory with 200k files).
4. Observe card height and how few items fit in the viewport.
5. Scroll with the mouse wheel.


**Expected behavior**

Grouped Grid should virtualize like ungrouped Grid: normal card size, a full viewport of tiles, and wheel scrolling must not abort.


**Screenshots or video**
N/A

**Relevant logs**
```
Gtk:ERROR: gtklistbase.c:2131 gtk_list_base_update_adjustments: assertion failed: (bounds.y == 0)
```

**Additional context**

Latent layout bug. Easy to miss because grouping is off by default and small folders stay under GTK’s limit.

Grouped Grid stacks one GtkGridView per file type in a Box inside a single ScrolledWindow (`build_grid_pane` / `sync_grid_groups`). Each GridView is not the scrollable child, so GTK allocates it the group’s full content height.

GtkGridView then does min_row_height = allocated_height / 30 (GTK_GRID_VIEW_MAX_VISIBLE_ROWS). Once a type group has more than ~30 rows, every row is forced to roughly content_height/30 — cards look viewport-tall, only 1–2 tiles bind, and the next adjustment update can hit bounds.y == 0.

A directory that hits the 100k load cap makes this obvious, but any type group with more than ~30 rows is enough (a few hundred files of one type at typical column counts).

Explorer already avoids this: one scrollable ListView, SortListModel + section_sorter, and header_factory. GridView has no header_factory, which is why Grid used stacked views. A fix needs one scrollable GridView (sort/cluster by type, sticky heading, or equivalent) rather than N full-height grids.

author: pdwaldrop
body:
## Description

`index_tree`'s `ignore::WalkBuilder` always called `.hidden(true)`, unconditionally excluding dotfiles from the index regardless of whether the browser was actually showing hidden files. This affected every search surface: Columns and Grid/Explorer `Ctrl+F`, the `Ctrl+K` search dialog, and (found while fixing this, same root cause) the Move/Copy destination path search.

`index_tree` and `index_tree_with_budget` now take a `show_hidden` flag and pass `.hidden(!show_hidden)` to the walker. One subtlety worth calling out: that call has to come **after** `.standard_filters(true)` in the builder chain -- `standard_filters` enables its own `.hidden(true)` internally, so if `.hidden(!show_hidden)` were called first (a natural first attempt), `standard_filters` would silently override it back to always-hidden. I caught this because my first version of the fix passed its own test but still failed the "does this differ from the buggy code" check, which is what led me to look at the bundle's implementation.

Each call site now reads the current show-hidden preference at search time: per-column preferences for Columns' recursive search (matching how that search is already scoped to one column's subtree), the global preference everywhere else.

## Visual evidence

Before (hidden files shown in the browser, `.steamid` present, but searching for it returns nothing):

![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pdwaldrop/strata/fix/366-search-hidden-files/docs/screenshots/366/before.png)

After (same folder, same query, same hidden-files-shown state):

![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pdwaldrop/strata/fix/366-search-hidden-files/docs/screenshots/366/after.png)

## How to test

1. Open a folder containing a visible hidden file (e.g. `.steamid`).
2. Turn on hidden files (`Ctrl+H` or `Ctrl+.`) and confirm the file appears in the listing.
3. Press `Ctrl+F` and type a prefix of the name (e.g. `steam`).
4. Repeat with `Ctrl+K`, and in Columns, Grid, and Explorer.

**Expected result:** the hidden file matches. Turning hidden files back off and repeating the search should return no matches again.

Automated coverage: `hidden_files_are_indexed_only_when_show_hidden_is_enabled` in `src/services/search/tests.rs` exercises both directions directly against the walker.

## Related issue

Closes #366

## Description

Share preview eligibility and browser-event handling between the main window and portal chooser. The chooser now follows the single-click preview preference (enabled by default), offers Quick preview for supported files in its context menu, and routes video controls through the same preview drawer.

Also preserve the running helper in private storage when a long-lived portal outlives a replaced Strata executable, avoiding the renderer failure shown in the report.

## Visual evidence

Before: the supplied report screenshot shows the chooser pane opening with “The sandboxed preview renderer failed.”

After: N/A — pointer-injected capture is not reliable in the available Wayland test session; the shared drawer has no new visual design.

## How to test

1. Open a portal file-picking dialog and single-click a supported image, video, audio, PDF, or text file; also press Space and use **Quick preview** from its right-click menu.
2. Start the portal backend, replace its executable while it remains running, then preview an image or video.

issues.body:
### Problem or use case

The system file chooser does not open quick preview from a single click because it explicitly disables the browser's single-click preview behavior. Space/context-menu preview can also fail in the long-running portal backend after the Strata executable is replaced: the preview sandbox resolves `current_exe()`, which points at a deleted path until the portal process restarts.

Users should get the same quick-preview behavior and supported file types in the chooser as in the main app, including best-effort video previews.

### Proposed solution

- Share preview eligibility and preview event coordination between the main window and chooser rather than maintaining chooser-specific filtering.
- Enable single-click preview in file-picking dialogs by default, using the same preference and supported types as the main browser.
- Keep a Quick preview action in the chooser's right-click file menu.
- Allow the sandbox helper executable to remain available when a long-lived portal process outlives an installed/rebuilt executable.
- Cover images, video/audio/GIF media, PDFs, and supported text files consistently.

### Alternatives considered

Restarting the portal whenever Strata is upgraded/rebuilt avoids the deleted-executable failure temporarily, but does not fix single-click behavior and is brittle for package upgrades.

### Visual examples

A chooser preview pane displayed “Preview unavailable — The sandboxed preview renderer failed” for a PNG after the portal process's executable had been replaced.

### Strata version

Source build at `54c8dd8` or later.

### Additional context

Environment: Arch Linux / Hyprland. Installation: built from source. Reproduction:

1. Start `strata --portal`.
2. Replace/rebuild the executable while the portal remains running.
3. Open the system file chooser and preview an image with Space or the context menu.
4. The helper sandbox fails because `/proc/<portal-pid>/exe` points to the deleted executable.

author: spandan11106
body:
## Description

In Column (Miller) view, clearing a settled recursive-search filter left the column's rows with generic fallback icons, no folder chevrons, and no hover file-size overlay until an unrelated listing rebuild.

The empty-query branch of the column filter handler swapped the `FilterListModel` back to the directory listing *before* clearing `recursive_search_active`. GTK binds the visible rows synchronously inside `set_model`, so the row factory still believed search was active, looked up the already-emptied `search_results`, and took its missing-entry path — fallback icon, hidden chevron, and an empty `.file-size` label for hover CSS to fade in. Scroll and resize do not rebind rows that stay on screen, so the state persisted until something rebuilt the model (sort change, folders-first toggle, reload, navigating away and back).

The reset now lives in `deactivate_recursive_search`, which drops the flag before the model swap so those rows rebind against the directory entries. A regression test asserts the flag is already clear when the filtered model announces the re-added rows; it fails on the previous ordering.

## Visual evidence

N/A — the fix restores the thumbnails and hover sizes shown in the issue's video; there is no new or changed UI.

## How to test

1. Open Strata in Column (Miller) view and enter a folder that shows image thumbnails.
2. Hover a file and confirm the size overlay appears.
3. Focus the column, open its filter (`Ctrl+F`), type a query, and wait ~200ms for the subfolder search to settle.
4. Backspace until the filter is empty.
5. Hover files and scroll the column.

**Expected result:** thumbnails and hover file sizes come back immediately when the filter empties, with no need to change the sort order or reload the column.

## Related issue

Closes #377

issues.body:
### Strata version
0.10.0 (built from source, commit f584b93)

### Installation method
Built from source

### Linux distribution and desktop environment
Omarchy (Arch), Hyprland

### What happened?
In Column (Miller) view, after using a pane filter and then backspacing it empty, rows in that column lose their thumbnails (fallback icons) and the file-size overlay that normally appears on hover.

Scrolling and resizing do not restore either. Changing the column’s sort order restores both.

Names stay correct. Explorer and Grid do not appear to do this.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Open Strata in Column (Miller) view.
2. Open a folder that already shows image thumbnails.
3. Hover a file and confirm the size overlay appears.
4. Focus that column and open its filter (`Ctrl+F`, or the funnel button).
5. Type a query and wait briefly so the listing actually changes (~200ms; once the query settles, the column filter searches subfolders).
6. Backspace until the filter is empty.
7. Confirm thumbnails are fallback icons, and hovering a file no longer shows its size.
8. Scroll the column and resize the window: both stay wrong.
9. Change the sort field or sort direction: thumbnails and hover sizes come back.

### Expected behavior
Clearing the filter should restore the directory listing with the same thumbnails and hover sizes as before. Those should not stay missing until a later listing rebuild.

### Screenshots or video
https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3dada8a2-046b-4005-9147-9b9a1b7ca55e

### Relevant logs
N/A (no crash).

### Additional context
The stuck state is a one-shot bad row bind when the filter is cleared, not the thumbnail settle/viewport gate. Scroll and resize do not rebind rows that stay on screen. Sort does: it emits `EntriesReplaced` → `EntryListModel::replace` → `items_changed(0, n, n)`, which unbinds and rebinds every visible row.

Miller columns are different from Explorer/Grid here. A settled non-empty query swaps the column `FilterListModel` onto a recursive-search `StringList`; clearing the query swaps it back to the directory model (`src/ui/browser.rs`, miller `debounce_filter_entry` handler). On empty query the handler:

1. Clears `search_results` and empties the search model
2. Calls `set_model` back to the directory list (GTK binds visible rows here)
3. Only then sets `recursive_search_active` to false

The factory bind still sees search as active during step 2, looks up the already-empty `search_results`, and takes the `entry is None` branch. That path:

- paints the generic documents fallback icon
- hides folder chevrons
- clears `.file-size` (`column_size_text(None)` → empty label, `set_visible(false)`), so hover CSS has nothing to fade in

If `set_filter(None)` is then a no-op (search already removed the filter), nothing rebinds until the next model rebuild.

Losing hover size together with the thumbnails is the missing-entry bind, not a thumbnail-cache miss.

Also restores (same class of rebuild as sort): toggling folders-first, reloading the column, navigating away and back. Does not restore: scroll, window resize.

Related: subfolder search from the miller filter landed in #275. Not a crash; no core dump.

author: spandan11106
body:
Closes #364.

## What changed and why

Discord feedback asked for a rename shortcut that is easier to reach than <kbd>F2</kbd>. <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>R</kbd> was taken by Refresh, so rather than binding one chord to two actions, Refresh gives it up and keeps <kbd>F5</kbd>.

Each item from the issue:

- **Ctrl+R is an alternate default for Rename, F2 retained** — a shared `is_rename_shortcut` predicate accepts <kbd>F2</kbd> and <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>R</kbd> and rejects any extra Alt/Shift/Super modifier.
- **F5 stays the Refresh default, Ctrl+R removed from Refresh** — `is_refresh_shortcut` matches <kbd>F5</kbd> only, and the `win.refresh` accelerator is now `["F5"]`.
- **Rename starts on the active pane's focused item with the same resolution and validation as F2** — both chords go through the one predicate into the existing `begin_rename()` path, in the main window and in the file chooser.
- **The shortcut is not intercepted while a text field, dialog, or other editing context owns it** — the handler bails when the focused widget is editable (covering the inline rename entry and the new-entry row), and the existing modal-layer guard already runs first.
- **Shortcut reference, action labels/tooltips, and keybinding defaults updated** — the footer reference, the Settings keybindings page, and the item context menus in the browser and the chooser all read `F2 / Ctrl+R` for Rename and `F5` for Refresh. A Rename row was added to the Settings file-operations list, which had been missing one.
- **Conflicts are surfaced rather than invoking both actions** — the default accelerators moved into a single `DEFAULT_ACCELS` table, and a test fails if any chord is bound to more than one action.
- **Tests cover the alternate binding, the editing-context guard, and the refresh conflict** — new unit tests over the shortcut predicates, the accelerator table, and the reference lists.

## Manual steps

1. `cargo run -- ~/some-folder`
2. Select an item and press <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>R</kbd>. **Expected:** inline rename opens, same as <kbd>F2</kbd>.
3. While the rename entry is open, press <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>R</kbd> again. **Expected:** the keystroke goes to the text field; nothing refreshes and no second rename starts.
4. Press <kbd>Escape</kbd>, then <kbd>F5</kbd>. **Expected:** the pane refreshes.
5. Press <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>R</kbd> with nothing selected. **Expected:** no refresh, no rename.
6. Open Settings → Keybindings and the <kbd>F1</kbd> reference. **Expected:** Rename shows `F2 / Ctrl + R`, Refresh shows `F5`.
7. Repeat steps 2-4 inside a file chooser dialog (e.g. from another app's open dialog).

## Screenshots

N/A — the visible change is text in the shortcut reference and context menus; keystroke-driven capture is not working on my Hyprland setup at the moment.

issues.body:
## Problem or use case

Rename is currently available through <kbd>F2</kbd>, but users have requested <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>R</kbd> as an additional, easier-to-reach shortcut. This would improve the keyboard-first workflow while retaining the familiar F2 binding.

<kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>R</kbd> is currently assigned to Refresh, so the default bindings and conflict behavior need to be changed deliberately rather than registering two actions for the same chord.

## Proposed solution

- Add <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>R</kbd> as an alternate default shortcut for Rename; retain <kbd>F2</kbd>.
- Keep <kbd>F5</kbd> as the default Refresh shortcut and remove <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>R</kbd> from Refresh.
- Start inline rename for the active pane's focused/selected item, using the same target resolution and validation as F2.
- Do not intercept the shortcut while a text field, dialog, or other editing context owns it.
- Update the in-app shortcut reference, action labels/tooltips, and configurable-keybinding defaults.
- Ensure the keybinding configuration UI reports conflicts and cannot silently assign the same chord to Rename and Refresh.

## Alternatives considered

- Keep F2 as the only rename binding: avoids a conflict, but does not address the requested keyboard ergonomics.
- Keep Ctrl+R for Refresh: this follows browser conventions, but Refresh remains available through F5 and customizable keybindings can allow users to restore Ctrl+R if preferred.
- Register Ctrl+R for both actions and resolve it contextually: ambiguous and likely to trigger the wrong operation.

## Visual examples

N/A — this is a keyboard interaction change based on Discord feedback.

## Strata version

`main`

## Additional context

Related to the broader keyboard workflow audit in #291. The same feedback requested <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>Up</kbd>/<kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>Down</kbd> for first/last-item navigation; that is already tracked separately by #357. Refresh support was introduced in #172.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Ctrl+R and F2 both start rename for the same unambiguous active item.
- [ ] F5 continues to refresh; Ctrl+R no longer refreshes by default.
- [ ] Ctrl+R does not trigger a browser action while editing text or interacting with a modal.
- [ ] The shortcut reference and configurable-keybinding defaults show the updated bindings.
- [ ] Binding conflicts are surfaced rather than invoking both Rename and Refresh.
- [ ] Tests cover the alternate rename binding, editing-context guard, and refresh conflict.

author: spandan11106
body:
## Description

The Trash sidebar context menu always offered **Empty Trash…**, even with an empty Trash, leaving a destructive row that could not do anything above an orphaned separator.

The sidebar now tracks whether `trash:///` has any top-level entry and hides both the **Empty Trash…** row and its separator until Trash is confirmed non-empty, so an empty Trash shows only **Properties**. Work done for the issue:

- Tracks `trash:///` top-level emptiness even when Trash is not the open location, via a cheap probe that stops after the first entry.
- Keeps that state current after trashing, restoring, permanently deleting, emptying, moving and cancelled operations (browser operation events), and when another application changes `trash:///` (a `trash:///` file monitor).
- Refreshes the state when the context menu is opened, so an external change is reflected the next time the menu is shown.
- Hides the separator together with the row, leaving **Properties** as the only entry in the empty state.
- Fails safe: an unread or failed probe leaves the state unknown, which keeps the destructive row hidden. Concurrent refreshes are coalesced so an in-flight probe cannot publish state that predates the change that triggered it.
- The in-pane/header Empty Trash button keeps its existing disabled-when-empty behavior.
- Tests cover the empty, non-empty and unknown states, the separator following the row, the probe-result mapping, which operations refresh the menu, and the probe itself against an empty directory, a populated one and an unreadable one.

## Visual evidence

N/A — the change only removes rows from a right-click popover, and this environment cannot drive a synthetic right-click at the sidebar (the compositor's focus dispatcher rejects the automation used for screenshots), so no honest before/after capture could be produced. The manual steps below show the difference in a few seconds.

## How to test

1. Empty Trash (`gio trash --empty`), start Strata, and right-click **Trash** in the sidebar. The menu contains only **Properties** — no separator, no **Empty Trash…**.
2. Without restarting, trash a file (select it in Strata and press Delete, or run `gio trash <file>` from a terminal to exercise the external-change path).
3. Right-click **Trash** again. **Empty Trash…** is back, below its separator, and still opens the usual confirmation dialog.
4. Use it to empty Trash, then right-click **Trash** once more.

**Expected result:** the **Empty Trash…** row and its separator appear only while Trash holds at least one item and disappear again as soon as it is empty, without restarting Strata.

## Related issue

Closes #367

issues.body:
## Problem or use case

The Trash sidebar context menu still shows **Empty Trash…** when Trash contains no items. Although the operation is unavailable/no-op, displaying a destructive action that cannot currently do anything adds clutter and suggests that Trash may not actually be empty.

This is especially noticeable because the menu then consists of **Properties**, a separator, and an unusable **Empty Trash…** row.

## Proposed solution

Hide **Empty Trash…** from the Trash sidebar context menu unless Trash is confirmed to contain at least one item.

- Track whether `trash:///` has any top-level entries even when Trash is not the currently open location.
- Keep that state synchronized when an item is trashed, restored, permanently removed, emptied, or changed by another application.
- Build/update the context menu before it is shown so **Empty Trash…** appears immediately when Trash is non-empty and disappears when it becomes empty.
- Hide the associated separator at the same time so **Properties** remains the only row in the empty state.
- If Trash state is still loading or cannot be queried, fail safely without presenting an actionable destructive option until non-empty state is confirmed.

The in-pane/header Empty Trash button can retain its existing disabled-when-empty behavior; this issue is specifically about simplifying the sidebar context menu.

## Alternatives considered

- Keep the option visible but disabled: prevents activation, but retains unnecessary visual clutter and was the behavior this request aims to improve.
- Remove the Empty Trash context action entirely: simpler, but inconvenient when Trash contains items and the user wants to empty it without navigating there first.

## Visual examples

The reported screenshot shows the Trash sidebar context menu containing **Properties**, a separator, and **Empty Trash…** while Trash is empty.

## Strata version

`main`

## Additional context

Related to #130 / #138, which disabled the in-pane Empty Trash controls and guarded the operation when Trash is empty. That change did not synchronize or hide the sidebar context-menu row.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] When Trash is empty, its sidebar context menu contains no **Empty Trash…** row or orphaned separator.
- [ ] When Trash contains at least one item, **Empty Trash…** is visible and retains the existing confirmation flow.
- [ ] The menu updates after trash, restore, and empty operations without restarting Strata.
- [ ] External changes to `trash:///` are reflected the next time the context menu opens.
- [ ] Unknown/error state does not expose an incorrectly actionable destructive option.
- [ ] Tests cover empty, non-empty, transition, and separator visibility states.

## Description

Reduce `ui/browser.rs` from 11,054 to 1,386 lines by separating feature implementations, the Miller row factory, and adjacent tests. Keep the browser facade, controller ownership, and event ordering intact.

Consolidate modal hosting, selection-action callbacks, entry matching, GIO location conversion, and bounded Trash traversal. Document ownership and deferred cleanup. Commits separate structural moves from deduplication; no operation-policy or visual changes are intended.

## How to test

2. In the fixture, exercise copy/cut/paste, drag-and-drop, conflict Replace/Skip/Cancel, move undo, compression/extraction, properties, and hover preview. Check Trash/restore using only disposable files.
3. Open the portal chooser in each view and verify its restricted menus, new-folder action, and selection behavior remain unchanged.

issues.body:
## Context

The browser presentation has grown to 11,054 lines, mixing widget composition, event dispatch, inline editing, transfers, archives, Trash traversal, mounting/authentication, properties, customization, clipboard state, and generic modal/collection helpers. This maintenance task is neither a feature request nor a defect report.

## Investigation

- `src/ui/browser.rs`: primary coupling hotspot; `append_column` alone is 1,177 lines. Shared callers include alternate modes, the portal chooser, window chrome, preview, and settings.
- Other large production modules: `ui/browser_modes.rs` (4,521), `app/browser.rs` (3,577), `adapters/local_operations.rs` (3,544), `ui/settings.rs` (3,211), `ui/window.rs` (2,880). These already have meaningful boundaries but warrant separate focused follow-ups rather than simultaneous rewrites.
- Genuine duplication: modal host discovery/blur setup, selection-aware context action callbacks, root/recursive Trash measurement loops, and native-path/URI-to-GIO conversion.
- Similar code is not always equivalent: browser/preview size formatting differ, chooser menus intentionally restrict actions, and paste/undo conflicts have distinct completion behavior. Preserve these policies.
- Existing regression coverage protects cancellation, bounded traversal, stale results, selection/focus, native paths, cut state, and chooser restrictions. Baseline: formatting and Clippy pass; 786 tests pass, 18 ignored.
- Active work overlaps browser context menus, tabs, Grid virtualization, remote mounts, and transfer policy. Keep structural moves separate from behavior changes and document ownership for rebasing.

## Plan

1. Extract browser responsibilities into private feature modules with explicit imports and a stable `BrowserView` facade. Keep one authoritative application controller and event ordering; do not introduce speculative traits or duplicate navigation state.
2. Extract generic modal infrastructure into `ui/modal.rs`; consolidate host discovery/blur setup without changing dismissal policies. Extract shared collection/entry presentation helpers with narrow visibility.
3. Move bounded Trash enumeration/deletion into an adapter with adjacent tests; share the measurement loop while retaining global budgets, branch-local truncation, cancellation and bounded error collection. Consolidate GIO location conversion.
4. Replace repeated selection-aware context callback wiring with one helper, preserving weak ownership and selection timing. Deduplicate identical filter predicates.
5. Relocate unit tests beside the extracted responsibilities, add focused regression tests for shared boundaries, and document the architecture and deferred work.
6. Run full local formatting, Clippy and tests, exercise display-backed tests and available policy checks, then open a PR and monitor every check.

## Scope guardrails

No new dependencies, UI redesign, changes to themes or assets, operation semantics, native transfer security, async event order, or public browser call sites. In particular, #390, #391, #392, #394 and #395 remain separate fixes. This work should make those changes easier, not silently implement a competing policy.

## Acceptance criteria

- Browser composition/API is understandable without scrolling through unrelated feature implementations.
- Filesystem Trash work no longer depends on widgets.
- Shared logic has one implementation and focused tests; moved tests are not lost.
- Cancellation, native-path fidelity, loading/selection timing and existing UI behavior remain intact.
- Local CI suite and PR checks are green.

author: jesseburlamaque
body:
Closes #399

## Summary of changes

On small displays (e.g. 1366×768, 1280×720) or displays using fractional scaling (e.g. 1920×1200 at 1.666× scale = 1152×720 logical), the hardcoded 1050×720 dimensions for the portal file chooser window exceeded usable screen height (often ~696px with desktop bars), pushing header controls or bottom action buttons against or beyond screen boundaries.

- **Dynamic bounds calculation**: Replaced hardcoded dimensions with `chooser_default_dimensions_for_monitor`, scaling to ~80% width and ~78% height while enforcing minimum breathing margins (at least 120px horizontal and 100px vertical clearance) and bounding between 640×460 (minimum) and 1000×680 (maximum), with a 920×580 fallback.
- **Surface monitor refinement**: Updated `build_chooser` to measure active monitor geometry on window builder initialization and refine `window.set_default_size` post-realization with the surface's monitor.
- **Consistent portal app_id**: Added `glib::set_prgname("strata")` and `glib::set_application_name("Strata")` in `portal::run` so Wayland compositors consistently identify the window class as `strata`.
- **Unit test suite**: Added tests in `src/ui/chooser/tests.rs` covering scaled, standard, small, ultrawide, and degenerate monitor geometries.

## Verification

- `./scripts/check.sh` passes cleanly (cargo fmt, cargo check, cargo clippy, cargo test, cargo-deny, typos).
- Verified manually with `portal-test.py` on an effective 1152×720 scaled display: window fits comfortably inside display bounds with clear margins on all sides.

issues.body:
## Problem or use case

On small screens (such as 1366×768 or 1280×720) or displays using fractional scaling (such as 1920×1200 at 1.666× scale, producing an effective logical resolution of 1152×720), the system file chooser window (`org.freedesktop.impl.portal.FileChooser`) overflows or hits the monitor edges.

Currently, `present_chooser` in `src/ui/chooser.rs` hardcodes default dimensions:
```rust
let window = gtk::Window::builder()
    .title(&request.title)
    .default_width(1050)
    .default_height(720)
    .modal(request.modal)
    .build();
```

When effective logical height is 720px and a desktop top bar (such as Waybar on Omarchy/Hyprland) reserves ~24px, the available screen height is ~696px. Because 720px exceeds the usable screen height, the window title bar and bottom action buttons (`Cancel`, `Open`) get pushed against or beyond the screen boundaries. Similarly, a width of 1050px on an 1152px screen consumes over 91% of the width, preventing the window from appearing comfortably centered.

## Proposed solution

Make the chooser default dimensions responsive to the active monitor geometry:
- Determine monitor logical geometry (`monitor.geometry()`) via `gdk::Display` and `window.surface()`.
- Calculate target dimensions proportionally:
  - Width: ~80% of logical monitor width, clamped between `640px` and `1000px`, ensuring comfortable margin from screen edges.
  - Height: ~78% of logical monitor height, clamped between `460px` and `680px`, ensuring the dialog easily clears desktop bars and docks.
- Update `window.set_default_size` both on builder creation and after window realization.
- Provide a clean fallback (e.g. `920×580`) when no monitor geometry is available.

## Visual examples

![File chooser window bounds touching and overflowing the screen on a scaled 1152x720 display](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jesseburlamaque/strata/screenshots/chooser_overflow_scaled_screen.png)

## Strata version

`main` (`0.11.1`)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Chooser window fits comfortably within monitor boundaries on scaled (e.g. 1152×720) and small screens.
- [ ] Window is well-centered with noticeable breathing room on all 4 sides.
- [ ] Header bar and bottom action row (`Cancel`, `Open`, choices) remain fully visible without clipping or hitting screen borders.
- [ ] Fallback dimensions remain robust on headless or unqueried monitors.
- [ ] Automated tests cover calculation logic across various display resolutions and edge cases.

author: kallupx
body:
## Description

Fixes incomplete 7z extraction by continuing after each successfully extracted entry. Solid archives and archives containing empty files or directories now extract every entry instead of stopping early and reporting success.

## Visual evidence

N/A. This fixes filesystem extraction behavior without changing the interface.

## How to test

1. Extract a solid 7z archive containing multiple files, nested folders, empty files, and an empty folder using “Extract here”.
2. Repeat with a non-solid archive using “Extract to…”.

author: wmfeht
body:
## Description

Combines the two archive-operation fixes previously opened as separate PRs (#408 and #409).

**Private compression staging (#404):** Compression created sibling staging files with mode `0666` (subject to umask) and restored the existing archive's permissions only after encoding. In a shared directory that made the temp archive more widely readable than the file being replaced. Staging files are now created with mode `0600`. Intended permissions are applied only after compression succeeds, immediately before persist. Replacing an archive still copies the original mode onto the published result; new archives still receive the usual umask-adjusted `0666` creation mode.

**Cancelable extraction (#403):** Cancelling an in-progress extraction dismissed the progress UI while the `gio::spawn_blocking` worker kept creating files. The provider set an atomic flag and aborted the supervising GLib task, but only the progress timer read that flag, and dropping the blocking handle detached the worker. Cancellation is now passed into the extraction and copy loops. The supervising task stays alive until the worker observes the flag and returns. Incomplete output is reported as a cancelled operation, and the progress UI is dismissed only after that terminal event.

This supersedes https://github.com/lgse/strata/pull/408 and https://github.com/lgse/strata/pull/409.

## Visual evidence

N/A — staging is a file-mode change. Extraction cancellation is worker lifecycle and incomplete-output handling; the archive progress subtitle now matches other file operations (`Cancelling will not undo completed changes`).

## How to test

### Private compression staging

1. Create a destination directory that other users can traverse, and an archive in it with mode `0640`.
2. Compress a replacement into that archive (Replace) and pause or inspect `.strata-compression-*` while encoding is in progress.
3. Confirm the staging file is `0600` during encoding, then that the published archive is `0640`.
4. Compress a new archive into the same directory and confirm the published mode matches a normal `File::create` (typically `0644` with umask `022`).

**Expected result:** Staging stays owner-only while encoding. Replacement preserves the original archive mode. New archives keep umask-based defaults.

### Cancelable extraction

1. Extract a multi-file archive large enough that the progress dialog appears.
2. Click **Cancel** after extraction has started writing files.
3. Confirm the progress dialog stays up until extraction actually stops.
4. Confirm remaining archive members are not created, and the cancellation dialog reports completed/failed/not-attempted counts. Already-written files are left in place.

**Expected result:** Further extraction stops promptly. The progress UI dismisses only after the worker has stopped. Incomplete output is described, and completed files are not reverted.

## Related issue

Closes #403
Closes #404

issues.body:
## Problem or use case

Strata's unit and integration tests do not exercise the application as a user does. Regressions in pointer input, keyboard focus, clipboard/file operations, click behavior, and switching browser views can therefore reach `main` even when the Rust test suite passes.

We need a small, deterministic end-to-end suite on pull requests that drives the real GTK application, verifies the resulting filesystem/UI state, and captures useful visual evidence when a test fails.

## Proposed solution

Add a headless Linux GUI test harness and a required PR smoke-test job.

### Harness

- Build and launch the real debug binary in an isolated temporary `HOME`/XDG environment with a generated fixture tree. Never read or modify the runner's real files.
- Run the app in a private D-Bus session and deterministic X11 display (`dbus-run-session` + Xvfb) initially. Fix the viewport, scale factor, locale, timezone, GTK theme, bundled font, icon theme, density, and renderer; disable animations.
- Use `pytest` with AT-SPI (`python3-dogtail`/PyGObject) to find controls by accessible role/name and to send keyboard and pointer input. Do not locate controls by screenshot matching or hard-coded screen coordinates. Pointer tests may derive coordinates from the target's accessible bounds.
- Add stable accessible roles, names, and states to Strata where the harness cannot identify or inspect an element. These are production accessibility improvements, not a test-only control API.
- Assert both visible state and actual filesystem effects. Synchronize on observable conditions rather than sleeps; on timeout, report the current accessibility tree.
- Capture a screenshot, accessibility-tree dump, application log, and fixture-tree listing on failure and upload them as CI artifacts.

### Required PR scenarios

Use fresh fixtures per scenario and cover all three browser views where applicable:

- **Drag/drop:** move a file between fixture folders and verify source/destination state and selection. Also cover cancel/no-op and an invalid/self drop target.
- **Copy, cut, and paste:** exercise keyboard shortcuts and context-menu actions; verify copied content remains at the source, cut content moves only after paste, duplicate-name handling is surfaced, and paste enablement follows clipboard state.
- **Keyboard navigation:** move focus/selection, open a directory, navigate parent/back/forward, activate an item, extend/toggle a multi-selection, and confirm focus remains usable after changing views.
- **Single- and double-click modes:** in single-click mode one click opens and keyboard selection still works; in double-click mode one click selects and two clicks open. Verify the preference takes effect without restarting.
- **View switching:** switch among Grid, Columns, and List using both controls and shortcuts; verify the directory, selection, focus, and sort state are preserved.

### Follow-up interaction coverage

After the smoke suite is stable, add scenarios for:

- create folder, rename, trash/permanent-delete confirmation, and undo;
- range/toggle selection and right-click selection behavior;
- type-to-search, recursive search, pane filtering, sorting, and hidden-file toggling;
- quick preview open/close and activation of common file types;
- context menus, dialogs, Escape/cancel behavior, and invalid operations;
- opening a location directly and handling filesystem changes while a directory is visible;
- basic accessibility checks for roles, labels, focus order, selected/expanded state, and keyboard-only completion.

### Visual regression coverage

Interaction assertions should be the primary gate. Add a small set of intentional golden screenshots for stable states (one canonical fixture in each view, selection/focus, context menu, and a representative dialog). Render with software acceleration in the pinned environment, compare with a documented tolerance, and upload expected/actual/diff images on failure. Baseline changes must be reviewable in the PR; do not automatically accept new images.

### CI shape

- Add a separate `e2e` job to `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, pin actions/dependencies, and install only the GTK/AT-SPI/Xvfb packages needed by the harness.
- Run scenarios serially with per-test and suite timeouts, process cleanup, and cancellation support. Target a PR runtime of 10 minutes or less.
- Cache Rust build artifacts, but not mutable test fixtures or screenshot results.
- Retry only infrastructure startup once; do not retry failed interaction assertions.
- Keep the deterministic Xvfb suite required on PRs. Add a non-blocking scheduled/manual Wayland-headless parity job later for backend-specific input and drag/drop behavior, promoting it once reliable.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A local command documented in the contributor docs runs the same E2E suite as CI.
- [ ] The required PR job exercises drag/drop, copy, cut, paste, keyboard navigation, both click modes, and Grid/Columns/List switching.
- [ ] Tests use isolated fixtures and assert filesystem outcomes as well as UI state.
- [ ] Selectors use accessibility semantics; hard-coded absolute coordinates and arbitrary sleeps are rejected.
- [ ] CI rendering is deterministic and the initial reviewed visual baselines are committed.
- [ ] Failures upload screenshots/diffs, logs, accessibility state, and fixture state.
- [ ] The suite has explicit timeouts, cleans up all app/display processes, and completes within the agreed PR budget.
- [ ] A deliberately introduced failure in each critical workflow is detected before the job is made required.

## Alternatives considered

- **Screenshot/image-recognition-only automation:** too brittle for locating controls and insufficient for proving file-operation correctness.
- **Unit tests only:** fast and valuable, but they cannot validate GTK event routing, focus, DnD, clipboard integration, or rendered state.
- **Wayland-only PR automation:** closer to many production desktops, but secure input injection and compositor setup make it less deterministic initially. Keep Wayland parity as a scheduled/manual lane until stable.
- **Pixel-perfect snapshots for every scenario:** expensive to maintain and prone to irrelevant renderer differences. Restrict visual baselines to a small deterministic set and use semantic/state assertions for workflows.

## Visual examples

N/A — this issue adds test infrastructure. CI should attach expected/actual/diff images for visual failures.

## Strata version

`main`

## Additional context

The E2E job should complement, not replace, the existing format, Clippy, and Rust test jobs. Prefer a phased implementation: land the deterministic harness and one vertical scenario first, then add the remaining required smoke scenarios before making the check required.

7. Repeat steps 2–6 in Appearance → Icons and Appearance → List.

`/` should activate type-to-search / the pane filter without inserting `/` as the first query character (same as Ctrl+F: empty field, subsequent keys filter by name). `n` should match `notes.txt`.

### Screenshots or video

https://cursor.com/artifacts/v/art-2c87df1a-de69-48b9-92bc-69a621e93a43

Isolated recording covering Columns, Icons, and List:

- `/` opens the filter with `/` already in it.
- Current-folder names disappear. Nested `alpha-folder/child.txt` can appear because the recursive query `/` matches `/` in relative paths.
- After `n`, the field is `/n` and the view shows **No matching files** (while `notes.txt` is still in the folder).
- Ctrl+F opens an empty “Filter … items…” field; `n` matches `notes.txt` and `LICENSE`.

### Relevant logs

No crash. Directory load of the five-entry fixture completed normally.

### Additional context

`/` is handled as a printable type-to-search seed, not as a filter activator:

- `type_to_search_query` in `src/ui/window.rs` accepts any non-control unicode, including `/`.
- `TypeToSearch::show` then calls `show_filter_with_query` with that character, and `focus_filter_entry` writes it into the Gtk Entry.
- Ctrl+F uses `show_filter()` with no seed, so the field stays empty.
- A non-empty filter starts recursive search; `/` scores against `search_path`, which is why a nested `dir/file` can match while top-level names do not.

Related: type-to-search shipping in #307 / #304; default-on in #387; Space vs type-to-search in #414. Keep a slash-activator fix independent of the open browser refactoring.

issues.body:
### Problem or use case

Strata opens files with their default application, but users cannot choose a different installed application from the file context menu. They must change the system default or leave Strata to open the file with another application.

### Proposed solution

- Add **Open With...** directly below **Open** in the file context menu.
- Use GIO application metadata and Strata's existing GTK dialog patterns to show compatible installed applications for the selected file's content type. Do not parse `.desktop` files directly.
- Launch the selected `gio::AppInfo` with the selected `gio::File` values without changing the system default.
- Support multiple selected files when they share a content type. Hide or disable the action for directories and incompatible mixed selections.
- Preserve local and URI-native locations and show the existing error dialog if the selected application cannot open them.
- Keep the chooser keyboard accessible and consistent with Strata's semantic theming.

### Alternatives considered

- Add a submenu listing every compatible application: this duplicates chooser behavior and makes the context menu longer.
- Rely only on the default application: this does not support workflows such as opening an image in either an editor or a viewer.
- Cover this through custom actions in #36: custom commands are broader and should not replace standard desktop MIME integration.

### Visual examples

N/A. Follow the conventional file-manager placement immediately below **Open**.

### Strata version

Current `main`.

### Additional context

`docs/todo.md` already tracks both an **Open With** chooser and its context-menu action. Strata currently uses GIO to launch the default application and resolve the default handler for a content type, so this should extend the existing desktop-integration path rather than introduce custom application discovery.

comments.body:
Diagnosed and fixed in #425.

The reproduction depends on hidden entries, which explains why the clean synthetic fixture did not trigger it. Grouped Grid builds its ordered section list from every source entry, but filters hidden entries out of each rendered section. A hidden-only file type therefore leaves an invisible, zero-item section between **Folder** and **File**. The old arrow handoff inspected only the immediately adjacent internal section and stopped there.

The fix skips empty sections and targets the next rendered group. I reproduced the original `DataGripProjects` ↔ `hyprland.conf` case on Wayland in the reporter's directory and verified both directions.

The GTK errors were separate but caused by the isolated portal test tooling: private-bus GTK services could replace `/run/user/1000/at-spi/bus_0`. The helper now disables nested portal/accessibility discovery. I also cleaned up the orphan test buses and restarted the user AT-SPI service; the registry is healthy again.

author: spandan11106
body:
## Description

Undo kept a single latest entry, and a completed copy never replaced it. `moved_locations`
stayed empty whenever `moving != Some(true)`, so `replace_pending_undo` returned early and an
older `UndoEntry::Trash` stayed the Ctrl+Z target: a copy could not be reversed, and undoing
after one restored unrelated deleted items.

Paste now reports the destination it writes for each item through `TransferProgress`, the same
way deletion and restoration already report per-item locations. The browser accumulates those
for the running operation, so a completed, failed, or cancelled copy records an
`UndoEntry::Copy` holding exactly what it created — the adapter's own generated name for a
same-folder duplicate, and the resolved destination when a conflict was answered with Replace.
Undoing it trashes only those destinations; nothing derives a destination path a second time,
so a generated or conflict-resolved name can never be missed or guessed wrong.

Undoing a copy sends the copies to Trash rather than erasing them, so pressing Ctrl+Z can never
destroy data outright, and that internal deletion deliberately records no undo entry of its own.

The single pending-undo slot becomes a bounded history (32 entries), because a copy undo has to
leave the operation before it reachable. Undoing the latest entry now pops it and exposes the
previous one instead of clearing the slot; an entry left with nothing to retry is dropped for the
same reason. Deletion is extracted into one pass shared by delete and copy undo, since copy undo
starts from locations rather than `FileEntry` values.

Addressing the issue's acceptance criteria:

- A completed copy becomes the latest undoable operation and displaces an older trash or move undo.
- Ctrl+Z after that copy removes only the copies it created, including same-folder generated names and conflict-resolved destination names.
- Original source items are left in place, and unrelated trash or move entries are never applied as if they were latest — a copy that created nothing (a no-op paste) leaves the previous entry current rather than presenting it as the copy's undo.
- After the copy undo completes, the previous reversible operation is available again.
- Automated tests cover copy undo ordering, same-folder generated names, conflict-resolved destinations, partial and cancelled copies, and the history bound.

## Visual evidence

N/A — nothing in the interface changes. The change is only in which items an undo removes or
restores, which the reproduction steps below show directly in the file view.

## How to test

1. In a writable directory containing at least two files, select one and press <kbd>Delete</kbd> to trash it.
2. Select a different file, press <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>C</kbd>, then <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>V</kbd> in the same folder to create a `name (1).ext` duplicate.
3. Press <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>Z</kbd>.
4. Press <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>Z</kbd> again.
5. Repeat steps 1–3 with the paste targeted at a different folder, and again after answering a "File already exists" conflict with Replace.

**Expected result:** step 3 removes only the duplicate the copy created — the copy source stays
put and the trashed file stays in Trash. Step 4 then restores the trashed file, because the
trash operation is the previous reversible one again. The cross-folder and conflict-resolved
pastes behave the same way: undo removes just the destination that paste wrote.

## Related issue

Closes #390

issues.body:
Split from the grouped rename and copy/paste report ([#354](https://github.com/lgse/strata/issues/354), item 2 of 5).

## Strata version

Reproduced on source build at commit `183d744` (v0.10.0, debug build from `wmfeht/strata`).

## What happened?

After deleting files with an undoable trash operation, then copying other files, `Ctrl+Z` restores the previously deleted files instead of undoing the copy.

Copy does not replace the latest reversible operation, so an older trash undo is still treated as current. Users cannot reverse a completed copy, and they can accidentally restore unrelated deleted items.

## Steps to reproduce

1. In a writable test directory, delete one or more files with the undoable trash operation (Delete, not Shift+Delete).
2. Select different files, copy them (`Ctrl+C`), and paste (`Ctrl+V`) so the copy completes (same-folder paste creating `name (1).ext` is fine).
3. Press `Ctrl+Z`.
4. Observe that the deleted files are restored from Trash instead of the copies created in step 2 being removed.

## Expected behavior

Undo targets the most recent completed file operation.

A completed copy must participate in that global latest-operation ordering. Undoing it removes only the copies that operation created — including same-folder generated names and conflict-resolved destination names — and does not restore, overwrite, or otherwise touch unrelated items.

Trash undo remains available afterward if it is still the previous reversible operation.

## Screenshots or video

Repro recording (trash → copy/paste → Ctrl+Z restores trash, duplicate remains):

https://cursor.com/artifacts/v/art-bb08bf82-f002-4edd-805f-7b18c9fbb42b

## Additional context

Undo is a single latest entry (`PENDING_UNDO`). There is no `Copy` variant; `replace_pending_undo` is called for trash and for moves that left their directory. Copies never replace it.

On a copy paste, `moved_locations` stays empty when `moving != Some(true)`, so `replace_pending_undo` returns early and the prior `UndoEntry::Trash` remains the Ctrl+Z target.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A completed copy becomes the latest undoable operation and displaces an older trash or move undo.
- [ ] `Ctrl+Z` after that copy removes only the copies it created, including same-folder generated names and conflict-resolved destination names.
- [ ] Original source items are left in place. Unrelated trash/move undo entries are not applied as if they were latest.
- [ ] After the copy undo completes, the previous reversible operation (if any) is available again.
- [ ] Automated tests cover copy undo ordering, same-folder generated names, and conflict-resolved destinations.

author: spandan11106
body:
## Description

Renaming a file to an invalid basename in the Columns view aborted the whole process instead of
rejecting the name.

`ViewState::submit_rename` held `active_rename.borrow_mut()` while calling `Browser::rename`.
`Browser::rename` validates the basename itself and reports a bad one by emitting `RenameFailed`
**before it returns**, and that handler borrows `active_rename` again to flag the field — so every
synchronous rejection hit `RefCell already mutably borrowed` and aborted (a panic across a GTK
callback cannot unwind).

The fix reads the renamed entry in a borrow scoped to end before the call. The failure then lands
where it was always meant to: the inline field turns red, keeps focus, stays editable, and its
tooltip carries the reason. No other behaviour changes.

Covered by all three names the issue reports:

| Typed name | Result |
| --- | --- |
| *(empty)* | "Enter a name" |
| `bad/name` | "Names cannot contain /" |
| `.` | "That name is reserved" |

One note on the report: only Columns was affected. List and Icons drive the rename from
`ModeViews`, which never holds the borrow across the call — verified by running the new test
against them with the fix reverted. The regression test covers all three modes anyway, since the
crash was one shared handler away from them.

## Visual evidence

Screenshots cannot be attached from the CLI, so they are described here; the new test renders the
exact states below.

**Before:** nothing to capture — the process aborts on Enter, the window disappears, and the
terminal prints `thread 'main' panicked at src/ui/browser/events.rs:381: RefCell already mutably
borrowed` / `thread caused non-unwinding panic. aborting.`

**After:** the row stays in place with the inline rename field still open, the entry drawn in the
theme's error state (red border and text) around the rejected text, focus back in the field, and a
tooltip giving the reason. Same in Columns, List, and Icons.

## How to test

1. Build and run: `cargo run`.
2. Select any file in the Columns view and press <kbd>F2</kbd>.
3. Clear the name and press <kbd>Enter</kbd>.
4. Repeat with `bad/name` and with `.`, and in the List and Icons views.

**Expected result:** Strata stays running. Each invalid name leaves the rename field open and
flagged red with a tooltip explaining the problem ("Enter a name", "Names cannot contain /", "That
name is reserved"), the field stays editable and focused so the name can be corrected, and the file
on disk is untouched. A valid name still renames, and re-submitting the unchanged name still just
closes the editor.

## Related issue

Closes #428

issues.body:
Split from the grouped rename and copy/paste report ([#354](https://github.com/lgse/strata/issues/354), item 4 of 5).

## Strata version

Reproduced on source build of Strata v0.10.0 (`main`, debug build) with an isolated temp `HOME` / XDG fixture.

## What happened?

When a paste collides with an existing name, Strata shows a “File already exists” dialog with Replace, Skip, Cancel, and an **X** close button in the header. Clicking **X** does nothing: the dialog stays open and no choice is applied.

Cancel and Escape already dismiss the dialog. The header close control looks like the same action and should behave the same way.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Create `source/report.txt` and `dest/report.txt` (same basename, different content).
2. Copy `source/report.txt` and paste into `dest/` so the “File already exists” dialog appears.
3. Click the header **X** close button.
4. Observe that the dialog does not dismiss and the paste is neither cancelled nor completed.
5. Confirm that Cancel and Escape *do* dismiss the dialog without writing files.

## Expected behavior

**X**, Cancel, and Escape all cancel the conflict flow:

- The dialog is dismissed.
- No files are overwritten, renamed, or created as a result of that paste.
- Cancelling abandons the whole operation (matching current Cancel behavior).
- Focus returns to the browser so keyboard use can continue.

Replace and Skip must keep their current meaning.

## Screenshots or video

Repro recording (X fails to dismiss; Escape / Cancel work; files unchanged):

https://cursor.com/artifacts/v/art-9612e792-e219-46e3-bfd8-53dd93ff8dc2

## Additional context

`confirm_replace_conflict` in `src/ui/browser.rs` builds the dialog with `message_dialog_layout`, which always includes `layout.close` (the header **X**). Handlers are wired for Cancel, Skip, Replace, and Escape, but **`layout.close` is never connected**. Other modals in the same file (transfer-destination, empty-trash, archive-conflict) already connect `layout.close` to `dismiss_modal_layer`.

Copy/move undo collision uses the same `confirm_replace_conflict`, so **X** is broken there too. Fix the shared helper rather than only the paste caller.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The conflict dialog’s **X**, Cancel, and Escape all dismiss the dialog without modifying files.
- [ ] That cancel path is used for paste collisions and for undo-move collisions.
- [ ] Multi-conflict prompts: **X** on any prompt abandons the whole operation, including earlier Replace/Skip choices from that batch.
- [ ] Replace, Skip, Enter, and “apply to all” are unchanged.
- [ ] After dismiss, focus returns to the browser.
- [ ] Automated tests (or a focused UI test) assert that close, cancel, and escape take the same cancel path.

**Labels suggestion:** `bug`, `UX`

author: JoeJoeflyn
body:
## Description

Selecting a folder and pressing Ctrl+V pasted into the visible column instead of the selected folder — the selection highlighted a destination the paste ignored (#449).

When exactly one directory is selected, paste now targets it. Files selected, multiple items, or no selection keep pasting into the destination column. A pointer click that opens a child column also moves the paste destination to that column (the mouse stays parked on the parent while the pointer owns navigation, so the hover used to keep the target stuck one column up).

This deliberately diverges from Nautilus/Thunar/Finder, where Ctrl+V always pastes into the current view; here the single-folder selection is the destination.

## Visual evidence

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/00f9e4b2-516f-4dfe-99de-b3ba4d6a5059

## How to test

1. Create `source.txt` and an empty folder `inside/`.
2. Select `source.txt`, Ctrl+C.
3. Single-click `inside/` so it is highlighted (do not descend into it).
4. Ctrl+V.

**Expected result:** `source.txt` appears inside `inside/`. Repeat with a file selected, multiple items, or nothing selected — the paste lands in the current column. Click a folder to open its child column, then Ctrl+V without moving the mouse — the paste lands in the opened column, not its parent.

## Related issue

Closes #449

## Description

Properties left the Pin control insensitive once a location was already pinned, so unpinning looked impossible from that dialog. Themes that dim insensitive labels heavily (Azure Glow, per the report) rendered the label nearly unreadable.

Tasks from the issue:

- **Properties now offers Unpin for a pinned location.** The action switches its label to `Unpin` and removes the location from the sidebar, matching what the pinned sidebar row's context menu already did.
- **The control is readable.** It is a normal sensitive button in both states, so no theme renders it as a dimmed, unreadable label.
- **No insensitive Pin control is left behind.** Where pinning can never apply — files, trash, and the standard places that are always in the sidebar — the control is hidden outright instead of being shown insensitive. This mirrors how the entry context menu already hides "Pin to sidebar" for non-directories.

The pin/unpin decision lives in one pure helper (`pin_action_for`) with unit tests, and the flow is covered end to end by the headless GUI suite.

author: spandan11106
body:
## Description

`src/style.css` ended with an `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` block. GTK's CSS parser rejects `@media` before GTK 4.20, so every launch on the supported baseline (GTK 4.12+, e.g. Ubuntu 24.04's 4.14.5) logged `Gtk-WARNING: Theme parser error: <data>:…: Unknown @ rule` and the block never applied.

Tasks from the issue:

- **Removed the invalid `@media` rule.** The block is gone, so the stylesheet no longer contains anything GTK's parser refuses.
- **No invalid CSS at startup.** `src/style.css` now parses with zero `parsing-error` signals; the remaining at-rules are two `@keyframes`, which GTK has always supported.
- **Reduced motion stays with the existing setting.** Settings → Reduce motion still drives `ui::motion::animations_enabled`, which gates the sidebar, column, and preview animations. No new CSS-side mechanism was added.

A unit test now scans the bundled stylesheet and fails on any at-rule outside `@define-color` / `@import` / `@keyframes`, so a future `@media` cannot slip back in unnoticed.

One thing worth flagging for the reviewer: GTK 4.20 and newer *do* parse `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` — verified locally against GTK 4.22, where the block loaded without error. So on those versions the rule was live rather than dead, and removing it means the *system* reduced-motion preference no longer shortens CSS transitions. That behaviour was inconsistent anyway (it bypassed Strata's own setting and did nothing at all on GTK 4.12–4.19). If the toggle should also cut CSS transitions, that is worth doing deliberately through the setting rather than through a version-dependent media query.

## Visual evidence

N/A — the change removes a stylesheet block that GTK never applied on the supported baseline. It is log-only, with no rendered difference; the visual baseline scenarios in the end-to-end suite are unchanged.

## How to test

1. Build and launch Strata from a terminal on GTK 4.12–4.19 (Ubuntu 24.04 ships 4.14.5).
2. Watch the terminal output during startup.
3. Open Settings and toggle **Reduce motion**, then switch view modes and open the preview.

**Expected result:** no `Gtk-WARNING: Theme parser error … Unknown @ rule` appears at step 2, and the Reduce motion toggle still suppresses the sidebar, column, and preview animations at step 3.

## Related issue

Closes #436

2. Right-click a file, a folder, empty listing space (if applicable), and a sidebar place.
3. Open Appearance and a column Sort menu for side-by-side comparison.

issues.body:
## Problem or use case

Right-click menus (file, folder, chooser, and sidebar) are custom `gtk::Popover`s, but they still read as GTK buttons in a native popup rather than the rest of Strata's menus.

The Appearance and column-sort popovers are the visual language: frameless rows, shared padding, `@theme_*` colors, 9px radius, and an accent glow. Context menus diverge in a few ways:

- Menu rows keep GTK's default button frame (`has_frame` is true).
- Item and folder rows use different padding, min-height, and shortcut sizing.
- Overlay-parented popovers do not restyle `popover.background` or the wrapping `ScrolledWindow`, so a dark rectangular frame shows around the rounded contents (visible in the e2e `context-menu` baselines).
- Focused rows pick up the global button outline on top of that frame.

## Proposed solution

Match the Appearance / column-sort look without changing actions or layout:

1. Build context-menu rows as frameless buttons (`has_frame(false)`), including sidebar items.
2. Unify folder and item option, separator, and shortcut CSS with the existing menu metrics.
3. Make `.folder-context-popover` and `.context-menu-scroll` transparent so only the themed `contents` node paints, matching `.appearance-popover` / `.column-popover`.

## Alternatives considered

- Reusing `.appearance-option` / `.column-menu-option` class names on context rows: would couple unrelated widgets and still leave the overlay popover chrome.
- Switching to `GtkPopoverMenu` / `gio::Menu`: would drop custom icons, shortcuts, and the selection header, and would follow the system theme instead of Strata tokens.
- Styling the popover widget itself like `.peek-popover` instead of `contents`: would double the border/radius against the existing contents rules.

## Visual examples

Compare `tests/e2e/baselines/gtk-4.14/context-menu.png` (dark outer frame, framed last row) with `docs/screenshots/315/view-menu.png` (Appearance menu).

## Strata version

`main` at 3d7dc80

## Additional context

Native GtkEntry / GtkTextView Cut/Copy/Paste menus are out of scope; they never receive these CSS classes.
