comments.author: nixfred
comments.body:
Confirmed on main at 110a433, with a fix available if useful.

Measured cause: for TAR/TAR.GZ the member is handed to `tar::Builder::append_file`, which copies it end to end; for 7z, `push_archive_entry` does the same and the multithreaded LZMA2 encoder additionally buffers a whole 64 MiB chunk before encoding it. `check_archive_cancelled` runs only after each member, so a cancel that arrived 300 ms into a 96 MiB file was honoured 208 seconds later. ZIP is unaffected because it streams through `copy_with_big_buf`.

Fix on my fork: https://github.com/lgse/strata/compare/main...nixfred:strata:fix/archive-cancel-mid-member. It feeds both writers through a reader that fails once the flag is set, refuses compressed output once cancelled (needed for the buffered LZMA2 chunk), maps a writer error back to `Cancelled` when the flag is set, and keeps TAR metadata by setting the header from the open file and using `append_data`. Two deterministic tests inject the output writer and assert nothing beyond one already-filled buffer is written after cancellation; both fail on current main.

Not opened as a PR because it was developed with an AI coding agent, which CONTRIBUTING.md excludes. Take the branch or the analysis in whatever form suits.

### Problem
ZIP already stores known incompressible files, but 7Z applies LZMA2 level 6 to every member. Already-compressed media wastes CPU and makes archive creation feel stalled. TAR.GZ also needs a container-aware policy.

### Proposed solution
Optimize encoding according to each supported format: per-member selection for ZIP/7Z, no compression for TAR, and valid stream-level handling for TAR.GZ. Preserve password encryption, mixed-input compression, file metadata, existing safety/publication behavior, and external-reader compatibility. Audit the existing incompressible-extension heuristic rather than treating every archive/container as compressed. RAR remains extraction-only.

### Acceptance criteria
Demonstrate round trips for every writable format, encrypted and mixed 7Z inputs, retained compression for compressible content, and representative timing/size measurements. Never emit raw TAR under a TAR.GZ extension or omit encryption.

### Context
Owner requested performance work in addition to feedback PR #977. Existing responsiveness/cancellation issue #413 is separate.

Trim tautological unit tests, unused product axes, and second GUI launches of the same UI sequence, and keep a named coverage owner for each remaining contract. The GUI suite spends about half of scenario wall time walking the accessibility tree on every poll, and both the crate unit tests and E2E scenarios still re-run the same observable contracts across unused product axes and duplicate launches. That inflates CI time without adding coverage owners.

issues.body:
### Problem or use case

Users should be able to filter filenames using asterisk notation, such as *.MOV to find files with a particular extension. The supplied screenshot shows *.MOV entered in the Photos folder filter with an empty result list.

### Proposed solution

Support * as a wildcard matching zero or more characters in filenames.

Proposed matching behavior:
- Patterns containing * match the whole filename: *.MOV matches names ending in .MOV, IMG* matches names starting with IMG, and *holiday* matches names containing holiday.
- Support multiple asterisks, for example IMG*.MOV.
- A single * matches all items in the current filter scope.
- Preserve existing plain-text filtering behavior when no wildcard is present, and retain the existing case-sensitivity policy.
- Apply matching consistently across browser view modes without expanding filtering into recursive search.

This request covers asterisk wildcards; full regular expressions or additional glob syntax are not required.

### Alternatives considered

Filtering by plain text such as .MOV is less precise than an extension pattern and does not express prefix/suffix combinations.

### Visual examples

Supplied screenshot: the Photos folder with *.MOV in the filter field and no visible results. Screenshot attachment is pending.

### Additional context

Acceptance examples using files clip.MOV, IMG_001.MOV, IMG_001.jpg, and clip.MOV.bak:
- *.MOV returns clip.MOV and IMG_001.MOV, but not clip.MOV.bak.
- IMG* returns IMG_001.MOV and IMG_001.jpg.
- IMG*.MOV returns only IMG_001.MOV.
- * returns all four files.
- Clearing the filter restores the unfiltered listing.

Also verify zero-character wildcard matches, multiple wildcards, no-match patterns, and unchanged plain-text filtering.

issues.body:
### Strata version

0.17.0

### Installation method

GitHub release (`strata-0.17.0-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz`, installed to `~/.local/bin/strata`)

### Linux distribution and desktop environment

Omarchy 4.0.3-1 (Arch Linux), Hyprland / Wayland
kernel 7.2.3-arch1-3 · gtk4 1:4.22.4-1 · glib2 2.88.3 · gvfs 1.60.2-4 · gvfs-smb 1.60.2-4 · smbclient 2:4.24.6-1

### What happened?

When browsing an SMB server at the **share-list level** (`smb://<host>/`), Strata lists the server's shares and renders them as folders, but activating one does nothing — no navigation, no error, no mount attempt. The panel stays on the share list.

This makes a bookmark pointing at a server root (`smb://<host>/`) a dead end in the sidebar, which is how I originally hit this: Strata reads `~/.config/gtk-3.0/bookmarks`, and a server-level bookmark created by another file manager lands the user on exactly this unusable listing.

The cause looks like GVFS file-type handling. At the browse level, `gvfsd-smb-browse` does not return directories — it returns `G_FILE_TYPE_SHORTCUT` (6) entries whose real destination lives in `standard::target-uri`:

```
$ python3 -c '...enumerate smb://<host>/...'
Backups     | type= 6 | target-uri= smb://<host>/Backups
Documents   | type= 6 | target-uri= smb://<host>/Documents
Music       | type= 6 | target-uri= smb://<host>/Music
Pictures    | type= 6 | target-uri= smb://<host>/Pictures
Videos      | type= 6 | target-uri= smb://<host>/Videos
```

The attribute set Strata uses for the first directory batch does not request `standard::target-uri`:

```
standard::display-name,standard::name,standard::type,standard::is-hidden,standard::is-symlink,access::can-trash,access::can-delete
```

so at render time a shortcut entry has no destination to navigate to, and its type is not `DIRECTORY`. (The later/full attribute set does include `standard::target-uri`.)

Everything else about Strata's SMB support works correctly — this is specific to the browse level. Given a full share URI, Strata mounts on demand and loads fine, including a share that was not mounted beforehand:

```
INFO strata::adapters::local_files: directory load started  request_id=1 backend=smb
DEBUG strata::adapters::local_files: directory load location request_id=1 location=smb://<host>/documents/
INFO strata::adapters::local_files: directory load finished request_id=1 entries=13 elapsed_ms=22
```

and the gvfs mount is created by Strata itself:

```
$ ls /run/user/1000/gvfs/
smb-share:server=<host>,share=documents
```

### Steps to reproduce

1. Have an SMB server on the LAN with at least one share (guest/anonymous read is enough).
2. Launch Strata with the server root: `strata "smb://<host>/"` — or add `smb://<host>/ MyServer` to `~/.config/gtk-3.0/bookmarks` and click that bookmark in the sidebar.
3. The share list renders as folders.
4. Click (or double-click) any share.

Result: nothing happens. Navigating directly to `smb://<host>/<share>` instead works normally.

### Expected behavior

Activating an entry in the server browse listing should navigate into that share — resolving `standard::target-uri` for `G_FILE_TYPE_SHORTCUT` (and `G_FILE_TYPE_MOUNTABLE`) entries and triggering the mount if needed, the way Nautilus does. Failing that, a visible error would at least be better than a silent no-op.

Suggested fix: include `standard::target-uri` in the first-batch enumeration attributes, and treat shortcut/mountable entries as navigable by following their target URI.

### Relevant logs

Full debug log of opening the browse level (`RUST_LOG=debug strata "smb://<host>/"`). The listing loads successfully — there is no error; the entries simply cannot be activated:

```
DEBUG strata: startup gvfs probe finished elapsed_ms=2
INFO  strata::adapters::local_files: directory load started request_id=1 backend=smb
DEBUG strata::adapters::local_files: directory load location request_id=1 location=smb://<host>/
WARN  strata::adapters::local_files: directory monitoring unavailable backend=smb error_domain=g-io-error-quark error_code=15
INFO  strata::adapters::local_files: first directory batch ready request_id=1 entries=11 elapsed_ms=8
DEBUG strata::app::browser: directory batch accepted request_id=1 location=smb://<host>/ entries=11
INFO  strata::metrics: first directory batch rendered entries=11 render_micros=4728 elapsed_ms=315
INFO  strata::adapters::local_files: directory load finished request_id=1 entries=11 elapsed_ms=13
```

(`error_code=15` = `G_IO_ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED` for the file monitor, which is expected on a GVFS browse mount and unrelated.)

### Additional context

Reproducible every time, not intermittent. I cannot say whether it is a regression — 0.17.0 is the first version I have used.

## Description

Portal save/open dialogs fell back to `$HOME` when the caller (browser, app) omitted a folder hint, so "Save As" dialogs opened in home instead of Downloads. Added `default_save_folder()` reusing the existing `home_directory()` helper; prefers `XDG_DOWNLOAD_DIR` (`glib::UserDirectory::Downloads`), falling back to home only when undefined. Wired into the three portal fallbacks: `accessible_folder` (Open + SaveFiles), `save_file_suggestion` (timeout fallback), and `resolve_save_file_suggestion` (invalid `current_file` / missing `current_folder`).

When Strata is installed as the system file chooser (`strata --install-portal`), it draws the browser's "Save As" dialog. The previous home-directory fallback contradicted the XDG convention and the user expectation that downloads land in Downloads. When a browser sends a remembered `current_folder`, Strata still honors it — this change only affects the no-hint fallback.

## Visual evidence

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/75cddd38-85ef-40e4-abfa-ab8822ae3c02

## How to test

1. Ensure Strata is installed as the portal file chooser (`strata --install-portal`).
2. From a browser, trigger a "Save As" with no remembered folder (clear the browser's download history or use a fresh profile).
3. Confirm the dialog opens in `XDG_DOWNLOAD_DIR` (typically `~/Downloads`).
4. Unset `XDG_DOWNLOAD_DIR` (`user-dirs.dirs`) and repeat; confirm the dialog falls back to home.

**Expected result:** With `XDG_DOWNLOAD_DIR` defined, the save dialog opens in Downloads. With it undefined, it falls back to home. Browser-supplied `current_folder` hints are still honored.

## Related issue

Closes #1014

author: Rizmi
body:
Resolves #994

### Problem

1. In Miller Columns mode, typing into the pane filter (`Ctrl+F`) did not filter entries when viewing non-native locations such as Trash (`trash:///`), network places (`network:///`), or remote mounts (`smb://`, `sftp://`, `mtp://`, etc.).
2. When filtering was active in Trash, single-clicking an item attempted to open it with the non-native URI in an external web browser instead of selecting/previewing it.
3. In filtered columns, keyboard arrow navigation stopped after 1–2 jumps because directory commands stepped through hidden underlying directory indices instead of letting GTK's `ListView` step across visible filtered rows.

### Root Cause

1. **Non-native filter early exit**: In `src/ui/browser/columns.rs`, `bind_filter_query` assumed every column location had a native filesystem path:
   ```rust
   let Some(path) = state
       .browser
       .location_at(depth_for_search)
       .and_then(|loc| loc.native_path().map(Path::to_path_buf))
   else {
       return;
   };
   ```
   For `LocationKind::Uri` locations, `loc.native_path()` returns `None`. When this occurred, `search_active` was set to `true`, but execution returned early without notifying or applying GTK's `CustomFilter` (`apply_filter_query`). The column remained unfiltered while leaving `search_active` set.

2. **Premature activation of Trash files on single click**: `column_rows` queued `PendingActivationKind::Mapped` for any filtered item click, which called `activate_in_place` on pointer release. In Trash, this emitted `BrowserEvent::OpenRequested` for non-directory items, causing GIO to launch a web browser on `trash:///...`.

3. **Filtered keyboard navigation lockup**: In `window/keyboard.rs`, `selected_search_results().is_some()` previously checked only `column.search_handle` (recursive search). For in-memory filters, this returned `None`, allowing `item_navigation` to intercept arrow keys and call `browser.move_selection(1)`. `move_selection` advanced through the unfiltered directory entries; if subsequent entries were filtered out, the visible selection became stuck.

### Solution

#### 1. In-Memory Column Filtering for Non-Native Locations
- In `columns.rs` (`bind_filter_query`), when `loc.native_path()` is `None`:
  - Cancel any background search handles/generations.
  - Call `deactivate_recursive_search` so `search_active` is `false`, search results are emptied, and the filtered model is backed by the column's directory model.
  - Apply `apply_filter_query` directly on the column's `FilterListModel` to filter loaded entries in-memory via `entry_matches`.
- Supported keyboard focus transition (Down from filter, Up return-to-filter from row 0) and Enter activation when in-memory filtering is active.

#### 2. Additional Fixes (Required for Filtered Non-Native & Trash Handling)
- **Trash single-click selection and preview**:
  - In `src/ui/browser/columns/rows.rs`, clicking filtered trash files now selects the item and enables single-click preview (`PendingActivationKind::Standard { preview: true }`), returning `None` instead of queuing `PendingActivationKind::Mapped` to prevent `activate_in_place`.
  - In `src/ui/browser_modes.rs`, guarded pointer clicks and filter entry activation to prevent invoking `activate_in_place` on trash files.
- **Safety guard in `open_location`**:
  - In `src/ui/browser/desktop.rs`, `open_location` rejects `trash:///` locations and displays a descriptive error dialog ("Items in Trash cannot be opened") instead of dispatching to external applications.
- **Filtered keyboard navigation**:
  - In `src/ui/browser.rs`, updated `selected_search_results` and `selected_search_result` to map selected positions via `column.map` when `column.map.has_query()` is active.
  - In `src/ui/window/keyboard.rs`, allowed GTK's native `ListView` to own arrow key navigation across visible filtered rows and mapped vim keys (`j`/`k`) via `activate_native_arrow`.

### Testing & Verification

- `cargo test ui::browser::desktop`: verified `open_location_rejects_trash_locations`.
- `cargo test ui::browser::tests::recursive_search`: added assertion in `non_native_location_filters_entries_in_columns_mode` ensuring selecting a filtered trash item does not emit `OpenRequested`.
- `cargo test ui::window::tests`: 78 passing window/keyboard dispatch tests.
- `cargo test ui::browser::columns`: 16 passing column view tests.
- `./scripts/quality.sh fmt`: formatting clean.
- `./scripts/quality.sh clippy`: 0 warnings.
- `cargo check --all-targets --all-features`: 0 errors.

Open Strata in Columns mode. 2. Navigate to Trash (`trash:///`) or any non-native location. 3. Press Ctrl+F to open the pane filter. 4. Type any search term matching an item in the directory. ### Expected Behavior The column list model should filter in real-time, showing only matching directory entries. ### Actual Behavior All directory entries remain visible completely unfiltered. Additionally, selection synchronization and keyboard navigation stop functioning as expected because `recursive_search_active` is left set to `true`. ### Root Cause In `src/ui/browser/columns.rs`, `bind_filter_query` assumes every active column has a native local filesystem path: ```rust let Some(path) = state .browser .location_at(depth_for_search) .and_then(|loc| loc.native_path().map(Path::to_path_buf)) else { return; }; ``` For `LocationKind::Uri` locations (`trash:///`, `network:///`, `smb://`, etc.), `loc.native_path()` returns `None`. When this happens, `search_active` has already been set to `true`, but execution returns early before notifying or updating GTK's `CustomFilter` (`apply_filter_query`). Because the filter is never notified, the model remains unfiltered. Preview:

Streams secondary metadata into visible icon cards without delaying initial directory rendering. Files show size, images show resolution, media shows duration, and folders show item counts. Detail probes use bounded workers and an mtime/ctime-validated in-memory LRU cache so revisits restore metadata immediately. Hover feedback now follows actual thumbnail and caption hit regions rather than the full grid cell.

Local full-suite verification reached 1,592 passing tests but failed in `services::search::tests::performance::fair_adversarial_walk_has_linear_scale` and `ui::browser::inline_edit::tests::entries::new_entries_scroll_into_view_when_the_default_name_sorts_past_the_initial_viewport`. 3. Hover in card gutters and over thumbnails/captions.

issues.body:
## Problem or use case

Icon view only shows file names, so users must open properties or switch views to see useful details. Hover feedback also applies to the whole allocated grid cell rather than the visible thumbnail or caption. Revisiting a directory should not repeat expensive media and image probes.

## Proposed solution

Stream secondary metadata for visible icon cards: image dimensions, media duration, file size, and folder item count. Keep expensive work off the GTK thread, bound worker concurrency and probe runtime, and cache detail results in memory with file-change invalidation. Restrict hover feedback to actual card content.

## Alternatives considered

Loading all metadata before rendering delays the initial directory view. Reusing full-directory sort fills would also probe off-screen files unnecessarily. Persistent disk caching adds complexity that is not needed for small metadata values.

issues.body:
### Problem or use case

Double-clicking (or otherwise activating) a file that has no XDG default application associated should still let the user pick a handler. Today Strata tries the MIME default and, when none is registered, shows an error instead of the existing Open With dialog. The chooser is only a right-click away, so the common activate gesture is a dead end for unassociated types.

### Proposed solution

When activation cannot resolve an XDG/GIO default for a file, open the existing Open With dialog for that file (the same chooser used from the context menu), including recommended and other installed applications. Keep launching the default application when one is registered. Directories should keep their current navigate-in-place behavior. Executable files without a handler should keep the existing Run confirmation.

### Alternatives considered

- Keep the current “Unable to open file” / “No application is registered for this file” error and require right-click → Open With…. That works but fails the activate gesture Nautilus/Dolphin-style managers use for unassociated types.
- Always show Open With on activate, even when a default exists. That would change the usual double-click path for associated files.

### Visual examples

N/A — no running-app capture this session.

### Strata version

N/A — no running-app capture this session.

### Additional context

Related but not the same request:

- [#174](https://github.com/lgse/strata/issues/174) added Open With to the file context menu.
- [#792](https://github.com/lgse/strata/issues/792) improved the chooser (recommended/other apps and search), so it is usable even when a type has no default.
- [#570](https://github.com/lgse/strata/issues/570) was about an empty context-menu chooser for `octet-stream` / broken symlinks, not about routing double-click to the dialog.
- Executables with no handler already take a separate Run confirm path.

Activation currently goes through `OpenRequested` → `open_location`, which launches the default app and reports “No application is registered for this file” when GIO has no default.

## #1013 implementation and validation

The iPhone gphoto2 path now pauses after each full-scan media batch: 200 ms for GTK to publish/bind rows, then up to 2 s for the current device's in-flight thumbnail wave to finish. New waves/other devices cannot extend the pause. This deliberately trades some total scan throughput for early visible previews. Bounded peeks are unchanged. Preview decoding remains sandboxed; the coordination guard ends after result application (or cancellation/failure).

Camera requests coalesce for one frame without continuous-batch debounce, rank visible items top-to-bottom/left-to-right, and rerank camera queue slots on dispatch. Deferred camera work uses the same rank. Cancellation-driven promotion is deferred out of GTK unbind/layout when camera work is present. Noncamera queue slots/FIFO remain unchanged.

The sidebar always shows the full set of default places: Home, Trash, Network, Desktop, Documents, Downloads, Pictures, and Videos. issues.body:
### Problem or use case

In Miller Columns mode, columns currently do not display directory item counts or selection counts. When navigating directory hierarchies or selecting multiple items to move, copy, or inspect, users have no immediate visual feedback on the total number of items within the directory or how many items are currently selected.

### Proposed solution

Display the item and selection count in the column footer on the right side, directly opposite the paste destination hint (`Pointer · Paste here` / `Keyboard · Paste here`), using matching typography and theme styles (`.column-destination-hint`).

To avoid visual clutter across multiple columns, display the count when the column is hovered or active (`active-column`):
- **Normal / Single selection (≤ 1 item)**: displays total item count (e.g. `15 items` / `1 item`).
- **Multi-selection (≥ 2 items)**: displays selection count (e.g. `3 selected`).
- **Filter / Search active**: displays match count (e.g. `4 matches`).
- **Special locations (e.g. Trash `trash:///`)**: displays item count and selection count when hovered or active, even though paste actions are suppressed.

### Alternatives considered

- Placing count indicators in a global window status bar: Miller Columns displays multiple folder tiers concurrently side-by-side; a global status bar cannot clearly convey which column the counts correspond to without awkward focus tracking.
- Keeping counts permanently visible on all columns: Creates visual noise across long horizontal column trails. Keeping it visible on active/hovered columns keeps columns clean while providing information when focused.

### Strata version

v0.18.0-rc.1

### Additional context

Counts update dynamically when directory contents change, items are added or removed, hidden files are toggled, selections change, or pane filters are applied.

body:
## Description

Add an "Open file location" action to the right-click context menu for single-selected files when viewing search or filter results, or when a file lives in a different folder than the current view.

- Visibility is gated to single-selected files with a parent directory; it remains hidden during standard unfiltered browsing for files in the current folder, on folders, in multi-selection, and inside the Trash.
- Uses the newly bundled `strata-folder-open` Lucide icon to visually distinguish the action from the closed folder icon on "Move to…" and "Restore".
- If the file is in a subdirectory or recursive search result, clicking the action navigates to the containing folder and selects/reveals the file.
- If the file is in the currently viewed folder while an inline filter is active, clicking the action clears the filter and re-selects/reveals the file in-place.
- Extends behavioral test coverage across Columns, Icons, and List modes.

## Visual evidence

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ab80f1e6-4656-40c5-8680-d345f2f2df5d


## How to test

1. Open a folder in Columns, Icons, or List mode. Right-click any file in the current directory and confirm **Open file location** is not shown.
2. Press Ctrl+F and type a filter query matching a file in the current directory. Right-click the match and select **Open file location**: confirm the filter clears and the file is focused in-place.
3. Search for a file in a subfolder, right-click the match, and select **Open file location**: confirm Strata navigates to the containing subfolder with the file selected.
4. Confirm the action is not offered on folders, multi-selection, or within Trash (`trash:///`).

**Expected result:**
"Open file location" appears exclusively when filtering or searching, clearly distinguished by the open-folder icon, and successfully reveals the file in its containing folder across all view modes.

## Related issue

Closes #1040

issues.body:
### Problem or use case

When searching or filtering files in Strata, users frequently need to navigate directly to the folder containing a specific result. Currently, there is no direct action to jump to a file's containing folder; users must manually read or copy the path and navigate through the directory hierarchy step-by-step.

### Proposed solution

Add an **Open file location** action to the right-click context menu for single-selected files:
- **Gated visibility:** Appears when search or filtering is active (Ctrl+F / inline filter text) or when the file lives in a different folder/subdirectory than the active view. Remains hidden during standard, unfiltered browsing for files already in the current folder, on folders, in multi-selection, and inside Trash.
- **Visual hierarchy:** Uses the dedicated `strata-folder-open` Lucide icon to visually distinguish it from the closed-folder icon used on **Move to…** and **Restore**.
- **Action behavior:**
  - If the file is in a subdirectory or external path (e.g. recursive search result), Strata navigates to its parent directory and selects/reveals the file.
  - If the file is in the currently viewed folder (e.g. inline filter result), Strata clears the active filter and selects/reveals the file in-place.

### Alternatives considered

- *Permanently showing the action:* Clutters the context menu during standard browsing when the user is already looking directly at the containing folder.
- *Reusing `strata-folder`:* Induces visual ambiguity with **Move to…**. Adopting Lucide's `folder-open` maintains clean semantic distinction.

### Strata version

v0.18.0

### Additional context

Fully supported and verified across Columns, Icons, and List modes.

Restore with **Restore default** (Omarchy only) or `strata --uninstall-udiskie-unlock`. The installer never installs the `udiskie` package. This is not a saved Strata preference.

## Visual evidence

Pending owner upload through the GitHub editor. Settings (**Unlock encrypted volumes**) and the installer prompt are user-visible; no supported authenticated attachment uploader is available in this session.

## How to test

1. On Omarchy with `udiskie` on `PATH`, open **Settings → General → Desktop integration** and choose **Use Strata**. Confirm `~/.config/udiskie/config.yml` points at this build's `--udiskie-hook` and that udiskie restarts.

3. Choose **Restore default**, then plug the volume in again. udiskie's previous prompt behavior should return, and restore state under `~/.local/share/strata/udiskie-install/` should be gone.
4. From a release archive or local install, run `strata --install-udiskie-unlock` / `--uninstall-udiskie-unlock`. On generic Arch, the installer should offer it only when `udiskie` is already on `PATH`.

**Expected result:** opting in makes a plugged-in encrypted drive open Strata's prompt; restore returns udiskie to its previous configuration without installing or removing the udiskie package.

Closes #537

## Description

Host-side helpers that Strata execs by bare name are resolved only under admin-managed search roots: NixOS wrappers first, then `/usr/bin`, `/usr/sbin`, `/bin`, `/sbin`, `/run/current-system/sw/bin` (NixOS), and `/run/current-system/profile/bin` (Guix). Lookup never reads inherited `PATH` or `$HOME`.

Canonicalize of a search hit must land under a trust root (FHS, `/run/wrappers/bin`, `/nix/store`, `/gnu/store`). The executed path is the search hit (for example `/run/current-system/sw/bin/bwrap`), not the store target, so argv0 stays intact for busybox/coreutils and Nix profiles.

Missing `bwrap` and `tar` fail closed. Relaunch and desktop/portal helpers skip or warn as before, without falling back to a relative program name.

Update archive verification hashes the downloaded file in-process with SHA-256 instead of executing `sha256sum`. Jail-internal helper names (`ffprobe`, `dcraw`, `ffmpegthumbnailer`, inner `prlimit`) are unchanged.

## Visual evidence

N/A — process spawn and hashing only; no user-visible UI change.

## How to test

1. Build a sandbox command with `Path::new("/usr/bin/bwrap")` (file need not exist) and confirm `get_program()` is that absolute path, with `--unshare-all`, `--clearenv`, and `--setenv PATH /usr/bin` still present.
2. Hash an empty file and a nonempty fixture with the in-process helper; matching published first-token checksums succeed and mismatches return `Downloaded update failed checksum verification`.
3. Resolve `bwrap`/`tar`/`sh` via search roots only. Confirm a basename that is missing or that is `.` / `..` / a path is `Err`. A symlink whose final target sits outside the trust roots is rejected. A profile symlink into a store fixture is accepted, and `get_program()` is the profile path, not the store target.

**Expected result:** Host helpers start from trusted absolute search-root paths. Inherited `PATH` is unused. Canonical targets stay under trust roots. Jail-internal helper names are unchanged.

## Related issue

Closes #1045

issues.body:
## Summary

Strata invokes a number of external helper programs by bare name, so they are resolved through `PATH` at runtime. Two of them sit on security-relevant paths: `sha256sum`, which performs update verification, and `bwrap`, which *is* the preview sandbox. The codebase already demonstrates the safer pattern elsewhere — `pacman` and `pacman-conf` are pinned as absolute-path constants (`src/services/update_install.rs:25-26`), and the in-sandbox `prlimit` and `ffmpegthumbnailer` invocations use `/usr/bin/...` — so this reads as an inconsistency rather than a deliberate choice.

This is a defense-in-depth report, not an exploitable bug on its own: an attacker needs to already be able to write an executable into a `PATH` directory that precedes `/usr/bin`. It is worth closing anyway because `install.sh` deliberately puts `~/.local/bin` on `PATH` (`install.sh`, `local_bin_on_path`), which is exactly the kind of user-writable directory that makes this reachable, and because two of the hijackable binaries are the ones enforcing other security properties.

## Affected call sites

Security-relevant:

- `src/sandbox.rs:328` — `Command::new("bwrap")`
- `src/services/update_install.rs:614` — `Command::new("sha256sum")`
- `src/services/update_install.rs:424` — `Command::new("tar")`
- `src/ui/settings.rs:1932` — `Command::new("sh")` (post-update relaunch)

Lower impact, same pattern:

- `src/services/update_install.rs:468,479` — `gtk-update-icon-cache`, `update-desktop-database`
- `src/portal_setup.rs:279,290,307,318` — `xdg-mime`, `gdbus`
- `src/portal_setup.rs:985,1006` — `systemctl`
- `src/portal_setup/omarchy.rs:125,250` — `omarchy`, `hyprctl`

The helper invocations in `src/sandbox_helper.rs` (`ffprobe`, `dcraw`, `simple_dcraw`, `ffmpegthumbnailer`) are **not** affected: they execute inside the bubblewrap jail, where `sandbox_command` has already applied `--clearenv --setenv PATH /usr/bin`.

## Impact

- **A planted `sha256sum` makes update verification vacuous.** `verify_checksum` compares `first_hash_token(&output)` from the subprocess against the published digest, so a shim that echoes back the expected hash passes verification for any archive. This also weakens the signed-manifest work planned in #506 if the digest comparison stays in a subprocess.
- **A planted `bwrap` silently disables the preview sandbox.** `sandbox_command` builds the full argument list and `spawn_renderer` execs it; a shim can drop every isolation flag and exec the payload directly. There is no unsandboxed fallback in the code today (good), but a hijacked `bwrap` reintroduces one while the UI still reports previews as sandboxed.
- A planted `tar` or `sh` runs during the update/relaunch sequence.

## Proposed fix

Resolve these by absolute path rather than by `PATH` lookup, following the existing `PACMAN`/`PACMAN_CONF` pattern:

1. Pin the security-relevant ones to absolute paths (`/usr/bin/bwrap`, `/usr/bin/tar`, `/bin/sh`), failing closed when the binary is absent rather than falling back to a `PATH` search.
2. Replace the `sha256sum` subprocess with an in-process digest. This removes the most consequential case entirely and drops a runtime dependency; it also fits naturally into #506, where verification moves in-process anyway.
3. For the desktop-integration and portal helpers, either pin absolute paths or resolve once against a fixed allowlist of system directories.

Distribution layouts differ (`/usr/bin` vs `/bin`), so a small resolver that checks a fixed list of trusted directories — and never the inherited `PATH` — may be cleaner than hardcoding one path per call site.

## Relationship to existing issues

Distinct from #334 and #148/#506, which cover the *trust model* of the update artifact (provenance, URL allowlisting, size caps, safe extraction). #334's item 6 mentions the `tar` subprocess, but from the angle of validating archive contents rather than of which `tar` gets executed. Neither issue mentions `PATH` resolution or the `sha256sum`/`bwrap` cases.

author: guisilveira
body:
## Description

Add Undo support for successful single-item file and directory renames through Strata's existing global Undo history.

After renaming an item, Ctrl+Z now restores its exact original native name/location and follows the same latest-operation-first ordering as the other reversible file operations.

The Rename Undo path:

- preserves exact native filenames, including local non-UTF-8 names;
- never overwrites an item that now occupies the original destination;
- keeps a failed Undo available for retry;
- consumes the history entry after a successful retry;
- does not create a Redo entry while performing the inverse rename;
- keeps open-directory navigation and columns coherent when a directory rename is undone;
- restores only the original name/location, preserving the item's current contents and metadata.

The change also adds focused regression and end-to-end coverage for the Rename Undo lifecycle and updates the Ctrl+Z documentation.

## Visual evidence

Before: 
`new file -> foo.txt → test.txt → Ctrl+Z → test.txt`

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0b9cd4e1-89b9-4bdd-b733-36462b8c32cc

After:
`new file -> foo.txt → test.txt → Ctrl+Z → foo.txt -> Ctrl + Z -> new file`

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4685d8e5-ffcf-4749-8f8f-ac99719843b6

## How to test

1. Create a file named `foo.txt`, rename it to `bar.txt`, then press Ctrl+Z. Confirm that `foo.txt` is restored and `bar.txt` no longer exists.

2. Rename a directory while it is open, navigate within it, then press Ctrl+Z. Confirm that the original directory name is restored and the open navigation/columns remain coherent.

3. Rename `foo.txt` to `bar.txt`, create a new conflicting `foo.txt`, then press Ctrl+Z. Confirm that Undo fails without overwriting either item. Remove the conflicting `foo.txt` and press Ctrl+Z again. Confirm that the retry succeeds and restores the original file.

4. In a fresh Strata session with no older Undo history, complete a rename and undo it successfully, then press Ctrl+Z again. Confirm that no second rename occurs and the completed Rename Undo is not treated as Redo.

5. Perform another undoable file operation after a rename, then press Ctrl+Z twice. Confirm that the most recent operation is undone first and the rename is undone second.

6. Rename a file, modify its contents and permissions under the new name, then press Ctrl+Z. Confirm that only the name/location is restored and the current contents and permissions are preserved.

**Expected result:** Successful single-item file and directory renames participate in the global Undo history. Ctrl+Z restores the exact original name/location without overwriting conflicts or restoring stale metadata, failed Undo remains retryable, successful Undo is consumed normally, and operations retain latest-first ordering.

## Related issue

Closes #1059

issues.body:
## Problem or use case

Renaming a file or directory currently does not participate in Strata's global Undo history.

After a successful rename, pressing Ctrl+Z cannot restore the previous name/location, even though other reversible file operations such as Move, Copy, and Trash already participate in the existing latest-operation Undo flow.

This makes Rename inconsistent with the rest of Strata's reversible file operations and makes accidental renames harder to recover from.

## Proposed solution

Make successful single-item file and directory renames participate in Strata's existing global Undo history.

For example:

`foo.txt → bar.txt`

followed by Ctrl+Z should restore:

`bar.txt → foo.txt`

The behavior should follow Strata's existing Undo semantics:

- Rename participates in the same global latest-operation-first Undo history as other reversible operations.
- The exact original native filename/location is restored, including local filenames that are not valid UTF-8.
- Undo must not overwrite an item that now occupies the original destination.
- If Rename Undo fails because of a conflict or backend error, the Undo entry remains available for retry.
- A successful Rename Undo is consumed normally and does not create a Redo entry.
- Renaming an open directory and undoing it should keep navigation and open columns coherent.
- Undo restores only the original name/location. Current file contents and metadata must be preserved rather than replaced with a historical snapshot.

## Alternatives considered

- Leave Rename outside the Undo system and require users to manually rename items back. This is inconsistent with Strata's other reversible file operations.
- Add a separate Rename-only Undo mechanism. This would duplicate the existing Undo lifecycle and make ordering with Move, Copy, and Trash ambiguous.
- Add Redo or a generic command/transaction framework at the same time. That would substantially expand the scope and is not necessary for single-item Rename Undo.

## Visual examples

A short example of the expected behavior:

`foo.txt → bar.txt → Ctrl+Z → foo.txt`

PR visual evidence can show the same flow.

## Strata version

version: `0.18.0`
commit: `59aeb234010a`.
toolkit: `GTK 4.22.5`

## Additional context

This request is intentionally scoped to single-item Rename Undo.

Out of scope:

- Redo
- Batch rename
- Persistent Undo history across restarts
- Stable file-identity tracking
- New cross-window coordination infrastructure

author: Rizmi
body:
## Description

Add configurable global-search exclusions for folder names and specific directory paths. Following the owner's requested design change, the form now sits directly inside **Settings → General → Search & filtering**, with a bounded, scrollable exclusions list instead of a Manage dialog.

Rules persist and synchronize across Settings windows. Each new global-search invocation reads the current rules; pane filters and destination selection retain their explicit browsing scope. Folder names match case-insensitively; absolute paths and `~/` identify specific subtrees. Validation rejects ambiguous paths, duplicates, root, and the entire home directory.

## Visual evidence

**Updated inline-form screenshots pending owner upload.** Wide, compact, validation, and scrolled-list captures have been generated and visually inspected; authenticated attachment upload is unavailable in this session. Exact local paths are in the handoff.

Previous modal design (superseded): https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/82302016-8ea2-4f87-8a23-85f315e7005f

## How to test

1. Open Settings (`Ctrl+,`) → General → **Search & filtering**, or search Settings for “exclusions”. The input, Browse, Add, and saved list appear directly under **Global search exclusions**.
2. Enter a custom folder name such as `private-build`, then press Enter or Add. Add a directory with `~/path`, an absolute path, or Browse followed by Add.
3. Add enough rules to fill the list; scroll within it and remove a rule near the bottom. Confirm the form stays above the list.
4. Try an empty value, a duplicate, `/`, `~`, a relative path, or a path containing `..`. Confirm a visible inline validation error.
5. Open a second Settings window and verify additions/removals synchronize without erasing a draft. Close and reopen Settings to verify persistence.
6. Open global search (`Ctrl+K`) and search for a file inside the excluded subtree; it should be absent. Remove the rule and reopen global search; the file should be found again.

**Expected result:** exclusions can be edited in place without opening a separate management dialog, long lists scroll, and new global searches honor the saved rules.

## Related issue

Closes #1062

issues.body:
### Problem or use case

When using global search (Ctrl + K), search traverses local trees to index files and directories. While Strata includes built-in prunes for common tool trees (`.venv`, `node_modules`, `target`, `.cache`, etc.), users cannot currently configure custom exclusions. Users often want to exclude specific directories (e.g. large data dumps, backup folders) or specific folder names (e.g. custom build directories or virtual environment names) from indexing and search results.

### Proposed solution

1. **Configurable Search Exclusions in Settings**:
   - Under Settings → **SEARCH & FILTERING**, add an option row for **Search exclusions** with a **Manage…** button.
   - Register it in Settings search so queries like "exclude", "search", or "filter" highlight it.

2. **Dedicated In-App Modal Dialog**:
   - Open a modal dialog built with `modal_layout` (1:1 visually consistent with modals like *Copy to*).
   - Allow adding folder names (e.g. `.venv`, `build`) to exclude matching folders anywhere in the tree.
   - Allow adding specific directory paths (e.g. `~/LargeData` or `/var/log`) to exclude only that specific subtree.
   - Provide a text field, an **Add** button, and a **Browse…** button using GTK's native folder chooser.
   - Display active exclusions in a styled list with folder icons and individual remove buttons.

3. **Search Service Integration**:
   - Pass user exclusions from `ThemeManager` / `Preferences` to the search indexer.
   - Prune excluded subtrees during traversal so they consume neither memory nor time budget, and omit them from search results.

### Alternatives considered

- Storing exclusions in a plaintext file without UI: inconvenient for users and lacks discoverability.
- Inline list directly in the Settings scroll view: clutters the general settings page; a dedicated modal keeps the settings view clean and focused.

### Strata version

v0.18.0 (commit 4b7cf86)

### Additional context

Consistent with Strata's modal architecture (`ui/modal.rs`, `ui/controls.rs`) and preference lifecycle (`ThemeManager::bind_preference`).

## Description

Ctrl + mouse wheel now steps the interface text size, matching the existing Ctrl +/- keyboard shortcut. The scroll handler runs in the capture phase so scrolled windows cannot consume the event first; scrolls anywhere in the PDF scroll container, including its scrollbars, pass through to its own zoom handler. author: Rizmi
body:
## Description

Discovers local devices in file chooser dialogs by scheduling device discovery after first paint, matching the main application window's behavior.

Device discovery in `SidebarState` is intentionally deferred at launch so that windows paint on screen immediately without blocking on D-Bus/GVfs/udisks2 I/O (`// Device discovery remains deferred to the window's first-paint callback.`). However, `build_chooser()` never wired up this first-paint rebuild callback, so any local USB drives or external block devices attached and mounted prior to opening the file chooser never appeared in the chooser's sidebar.

- Added `schedule_after_first_paint` to `SidebarView`, connecting to the window's frame clock after paint (with fallback for headless environments) to run `state.rebuild()`.
- Called `sidebar.schedule_after_first_paint(&window)` in `build_chooser()`.
- Filtered non-native mounted and unmounted volumes in `append_volume()` when in `local_only` chooser mode, keeping local USB drives with native paths while excluding non-native network shares.
- Added regression test `schedule_after_first_paint_rebuilds_sidebar_places`.

## Visual evidence
https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ec51ad86-1cb7-4f14-9774-9e0084f97c72


## How to test

1. Attach and mount a local USB drive (e.g. exFAT/ext4). Confirm it is mounted at a local path such as `/run/media/$USER/$LABEL`.
2. Open a portal-based file chooser dialog (e.g., via a browser upload button or `strata --portal`).
3. Check the chooser dialog's sidebar.

Expected result: The attached drive appears under the `DEVICES` section, and clicking it navigates to its mount directory.

## Related issue

Fixes #1067

issues.body:
### Strata version

0.18.0

### Installation method

Omarchy default install (`~/.local/bin/strata`), registered as the preferred `org.freedesktop.impl.portal.FileChooser` backend via `~/.config/xdg-desktop-portal/hyprland-portals.conf`.

### Linux distribution and desktop environment

Omarchy (Arch-based), BUILD_ID 4.0.3, Hyprland 0.56.2. Portal stack: xdg-desktop-portal 1.22.1, xdg-desktop-portal-gtk 1.15.3, xdg-desktop-portal-hyprland 1.4.1, gvfs 1.60.2, udisks2 2.11.2.

### What happened?

A USB-C external drive (LaCie, exFAT) is correctly detected, mounted, and shown in Strata's main window (Devices sidebar), but the same drive does not appear in the sidebar of Strata's **portal-mode** file chooser (the `strata --portal` process that backs `org.freedesktop.impl.portal.FileChooser`), invoked e.g. from a browser's upload/download dialog.

This is not the same as #441 (which was about the drive being invisible in the main app window) or #176 (which is about *remote* GVfs locations like `smb://` needing FUSE-path resolution before they can be returned as `file://` URIs). This drive is a local block device, already udisks2-mounted at a native path, and already correctly exposed via GIO/GVfs — confirmed with `gio mount -l`, which lists it as a `GProxyVolumeMonitorUDisks2` volume/mount:

```
Drive(1): ST2000LM007-1R8174
  Volume(0): LaCie
    Type: GProxyVolume (GProxyVolumeMonitorUDisks2)
    Mount(0): LaCie -> file:///run/media/rbrouwer/LaCie
      Type: GProxyMount (GProxyVolumeMonitorUDisks2)
```

`udisksctl dump` also shows a normal, healthy mount:

```
org.freedesktop.UDisks2.Filesystem:
    MountPoints:        /run/media/rbrouwer/LaCie
IdLabel:                    LaCie
IdType:                     exfat
```

So the main Strata window and the portal picker are apparently drawing their sidebar contents from different code paths, and only the portal-mode one is missing local removable/external drives.

Ruled out:
- Not a stale-cache issue — restarting both the main Strata process and the `strata --portal` process (confirmed via fresh PIDs/start times) did not make the drive appear in the portal picker, even though it appeared immediately in the main window on relaunch.
- Not a `gvfs`/`udisks2` service problem — `gvfs-udisks2-volume-monitor.service` was active and had been running well before the drive was plugged in; `gio mount -l` and `udisksctl dump` both show the volume correctly the whole time.
- Not a sandboxing issue — the `strata --portal` process is unconfined (no `.flatpak-info`, no seccomp filters), running under the same user session bus (`DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS=unix:path=/run/user/1000/bus`) and same `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` as the main window process.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Set Strata as the system file chooser (`org.freedesktop.impl.portal.FileChooser=strata;...` in the active xdg-desktop-portal config).
2. Plug in and mount a local USB drive (exFAT, LaCie Rugged in this case, but likely filesystem-agnostic).
3. Confirm it shows correctly in Strata's own main window under Devices.
4. Open a portal-based file chooser from another app (e.g. a browser's file upload button).
5. Observe that the same drive is absent from the portal picker's sidebar/location list.

### Expected behavior

The portal-mode file chooser should show the same local Devices/removable-drive entries as Strata's main window, since the underlying GVfs/udisks2 state is identical and already correctly detected.

### Screenshots or video

None yet — happy to attach if useful, but the behavior is consistent and reproducible via the steps above.

### Relevant logs

No errors were logged by either the main Strata process or `strata --portal` at any point; the drive is simply absent from the portal picker's list with no diagnostic output.

### Additional context

Workaround in use: reordered the local FileChooser portal preference to prefer `xdg-desktop-portal-gtk` ahead of `strata` (`org.freedesktop.impl.portal.FileChooser=gtk;strata;hyprland;`), since `xdg-desktop-portal-gtk` correctly lists the same GVfs/udisks2 volume. This restores drive access in browser file pickers but loses the Strata picker UI everywhere portal choosers are used.

body: ## Description AppImage files fall back to a generic executable icon when the icon theme lacks the AppImage MIME icon (e.g. Yaru), hiding the app's real branding. This adds a `ThumbnailKind`/`ParseOperation` for `.appimage` that locates the embedded SquashFS payload from the ELF section layout and renders its icon through the existing sandboxed preview-helper path: - prefers `.DirIcon`, resolving regular files, relative symlinks, and broken absolute build-host symlinks by basename - falls back to the root `.desktop` entry's `Icon=`, matched case-insensitively against top-level `png`/`svg`/`xpm` files - bounded `unsquashfs` reads with per-read timeouts inside the sandbox wall clock; malformed or icon-less AppImages fall back to the normal file icon `squashfs-tools` (`unsquashfs`) is added as an optional dependency, matching the other preview helpers. ## Visual evidence Before: After: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6ba5c0e4-564a-4b71-b9cc-22f220d0a7ae **Pending owner upload.** Captures retained locally: - `target/appimage-icon-kamehadb.png` — the 256×256 PNG produced by the preview helper for a real AppImage (`~/bin/kamehadb.AppImage`), whose `.DirIcon` is a broken absolute symlink to a build-host path; the basename fallback recovers the real app logo - Before: the same file renders the generic `application-x-executable` icon on themes without `application-vnd.appimage` ## How to test 1. Install `squashfs-tools` and place an AppImage (e.g. `~/bin/kamehadb.AppImage`) in a browsed directory. 2. Open the directory and look at the AppImage's thumbnail. **Expected result:** the AppImage shows its embedded application icon instead of the generic executable icon. Without `squashfs-tools` installed, or for a malformed `.AppImage`, it keeps the previous generic icon. ## Related issue Closes #1076

issues.body:
### Problem or use case

AppImage files (e.g. `kamehadb.AppImage`) show a generic `application-x-executable` icon because most icon themes (Yaru, Adwaita) do not ship an `application-vnd.appimage` icon. Other file managers (Dolphin via appimage thumbnailer) display the application's real bundled icon.

### Proposed solution

Render the icon embedded inside the AppImage as the file thumbnail:

- `.appimage` files get a new thumbnail kind routed through the existing sandboxed preview-helper pipeline.
- The helper parses the ELF header to locate the appended SquashFS offset, extracts the icon with `unsquashfs` (new optional dependency alongside `ffmpegthumbnailer`/`imagemagick`), and scales it through the existing pixbuf path.
- Icon resolution order: `.DirIcon` (resolving symlinks inside the image — some builds emit absolute build-host symlinks), then the root `*.desktop` `Icon=` name matched against icon files in the image.
- Missing `unsquashfs`, type-1 (ISO) AppImages, or images without icons fall back to the theme icon as today.

### Alternatives considered

- Shipping a bundled `application-vnd.appimage` mime icon: shows an AppImage-branded icon, not the app's own logo.
- `backhand` crate for in-process SquashFS reads: avoids a runtime dep but adds a filesystem parser dependency; shelling to `unsquashfs` inside bwrap matches the existing helper style.
- `--appimage-extract`: executes the image's bundled runtime; unnecessary for icon extraction.

author: JoeJoeflyn
body:
## Description

In Columns view, opening the quick preview shrinks the horizontal viewport, so the scroll offset is pushed to keep the focused column visible. Closing padded `columns_widget`'s `margin_end` to preserve positions through the reallocation — but nothing ever released that margin. With overflowing columns, the view kept a preview-sized void at the right edge plus a phantom scrollbar range until the next navigation or mode switch.

After the viewport expands, the preserved margin is now animated back to zero; GTK re-clamps the scroll offset each frame, so columns slide into the reclaimed space instead of snapping. The release cancels if the preview reopens, the view mode changes, or another scroll animation takes over, and `reveal_column` clears any residual margin when it takes ownership. With reduced motion the release is instant.

## Visual evidence

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b083fdbf-341f-4721-8bf8-b2c1d95de4a1

## How to test

1. Switch to Columns view and navigate deep enough that columns overflow horizontally (scrollbar appears).
2. Open the quick preview (Space), then close it.
3. Expected: columns slide right into the freed space, the last column ends flush with the viewport's right edge, and the horizontal scrollbar covers only the real column content.
4. Before: a preview-width blank region remained at the right edge and the scrollbar kept the phantom range.

Regression coverage: `closing_the_preview_releases_preserved_column_scroll_space` exercises the overflowing case in both motion modes; `closing_preserves_column_positions_without_locking_horizontal_scrolling` covers the fitting case.

N/A

## Description

Render thumbnails for GVfs-backed locations through their local FUSE mirror when available, using the existing sandboxed renderer. Navigation retains its URI identity; without a mirror, files retain their generic icons. Metadata fills release thumbnails parked under the mirror path, avoiding duplicate network reads.

The URI-routing regressions use file:// fixtures; they do not exercise GVfs/FUSE integration. The author and prior reviewer separately reported live SMB/archive-mount verification in the discussion.

## Visual evidence

Author-provided sanitized captures from [the PR discussion](https://github.com/lgse/strata/pull/1080#issuecomment-5707145598):

Before:
![SMB directory before: generic icons](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ab1c9f54-420b-4188-9ca5-e43dee9c1779)

After:
![SMB directory after: image thumbnails](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b28df6a2-736d-4f42-adc9-0d0c01f745cc)

## How to test

1. Mount a GVfs network share containing images, for example with `gio mount smb://<host>/<share>`, and ensure its `gvfsd-fuse` bridge is available.
2. Open that share in Strata with the default name sort. Wait without scrolling or changing the sort.
3. Browse a backend without a local mirror to check the fallback.

issues.body:
**Summary**

Strata never generates thumbnails for files on a network share mounted via GVFS (tested with `smb://`), even though the files are readable, the directory listing works, and metadata (size/mtime) loads correctly. Thumbnails work fine for local files.

**Environment**
- Strata version: 0.18.0
- Install: Arch Linux (Omarchy), `~/.local/bin/strata`
- Backend tested: SMB share mounted via GVFS (`gvfsd-smb`), with `gvfsd-fuse` running so a real local path exists at `/run/user/$UID/gvfs/smb-share:server=...,share=...`

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Mount an SMB share via GVFS (e.g. through the Files/Network sidebar entry, or `gio mount smb://<host>/<share>`).
2. Open that share in Strata, browse to a folder containing PNG/JPEG files.
3. Observe: no thumbnails render for any image, even after waiting, scrolling, or reopening the folder.
4. For comparison, open a local folder with the same image files — thumbnails render immediately.

**Evidence**

Ran with `RUST_LOG=trace`. For a local folder, thumbnailing fires immediately per file:
```
DEBUG strata::metrics: thumbnail requested total=1
DEBUG strata::metrics: thumbnail started total=1
DEBUG strata::metrics: thumbnails eligible count=1 total=1
```

For the exact same kind of files on the `smb://` share, directory load/metadata succeed, but there is **no `thumbnail requested`/`thumbnail started`/`thumbnails eligible` log line at all** — the thumbnail pipeline is never invoked for this backend:
```
INFO strata::adapters::local_files: directory load finished request_id=1 entries=5637 elapsed_ms=687
DEBUG strata::app::browser: selection changed depth=0 selected=1
DEBUG strata::app::browser::loading::metadata: metadata fill applied request_id=5 depth=0 filled=98 stale=0
```
(zero occurrences of "thumbnail" anywhere in the trace log for the SMB session, on a share mounted at `smb://nas1.funny-name.ts.net/home/Screenshots`)

**Why this seems fixable**

This isn't a sandboxing/permissions failure — it looks like an upfront eligibility check that gates thumbnailing to the local backend before the (bwrap-sandboxed) preview renderer is ever reached. On a system where `gvfsd-fuse` is running, GVFS-backed locations like `smb://` do have a real, bind-mountable local path (`gio info` reports a `local path:` for these mounts), so the existing sandboxed renderer should in principle be able to handle them the same way it handles local files — the eligibility check just appears to exclude them categorically.

**Suggested fix**

Relax the local-only eligibility gate to also allow thumbnailing when GIO reports a resolvable local path for the file (e.g. via `g_file_get_path()` after ensuring the GVFS FUSE bridge is available), rather than excluding all non-`file://` backends outright.


🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: ogarza
body:
## Description

Replace per-file browser sandbox startup with a lazy, process-wide worker pool for Columns, List, and Icons.

- Configure **Thumbnail workers** under **Settings → General → Performance** with the same −/+ control as text size (CPU-based default capped at four; range 1–16; click the number to reset). The saved limit applies live across navigation, mode switches, and windows without interrupting busy jobs. `STRATA_THUMBNAIL_WORKERS` now seeds the default only when no count is saved.
- Retire idle supervisors after **60 seconds**, configurable with `STRATA_THUMBNAIL_IDLE_SECONDS`. The pool can shrink to zero and restart lazily. Busy jobs are never interrupted; cached/displayed thumbnails stay available. The existing launcher handles expiry without polling or another maintenance thread.
- Keep decoding disposable and isolated: codec-free supervisors fork per-file namespace-isolated children, with read-only source protections, bounded direct-result pipes, deadlines, and worker replacement. Systems without Landlock ABI 3 retain the bounded one-shot sandbox path. Preview sessions and Properties stay separate.
- Deliver dimensions discovered by fresh thumbnail decoding directly to bound entries, and publish each completed media detail promptly. Reprioritize queued metadata toward visible files in bounded batches without cancelling active fills. Permit at most one shared-pool metadata probe, with a turn after four thumbnail admissions under contention, so scrolling cannot starve captions.
- Prioritize visible items, then overscan; demote offscreen queued work and preserve stale-result/unbind guards. Reserve capacity for ordinary images alongside slower work.
- Share canonical 256-pixel RAM textures across views and separate bounded cache/render executors from GIO listing threads.
- Remove the fixed metadata/presentation/camera scheduling waits: metadata batches on idle, and UI housekeeping/camera admission follow GTK frames. Continuous scrolling does not postpone updates, and presentation refreshes no longer cancel/requeue file work.

A small paired, pinned-environment sample showed **34–36% faster thumbnail readiness**, with CPU roughly flat/slightly lower. This is not a sustained-scroll FPS or release-build benchmark. Architecture, configuration, and the narrow fork safety boundary are documented in `docs/preview-sandbox.md` and `docs/unsafe-code.md`.

### Known validation limits

Full-run results and scoped corrections are recorded in PR comments, not relabeled as new full-suite passes. The metadata follow-up exposed two rename-test synchronization races; their assertions remain unchanged and the corrected cases pass scoped reruns. A three-pair pinned debug-build sample versus `9d125a4` measured caption readiness at 417→354 ms, thumbnail readiness at 306→295 ms, and median keyboard response during scrolling at 93→95 ms. These small samples do not establish sustained-scroll FPS, tail-latency guarantees, release performance, or ARM behavior. Fill-budget and queue-capacity exhaustion remain unverified. Required checks still apply before merge.

## Visual evidence

Pending owner upload through the GitHub editor: sanitized before/after Icons captures of the synthetic mixed-media folder are retained locally. They show unchanged settled thumbnails, dimensions, durations, and selection; timing evidence is reported separately. No supported authenticated attachment-upload route is available in this session. No baseline was weakened or regenerated for the metadata changes. Sanitized before/after Performance settings captures also await owner upload; they show the new themed −/+ worker control at its default of four.

## How to test

1. Start a fresh instance in your test environment with `RUST_LOG=strata::sandbox::browser=debug strata /path/to/media` (close existing instances first). Under **Settings → General → Performance**, set **Thumbnail workers** to two.
2. Browse a folder containing images, videos, audio, and PDFs in Columns, List, and Icons. Scroll quickly, reverse direction, navigate away/back, switch modes, and open another window.
3. In Icons, select an image and verify dimensions and video durations populate without changing selection or scrolling away/back. Scroll continuously and reverse direction: visible captions should take priority over queued offscreen details. Revisit cached files and inspect the debug log for worker reuse.
4. Leave Strata open without new decoder work for over 60 seconds (or start with `STRATA_THUMBNAIL_IDLE_SECONDS=5` for a quicker check). Verify idle retirement messages, then navigate to uncached media and confirm workers are recreated.

5. Change the worker count with −/+ while browsing in two windows, including lowering it during active work. Click the number to reset; close/reopen Strata and confirm the saved count is retained. Existing text-size controls should behave as before.

**Expected result:** Names and fallback icons remain responsive; visible items receive work before offscreen items. Cached thumbnails are reused across views, optional metadata does not block cheap filesystem data, and stale results never appear on recycled rows. On the persistent path, ordinary navigation reuses at most the configured number of supervisors rather than starting a new `bwrap` per file; a failed worker may be replaced. Idle supervisors release their process memory while Strata and its thumbnail caches remain available. Worker-count changes apply across windows; lowering the limit lets busy jobs finish and retires excess idle supervisors. Originals remain unchanged.

## Related issue

Closes #516

issues.body:
### Problem or use case

Listing a photo folder is already cheap: names and fallback icons paint on the first bind. Thumbnails then lag because **every cache miss execs a new bubblewrap** (`bwrap` + `prlimit` + helper or `ffmpegthumbnailer`), and a few cheaper bugs make that worse (disk hits share the 4-wide render cap, RAM cache is keyed by icon slot size, first visit waits on GIO mtime fill, a still viewport still pays 120 ms settle, one video blocks the JPEG FIFO).

Thumbnails are decoration after first paint. They should not stall the listing or spawn a sandbox per JPEG.

### Proposed solution

Keep decoding untrusted bytes in bwrap. Stop paying process startup per file: a small **process-wide pool of long-lived sandboxed helpers**. The parent opens the file, passes the fd, reads a thumbnail back, and reuses the helper.

**Today**

```text
bind row → fallback icon
        → (settle / wait for mtime)
        → spawn_blocking: XDG lookup + maybe render
        → one-shot bwrap+prlimit+helper per miss
        → PNG → main thread decode → gtk::Image
        → persist 256 px into thumbnails/large
```

Helpers die after one job. Disk lookup and render share the same 4 slots. List/icons/columns each miss the RAM cache for the same file. Preview (`sandbox::parse`) is the same one-shot path.

**Target**

```text
bind row → fallback icon (or RAM texture hit)
        → disk lookup off the render cap
        → miss: check out an idle helper (spawn one if the pool is empty)
        → send fd over a socket → PNG/pixels back → apply
        → check helper in
```

Pool is lazy (empty until the first real render miss), process-wide (survives folder/view/window changes), and not shared with Space preview. Unbind/navigate drops the result; it does not kill the helper. Listing and `gio::spawn_blocking` stay ahead of thumbnail work.

Exact queue split, protocol, worker count, and whether the RAM cache stores PNG vs `gdk::Texture` can move during implementation. The architecture above is the thing we are aiming at.

### Alternatives considered

- **In-process decode for “trusted” local files** — no. Codecs stay in bwrap.
- **Tumbler / `org.freedesktop.thumbnails`** — extra daemon, weaker integration, does not fix our queue/cache issues.
- **Keep one-shot bwrap, only tune settle/cache** — those wins are real but miss-path cost is still exec-per-file.

### Visual examples

N/A — performance, not a UI redesign. Settings for worker count only if we add a control later.

### Strata version

0.11.2

### Additional context

Invariants we are not dropping: Freedesktop `large` (256 px) disk cache, viewport gating, unbind cancel, negative cache, `valid_output` before `gtk::Image`, no thumbs on recycled rows after navigate.

Space preview stays on one-shot `sandbox::parse` (different size limits, optional GPU, 30 s budget).

author: guisilveira
body:
## Description

Adds a **Recent** destination to the sidebar, backed by the desktop's existing GTK/GIO recent-file history.

Recent behaves as a virtual collection while keeping each displayed entry backed by its real target file. This allows normal file actions to continue operating on the underlying files without treating `recent:///` as a writable directory.

This PR:

- adds Recent as a built-in sidebar destination when supported by the platform;
- resolves Recent entries to their real local or remote targets;
- sorts Recent by last-used time by default, without changing normal folder sort preferences;
- keeps normal item actions such as Open, Open With, Preview, Rename, Move, Trash, Delete, Properties, and Open File Location working on the real target;
- prevents directory-level operations such as New File, New Folder, Paste, and drop-into from targeting the Recent collection itself;
- records successfully opened files through GTK's existing recent-file infrastructure;
- monitors platform Recent history changes and refreshes the collection when it changes;
- adds a preference to show or hide Recent in the sidebar.

The implementation relies on the platform's existing Recent infrastructure rather than maintaining a separate Strata-specific history.

## Visual evidence

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/98e25a4c-bdcb-48a3-bcfa-553ff0e7e3e1

## How to test

1. Launch Strata on a desktop where GTK Recent files and the `recent` GIO scheme are available.
2. Confirm **Recent** appears in the left sidebar and open it.
3. Verify recently used files are shown with the most recently used entries first.
4. Open a file from Recent, then return to Recent and verify its recency is updated.
5. Use normal item actions such as Open, Open With, Properties, Open File Location, Rename, Move, Copy, Trash, or Delete and confirm they operate on the underlying file.
6. Confirm collection-level actions such as New File, New Folder, Paste, and dropping files into Recent are unavailable or rejected.
7. Change the sort order while in Recent, navigate away and back, and confirm ordinary folder sort preferences are unaffected.
8. Add or remove an entry from the platform Recent history while Recent is open and confirm the view refreshes accordingly.
9. Disable **Show Recent** in Strata's sidebar preferences and confirm the destination disappears; re-enable it and confirm it returns.

**Expected result:** Recent behaves as a live, platform-backed collection of recently used files. Entries operate on their real targets, are ordered by recent use by default, and the virtual Recent root cannot be used as a normal writable directory.

## Related issue

Closes #1082

issues.body: ## Problem or use case Finding a file that was recently opened or used can require navigating back through its original folder structure, even when the user remembers the file itself but not exactly where it is stored. This is especially useful in workflows such as file uploads, where users often want to quickly find something they were working with recently. This request originally came from a user on Discord: > Having a Recent tab in the left vertical bar would be really useful, especially for file uploads. It makes finding recently used files much easier. I think some file managers already use a similar approach. ## Proposed solution Add a **Recent** destination to the left sidebar that shows files from the desktop's existing recent-file history. It should behave as a normal Strata location for browsing and selection, while actions on its entries should operate on the actual underlying files. Recent files should be ordered by recent use by default, with the most recently used files first. The feature should use the platform's existing recent-file infrastructure rather than maintaining a separate Strata-specific history. ## Alternatives considered The current workaround is to navigate manually to the file's original directory or use search when the location is not immediately known. Search can help when the filename is known, but it does not provide the same quick workflow as a dedicated list of recently used files. ## Visual examples Other desktop file managers expose a similar **Recent** location as a built-in place in their navigation/sidebar. ## Strata version 0.18.0 ## Additional context This feature request originated from the Strata Discord community. The Recent destination should remain conceptually separate from Smart Folders or saved searches: Recent represents the desktop's existing recent-file history rather than a user-defined query.

author: spandan11106
body:
## Description

In Miller Columns, clicking empty space in a column jumped the listing back to the
selected row after the user had scrolled it out of view.

Focusing a column from its background calls `focus_active()`, and the `FocusChanged`
handler unconditionally scrolls the column to the focused row — so a click that was
only meant to focus the column dragged the viewport back to the top. This suppresses
that vertical follow-up scroll for the background-click path only, reusing the same
flag pattern already used for Page Up/Down in the other view modes. Keyboard focus,
the horizontal column reveal, selection sync and preview updates are unchanged.

## Visual evidence

Original reproduction supplied by the author:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8db6fe41-6250-481f-b26a-9d1be90632c9

Current-head before/after-click screenshots were captured during review: files
`058.txt`–`079.txt` stay visible while the gutter click clears selection. Upload
through the GitHub editor is pending; the review environment has no authenticated
attachment-upload tool.

## How to test

1. Open a folder with enough files that a column scrolls (80 works) in Columns view.
2. Click the first file so the footer reads `1 file selected`.
3. Scroll that same column until the selected row is off-screen.
4. Click empty space in that column — the left gutter, not a filename.

**Expected result:** the column stays where you scrolled it. Before this change it
snapped back to the first file at the top. Clicking empty space in a *different*
column still focuses and reveals that column as before.

issues.body:
### Strata version

0.18.0 (`70ec2d3e4e91`, lgse/strata `main`)

### Installation method

Built from source

### Linux distribution and desktop environment

Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS, GTK 4.14.5, private Xvfb (`GDK_BACKEND=x11`). Not a user desktop session.

### What happened?

In Miller Columns, selecting an item in a long folder, scrolling until that item is out of view, then clicking empty space in the same column (without choosing another row) jumps the listing back to the selected item.

The empty click can also clear the selection afterward, but the viewport has already snapped back. In a folder of 80 files the listing went from `058.txt`…`079.txt` (first item still selected off-screen) to `000.txt` at the top of the column.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open a directory with many files in Columns (enough that the selected row can be scrolled out of view).
2. Select an item near the top (for example the first file).
3. Scroll the same column until that item is no longer visible. Do not click another row.
4. Click empty space in that column — the list background / gutter, not a filename and not a new item.
5. Watch the vertical scroll position.

### Expected behavior

The column should keep the scroll position the user just moved to. An empty-space click should not reveal or jump back to the (possibly then-deselected) item.

### Screenshots or video

Private Xvfb stills from this filing:

- After select: first file selected at the top (`1 file selected`).
- After scroll: later names visible (`058.txt`…`079.txt`); footer still `1 file selected` while the selected row is off-screen.
- After empty-space click: listing is back at `000.txt`.

A GTK unit-path measurement on the same build (column background gesture, 80 files, 360px window):

```
before=1452.0 after=0.0 delta=-1452.0 selected=[0] page=308.0 upper=1760.0
```

Binary stills/recording were not uploaded to GitHub from this session.

### Relevant logs

N/A — no crash or terminal error. The jump is the vertical adjustment reset above.

### Additional context

Reproduced on `70ec2d3` with an isolated HOME and a synthetic `many/` folder of 80 files. Pointer click on the list’s left gutter (not a filename) was enough; the same jump happens when the column background gesture runs directly (`press`/`release` on the stack, 40px above the bottom).

Empty clicks that land on a row, the Paste-here hint, or the location bar do not show this jump.

**Likely code path (no patch):** empty-space release on the column stack/header runs `install_column_background_focus` (`src/ui/browser/columns.rs`), which calls `Browser::set_active_column` then `Browser::focus_active()`. `focus_active` emits `FocusChanged` (`src/app/browser.rs`). The Columns handler (`src/ui/browser/events.rs`) then calls `scroll_column_to`, which uses `scroll_collection_when_allocated` with `ListScrollFlags::FOCUS` (`src/ui/browser/collection.rs`) and snaps the list back to the selected row. `reveal_column` on that same path is horizontal and is not this jump. A later selection-clear from the grouped marquee click can run after the scroll, matching the footer going from `1 file selected` to `80 items`.

Not a duplicate of:

- Closed #520 / #523 — focusing/revealing a *column* horizontally from empty-space or header clicks.
- Closed #346 / #874 — empty-pane click should focus or reveal the next column.
- Closed #767 / #803 — `/tmp` wheel scroll / background directory changes resetting scroll.
- Closed #241 — keyboard selection should stay in view.

No pull request; filing only. Do not request a core dump.
