author: spandan11106
body:
## Description

Songs with embedded cover art now get an album-art thumbnail in the browser views, and
the audio preview no longer breaks on the format most of them use.

**Thumbnails.** `thumbnail_kind()` matched video extensions only, so audio files never
entered the thumbnail pipeline at all. The renderer behind them (`ffmpegthumbnailer`,
with an `ffmpeg` fallback) already extracts attached cover pictures, so the audio
containers FFmpeg exposes artwork from simply schedule the same job. No new dependency,
no new extraction path, no sandbox change. Ogg, Opus and WAV are deliberately excluded:
they store artwork in tags FFmpeg reports no stream for, so including them would spawn a
decoder per song that can never produce a thumbnail. Songs without art keep their generic
audio icon through the existing failure path.

**Preview fix.** While testing the above I hit a pre-existing bug: an MP3 keeps its cover
in an ID3 frame that FFmpeg discards when the input is seeked, and the decoder always
passed `-ss 0` for attached pictures. It therefore returned no frame, every backend
attempt failed, and the preview showed "Unable to play this media preview" — taking audio
playback down with it, for any MP3 that has artwork. Attached pictures are now read from
the start of the file. FLAC and M4A were unaffected, which is why this only ever showed up
on the most common music format.

## Visual evidence

**Pending — captures are ready locally and need to be attached through the GitHub editor.**

- Before: a music folder in the previous build — generic audio icons throughout, and
  "Preview unavailable" on an MP3 with cover art.
- After: the same folder — MP3, FLAC and M4A show their embedded covers at their real
  aspect ratios, artless tracks and a tag-only Ogg keep the generic icon, and the preview
  pane plays an MP3 with its artwork.

## How to test

1. Put a few songs in one folder: one MP3 with embedded cover art, one FLAC or M4A with
   art, one MP3 with no art, and one `.ogg`. `ffmpeg -i song.mp3 -i cover.jpg -map 0:a
   -map 1:v -c copy -disposition:v:0 attached_pic out.mp3` builds one with art.
2. Open that folder in the Icons view.
3. Select the MP3 with art and press <kbd>Space</kbd>, then
   <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>Alt</kbd>+<kbd>Space</kbd> to play it.

**Expected result:** songs with embedded art show that art as their thumbnail, at its own
aspect ratio; songs without art and the `.ogg` keep the generic audio icon and no error
appears. The MP3 plays and shows its artwork in the preview pane instead of failing with
"Unable to play this media preview", and switching songs leaves no artwork behind from the
previous track.

Built from source

### What happened?

Two interactions that work in the main browser window are broken or missing in the XDG portal file chooser:

- Ctrl+click focuses the item just toggled, and the preview follows it — matching the Columns-mode handler and the main browser.
- Typing a printable character with the file view focused opens the filter seeded with that character; `/` opens an empty filter; Space remains quick preview — identical to the main window's type-to-search.

## Description

Show RAW photo details in the preview panel and Properties: dimensions, camera, lens, focal length, shutter speed, ISO, and GPS latitude/longitude. All seven fields remain visible, using `N/A` when unavailable. RAW metadata rows retain their space during navigation and loading; only the values update.

Reuse sandboxed LibRaw/dcraw identification and supplement it with `kamadak-exif`: the existing utilities omit GPS, and ImageMagick's DNG/EXIF output varies by version. No pixel decoding or external geocoding is needed for metadata. Ordinary image/audio/video metadata behavior is unchanged. RAW metadata also uses the local backing file for Trash entries, including collision-suffixed names. Shutter speeds use integer reciprocals or decimal seconds, and identify-path camera de-duplication is case-insensitive.

File browsing now takes priority over the preview in narrow windows. The preview shrinks, then suspends instead of hiding Columns, Icons, or List; widening restores it automatically. This preserves the session width and selection, pauses hidden media, defers new loads, and keeps keyboard input in the browser.

## Visual evidence

Preview panel preiority lower than files/cons/column
https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/26fbd3fa-3473-4fed-b102-f00eefd5668d

Raw metadata in preview panel
https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2389e2a2-de26-4e12-ad6a-2d46580306f6


**Trash follow-up evidence: pending upload.** Cropped, sanitized before/after Preview and Properties captures are prepared locally; paths are listed in the review response.

## How to test

1. Select a local RAW image and open its preview with Space. Navigate between RAW images with the arrow keys, including files without readable metadata. The labels should remain in place while their values reset and load.
2. Open the RAW file's Properties and compare the values. Test an image without GPS or other tags, or an unreadable RAW file.
3. Inspect an ordinary image or video: its existing Properties information should remain unchanged.
4. In Columns, Icons, and List, open a preview and narrow the window until both panes no longer fit. Browsing must remain available while the preview hides. Change selection, then widen: the latest preview should return. Space while hidden disables it, so widening must not reopen it.

5. Using disposable RAW copies, check Preview and Properties in Trash, including entries whose stored names acquired a collision suffix. Their metadata should match the original file. Inspect a non-reciprocal exposure such as 0.3 seconds: it should read `0.3 s`, not `1/3.333 s`.

**Expected result:** Both RAW surfaces show identical, readable values, including in Trash; unavailable values are `N/A`, and stale details disappear when selection changes.

**Known upstream limitation:** A filtered List result can lose selection after closing Properties. The failing E2E case reproduces on unmodified main (`152299c`) as well as this branch. The owner explicitly authorized pushing merge commit `0daedce` with this failure documented; it remains unresolved, not passed or quarantined. No full-suite retry was performed. The earlier #1154 native-menu limitation is superseded by the fixes included from main.

Closes #1168

author: l0gicgate
body:
## Description

Share collection behavior across Columns, List, Icons, and browser/open/save chooser consumers without replacing their native presentations:

- Centralize pointer-selection decisions, gesture lifetime, and cancellable search sessions.
- Resolve filtered actions through the displayed model and publish coherent post-reconciliation selection snapshots.
- Use typed edit targets and shared rename leases; retain filesystem-operation coordination in the browser.
- Keep live hidden-file changes and focus restoration consistent with the displayed search selection.

Document ownership, cancellation, and intentional mode differences in `docs/architecture.md`.

## Visual evidence

N/A — internal architectural refactor, with no intended visual redesign or new interface. Existing presentation and interaction policies are preserved.

## How to test

1. In each view mode, filter a folder containing nested files with duplicate basenames. Try Ctrl/Shift selection, keyboard selection, dragging a selected group, context-menu actions, and Properties → Rename. Change or clear the query and switch view modes.
2. Rename with Enter, Tab, click-away, and Escape; change the query while editing. Repeat filtered selection/acceptance in open and save choosers, including a single-selection chooser.

**Expected result:** Actions target the displayed files at their real locations; selection and drafts survive unchanged bindings, removed/rebound editors cancel cleanly, and old searches cannot update rebuilt views. Chooser restrictions and filename/preview updates remain intact.

## Related issue

Closes #1167

issues.body:
## Problem or use case

Follow up on the view-abstraction work in #1155 (related original issue: #1154). The goal is to stop maintaining parallel implementations of the same browser behavior for **Miller Columns, List, and Icons**, including their filtered/unfiltered states and file-chooser consumers.

PR #1155 is a useful first extraction, not a completed separation of concerns. It introduces a stable shared filtered-results collection for List and Icons, with presentation-specific factories and consumer-supplied activation/selection/focus callbacks. Columns intentionally continues using its native collection. Normal List/Icons collections also retain separate interaction machinery.

As a result, changes to gestures, search lifecycle, rename, and selection notifications can still require edits in multiple places. The desired outcome is **shared behavior and lifecycle, with specialized presentation and navigation**—not one universal widget or a cosmetic reduction in file length.

This is an architectural enhancement and maintainability follow-up. The observations below come from source/test inspection of #1155 at `cbc2e01a55a4d1c767fb13c9e5d180377cd99f45`; they are not a new runtime bug report. Rebase the investigation onto the merged/current implementation before making changes.

### What #1155 already gets right—preserve these gains

- `SearchCollectionOptions` separates presentation choice and consumer policy: activation, single-click behavior, selection mode, selection notifications, and keyboard-focus ownership.
- Filtered List/Icons share result-model reconciliation, selection infrastructure, context targeting, drag-source setup, and navigation plumbing.
- Progressive results reconcile by path rather than replacing the entire collection; existing coverage checks retained objects, selection, focus, and thumbnails.
- Icon cards, thumbnails, marquee selection, context-menu infrastructure, and some rename handlers are reused rather than reimplemented.
- Browser and chooser tests increasingly exercise the same observable workflows across modes.
- Columns retains its multi-pane navigation and existing collection instead of being forced into an unsuitable single-pane widget.

### Confirmed duplication and incomplete boundaries

All source links below are pinned to the assessed PR revision; line numbers will change after extraction.

#### 1. Selection/gesture policy exists in three interaction paths

The modified-click/marquee fix in #1155 maintains parallel press/release/cancel state and selection-preservation logic in:

- [Columns row interactions](https://github.com/lgse/strata/blob/cbc2e01a55a4d1c767fb13c9e5d180377cd99f45/src/ui/browser/columns/rows.rs#L371).
- [Normal List/Icons `install_modified_selection_click`](https://github.com/lgse/strata/blob/cbc2e01a55a4d1c767fb13c9e5d180377cd99f45/src/ui/browser_modes.rs#L3730).
- [Filtered List/Icons `install_result_interactions`](https://github.com/lgse/strata/blob/cbc2e01a55a4d1c767fb13c9e5d180377cd99f45/src/ui/inline_search.rs#L739), with a separate `pointer_selection` helper.

Shared concerns include Ctrl toggling, Shift range selection, preserving an already-selected group for dragging, preventing modified clicks from activating entries, and deferring gesture claims so marquee selection can participate.

**Cost:** a single behavior fix still has several owners and can drift across modes. Not every detail is identical: hit testing, source/view position mapping, slow-click rename, chooser activation, and column navigation must remain explicit policies rather than being accidentally erased.

#### 2. Columns and single-pane results independently own search lifecycle

- [Columns search setup/polling](https://github.com/lgse/strata/blob/cbc2e01a55a4d1c767fb13c9e5d180377cd99f45/src/ui/browser/columns.rs#L813) handles query updates, search handles, generations, worker polling, stale-result rejection, and model switching.
- [Columns result reconciliation](https://github.com/lgse/strata/blob/cbc2e01a55a4d1c767fb13c9e5d180377cd99f45/src/ui/browser/columns/search.rs#L10) separately restores selection by path.
- [Single-pane `inline_search::wrap`](https://github.com/lgse/strata/blob/cbc2e01a55a4d1c767fb13c9e5d180377cd99f45/src/ui/inline_search.rs#L1205) owns another search lifecycle and result delivery loop.

Keeping separate native presentation adapters is appropriate. Duplicating query/session/cancellation ownership is not required by those presentation differences. Existing differences, including per-column versus browser preference lookup, status/coverage handling, and selection fallback, must be inventoried and intentionally preserved or explicitly changed—not normalized silently.

#### 3. The shared collection reaches into consumer internals

- [`InlineSearch::begin_rename`](https://github.com/lgse/strata/blob/cbc2e01a55a4d1c767fb13c9e5d180377cd99f45/src/ui/inline_search.rs#L485) accepts `Browser`, `ViewState`, and `browser_modes::ActiveModeRename`, and calls `browser_modes::install_mode_rename_handlers`.
- `InlineSearch::install_context_menu` accepts `ViewState` directly.
- [`ModeViews::begin_rename` and `begin_search_rename`](https://github.com/lgse/strata/blob/cbc2e01a55a4d1c767fb13c9e5d180377cd99f45/src/ui/browser_modes.rs#L729) separately locate editors and initialize rename state.
- [Columns/search rename dispatch](https://github.com/lgse/strata/blob/cbc2e01a55a4d1c767fb13c9e5d180377cd99f45/src/ui/browser/inline_edit.rs#L1027) remains another presentation-specific route.

**Cost:** `browser_modes` constructs `InlineSearch`, while `InlineSearch` depends on rename machinery owned by `browser_modes`. The callback boundary is therefore incomplete. Shared code knows too much about its consumers, and rename lifecycle fixes can still need multiple implementations.

#### 4. Result data and ordering have multiple representations

The new collection maintains `State.items`, result objects in a `gio::ListStore`, a `SortListModel`, and a path-to-position map. Some operations resolve entries through the sorted model; others index `State.items`.

- [`ResultCollection::update`](https://github.com/lgse/strata/blob/cbc2e01a55a4d1c767fb13c9e5d180377cd99f45/src/ui/inline_search.rs#L206).
- [`State::selected_entries` and selection callbacks](https://github.com/lgse/strata/blob/cbc2e01a55a4d1c767fb13c9e5d180377cd99f45/src/ui/inline_search.rs#L351).
- [`update_results`](https://github.com/lgse/strata/blob/cbc2e01a55a4d1c767fb13c9e5d180377cd99f45/src/ui/inline_search.rs#L1420) replaces `State.items` before GTK-model reconciliation.

GTK model/selection notifications can be synchronous. This creates a **risk to investigate**: a selection callback may resolve a position against the new item vector while the model is only partially reconciled. This issue does **not** claim that an incorrect chooser callback was reproduced.

Existing selection-event coverage counts notifications and verifies selection mode; it does not establish that every callback payload remains consistent throughout insertion/removal/reordering. Final-state selection assertions alone do not cover the intermediate notification contract.

#### 5. Responsibilities and widget structure remain entangled

At the assessed revision, `inline_search.rs` is approximately 1,441 lines and `browser_modes.rs` approximately 4,917 lines. Size alone is not the problem: search orchestration, reconciliation, gesture state, rendering, thumbnails, rename, menus, and keyboard navigation have overlapping ownership.

`row_parts`, `rename_widgets`, and normal-mode rename discovery rely on sibling traversal and/or CSS classes to recover operational widgets. That makes presentation structure an implicit behavioral API.

**Cost:** a presentation edit can affect rename or targeting without changing an explicit contract. Simply splitting the same coupled functions into smaller files would not solve this.

## Proposed solution

### Target boundaries

The following are responsibility boundaries, not prescribed type names or a requirement to introduce a trait for each box.

| Owner | Owns | Must not own |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Search session | Query/root/scope inputs, worker handle, generations, cancellation, event draining, stale-result rejection, coverage/status output | GTK row construction, browser/chooser acceptance, column navigation |
| Collection model/update boundary | Stable entry identity, ordered lookup, reconciliation, selection/focus restoration, coherent post-update notifications | File opening, chooser completion, filesystem rename execution |
| Interaction policy/controller | Selection transitions, range anchors, drag-group preservation, activation suppression, gesture cancellation/claim lifecycle | Icon geometry, column traversal, MIME-specific actions |
| Presentation adapters | Row/card construction and binding, hit testing, reveal/scroll hooks, typed edit targets, mode-specific navigation | Duplicate generic selection/search/rename state machines |
| Rename controller | Edit session lifecycle, validation/submission coordination, commit/cancel/error handling, cleanup/focus restoration | Discovering fields through consumer-private widget trees |
| Browser/chooser adapters | Activation policy, acceptance, filename/preview updates, preferences, command/context-menu integration | Copying the generic collection implementation |

### Required design properties

1. **One owner for shared selection decisions.** Prefer a small, testable transition function/controller plus thin GTK adapters. Define how pointer, keyboard, marquee, drag, and cancellation interact; do not merely extract the same long parameter list into a utility.
2. **One owner for search-session lifecycle.** Both Columns and single-pane collections consume results. Keep the existing search service where appropriate; do not rewrite indexing as part of this task.
3. **One authoritative entry lookup per collection.** A model may still need an ordering index or cache, but all entry resolution must use a documented consistent identity/mapping contract. Avoid parallel unsynchronized position-based lookups.
4. **Transactional result publication.** Reconcile model, selection, and focus under an update boundary, then publish coherent consumer notifications. Document how no-op updates and reentrant callbacks are handled; do not mandate arbitrary notification counts without a behavioral reason.
5. **Typed edit targets.** Presentations provide the entry identity, editor/display handles, and any necessary reveal/focus hooks. Shared rename code manages the lifecycle. Use small concrete structs/enums where they are clearer than traits.
6. **One-way dependencies.** Generic collection/interaction code must not depend back on `browser_modes` rename internals or a concrete browser `ViewState`. Consumer adapters may still depend on shared browser services where appropriate.
7. **Explicit resource ownership.** Document ownership/cancellation of handlers, timeout/tick callbacks, search receivers, thumbnail requests, deferred focus/scroll work, and active edits when views are rebound, rebuilt, switched, or destroyed. Avoid introducing strong-reference cycles or callbacks into detached views.
8. **Preserve mode-specific behavior.** Miller depth/navigation, List metadata/grouping, Icon presentation, nonlocal fallback, source/view mapping, chooser restrictions, and live preferences remain explicit capabilities/policies.

### Implementation sequence

Keep this as one scoped follow-up issue. The phases below are ordering guidance, not automatic authorization for stacked or separate PRs.

- [ ] **A. Inventory behavior and ownership at current HEAD.** Map filtered/unfiltered Columns/List/Icons and browser/open/save chooser routes. Identify intentional differences, existing tests, overlapping work, and exact selected scope before extracting.
- [ ] **B. Consolidate selection/gesture policy.** Migrate all three current interaction paths to the shared policy while retaining their hit testing, navigation, and source-position adapters. Remove superseded implementations rather than keeping a second fallback indefinitely.
- [ ] **C. Extract search-session ownership.** Migrate both Columns and single-pane result consumers without replacing Columns' native collection. Preserve preference source, cancellation, stale-event handling, and status semantics.
- [ ] **D. Establish coherent model/notification ownership.** Characterize intermediate callback payloads during insertion/removal/reordering; consolidate entry lookup and make reconciliation transactional. Fix any confirmed inconsistency with a behavioral regression.
- [ ] **E. Unify rename lifecycle and typed edit targets.** Move common lifecycle ownership out of `browser_modes`; adapt normal/filtered List/Icons and Columns. Preserve operation safety, inline edit behavior, and error/focus handling.
- [ ] **F. Finish module boundaries and cleanup.** Split by the owners above, remove obsolete helpers/re-exports, and record lasting ownership/invariants in maintained architecture documentation. Record any deliberately retained duplication and why.

Resolve prerequisites discovered in A before following this order mechanically. No big-bang rewrite is required.

### Acceptance criteria / definition of done

- [ ] A generic modified-click/range/drag-preservation policy change has one implementation owner, with mode adapters supplying only genuine differences.
- [ ] Columns and single-pane filtering share query/session/generation/cancellation ownership; neither duplicates the common polling state machine.
- [ ] Entry resolution for activation, selected entries, drag payloads, context targeting, and rename follows a consistent identity/mapping contract.
- [ ] Consumer selection callbacks cannot expose a half-reconciled collection; payload correctness is covered through result insertion, removal, and reordering.
- [ ] Rename lifecycle is shared without a dependency from the generic collection back into `browser_modes` internals. Presentation adapters expose typed edit targets.
- [ ] View rebuilds, mode changes, query restarts, and destruction do not leave active handlers/tasks/edit sessions attached to stale views.
- [ ] Browser/open/save chooser behavior, single/multiple selection, real recursive locations, and existing live preferences remain correct.
- [ ] Existing meaningful regression coverage is preserved; cross-mode cases are extended at their existing owners, not replaced with a generic launch smoke test.
- [ ] Old parallel implementations are removed where superseded. Any retained duplication is explicitly justified by behavior, not convenience.
- [ ] Handoff documents the resulting ownership map, actual validation, remaining risks, and explicit deferrals. File count, line count, and a particular code-health score are not closure criteria.

### Regression coverage and validation plan

**Start with existing coverage owners:**

- `src/ui/inline_search/tests.rs`: result identity, selection mode/events, inline edit initiation, focus/thumbnail retention.
- `src/ui/browser/collection/tests.rs`: source/view mapping, query behavior, recursive activation, deferred collection work.
- `src/ui/browser/tests/recursive_search.rs`, `search_result_mutations.rs`, `filter_scope.rs`, and `view_mode_filter.rs`: browser integration, mutations, live filter scope, mode switching.
- `src/ui/browser_modes/tests/` and `src/ui/browser_modes/events/`: existing alternate-mode behavior and lifecycle coverage.
- Existing inline-rename and context-menu test owners under `src/ui/browser/`.
- `src/ui/chooser/tests/acceptance.rs`, `filename.rs`, and `filtered_preview.rs`: chooser selection, acceptance, save filename, and preview behavior.
- `tests/e2e/scenarios/test_filter_results.py`, `test_selection.py`, `test_drag_and_drop.py`, `test_inline_renaming.py`, `test_quick_preview.py`, and `test_search_filter_sort.py`: actual input routes and filesystem effects.

**Extend behavior coverage where missing:**

1. Plain/Ctrl/Shift pointer selection, keyboard range selection, select-all, and marquee; preserve a selected group during drag and modified gestures. Cover cancellation and release, not just press.
2. Single-selection chooser restrictions versus multi-selection consumers; activation must use the displayed result rather than stale hidden directory selection.
3. Progressive insert/remove/reorder with duplicate basenames in different directories. Verify entry identity, selection, focus, thumbnail retention, and **consumer callback payloads**, not only final widget state.
4. Remove the selected/focused result; define and preserve intentional fallback behavior per consumer. Empty results and clearing the query must not expose hidden stale selections.
5. Query restart, scope/hidden-file preference changes, stale worker events, mode switch, view rebuild, and destruction. Verify stale sessions cannot update the current collection.
6. Rename commit/cancel/failure and Properties → Rename in normal/filtered presentations. Investigate updates arriving during an active edit and row rebinding; preserve the edit or intentionally cancel it with cleanup rather than accidentally hiding the editor. This is a coverage requirement, not a claim of a reproduced bug.
7. Context menus, clipboard, drag, delete, Quick Preview, and Open file location continue targeting real recursive result locations.
8. Relevant live preference behavior before Settings opens, across two windows, and after view rebuilds. Distinguish pointer/keyboard/lifecycle routes when they exercise different behavior.

Do not add layout, geometry, child-count, CSS-text, or setter-echo assertions. Presentation preservation can be checked manually with isolated screenshots; keep one-off captures outside the source tree. Do not add irrelevant Cartesian-product test axes or collapse distinct input/lifecycle regressions merely to reduce test count.

**Validation execution:** follow current `AGENTS.md` and `docs/e2e-testing.md`. This issue spans cross-cutting behavior, so an implementation covering the full scope warrants the pinned full Rust/E2E gate; state the escalation rationale before running it. Use scoped tests during development and to isolate failures, and do not repeatedly rerun full suites to diagnose one case.

Illustrative scoped commands (recheck names/collection after extraction and require nonzero selected counts):

```sh
./scripts/test-headless.py ui::inline_search::tests
./scripts/test-headless.py ui::browser::collection::tests
./scripts/test-headless.py ui::chooser::tests
STRATA_CONTAINER_ENGINE=podman ./scripts/e2e.sh tests/e2e/scenarios/test_filter_results.py
```

For full cross-cutting completion, use the repository's pinned quality phases and canonical E2E runner, preserving image provenance/caches:

```sh
./scripts/quality.sh test
STRATA_CONTAINER_ENGINE=podman ./scripts/e2e.sh
# Final pre-push checkpoint, not after each implementation edit:
./scripts/quality.sh fmt
./scripts/quality.sh clippy
```

All GUI checks require private Xvfb/private D-Bus with inherited desktop/session state cleared. Canonical E2E needs its isolated AT-SPI bus. Do not substitute host GUI debugging for the pinned E2E gate or silently skip GTK tests. Record exact commands, selected counts, outcomes, and any owner-approved omissions; required CI remains authoritative.

## Alternatives considered

- **Leave the current extraction as the final architecture:** lower immediate work, but repeated gesture/search/rename maintenance remains. #1155 is a foundation, not completion of the broader objective.
- **One giant view trait or universal widget:** risks hiding legitimate Miller/navigation and presentation differences behind flags and callbacks. Prefer focused capabilities and concrete adapters.
- **Only split large source files:** improves navigation but does not establish ownership or remove parallel behavior. File splitting should follow the responsibility boundaries.
- **Copy the new `ResultCollection` into Columns:** recreates the duplication and may disrupt existing column behavior. Share lifecycle/policy instead.
- **Unify all rendering, model types, and indexing in one rewrite:** unnecessarily broad. Keep specialized rendering and the existing search service; migrate shared behavior incrementally.

## Visual examples

N/A — internal architectural follow-up with no intended visual redesign. Preserve the existing Columns/List/Icons presentation and the behavior repaired in #1155. Any deliberate user-visible changes discovered during implementation require their own explicit scope and visual evidence under repository rules.

## Strata version

Source assessment: PR #1155, commit `cbc2e01a55a4d1c767fb13c9e5d180377cd99f45`. This is not an installed-version crash/defect report.

## Additional context

- Follow-up to #1155 / #1154; do not treat this issue as a requirement to expand or block the originating PR without an explicit decision.
- Related quality umbrella: #763, especially renderer units 8–10, browser-facade unit 14, and rename units 21–22. This issue provides a concrete behavior/ownership scope for part of that debt; it does not reopen completed units or claim to resolve the entire umbrella. Coordinate with any active overlapping work.
- Out of scope: Arch/GHCR/image publication changes, new GTK compatibility patches, unrelated native-menu rewrites, new browser features, visual redesign, search-index algorithm replacement, remote-search feature expansion, CodeScene setup, or chasing metric targets.
- Inspection only: no tests were executed and no product changes were made as part of preparing this issue. Architectural risks above are explicitly separated from reproduced failures.

body:
## Description

Two Columns-mode gaps versus Finder, plus a placeholder inconsistency:

- **Filter placeholders** (`fix` commit): Columns already rendered `Filter N items…` while List and Icons kept a static `Filter items…`. The count formatter is now shared and refreshed from `show_count`, so all three modes show the live count.
- **Selection mirror** (`feat` commit): Up/Down in Columns now mirrors the selection in the next pane — a folder shows its contents without moving focus, a previewable file opens Quick Preview (gated by `single_click_previews`), and any other file closes the child pane. The mirror is debounced at the same 75 ms as `FOCUS_PREVIEW_DELAY` so rapid arrow presses only load the landing item, and it re-verifies focus at fire time so a stale selection or an explicit close cannot act or reopen. Pointer selection keeps the configured click behavior; inline rename and pending new-entry flows are guarded; unreadable folders surface their inline column error instead of a dialog.

## Visual evidence

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f1794838-816e-4efb-abb3-32c510f540c0

## How to test

1. Columns mode: arrow Up/Down onto a folder — the next pane shows its contents while focus stays in the current pane; onto a `.txt`/image/PDF — Quick Preview opens and the child pane closes; onto an unsupported file — the child pane closes.
2. Hold Down through a mixed list — only the landing folder loads (no per-keystroke lag).
3. Right on a folder enters the already-open child pane; Escape clears selection, then closes the pane — and it stays closed.
4. Ctrl+F in Icons, List, and Columns — all show `Filter N items…` with the live count, updating as entries appear.

**Expected result:** the next column always reflects the keyboard selection, like Finder's column view; placeholders are identical across modes.

## Related issue

Closes #1178

issues.body:
## Problem or use case

In Columns mode, arrow-key selection does not update the pane to the right: pressing Up/Down onto a folder leaves the previous folder's column open (stale contents), and landing on a file leaves the folder column open. Finder's column view always mirrors the current selection in the next column — folder selection shows its contents, file selection shows a preview — so keyboard-only browsing requires an extra Right/Enter press per folder and can display misleading contents.

Separately, the per-pane filter placeholder is inconsistent: Columns shows a live count (`Filter N items…`) while List and Icons show a static `Filter items…`.

## Proposed solution

- In Columns mode, debounced keyboard selection mirroring: landing on a folder shows its contents in the next pane without moving focus; landing on a previewable file opens Quick Preview; landing on any other file closes the child pane. Pointer (mouse) selection keeps the configured click behavior. An explicit column close must not be reopened by the mirror, and the mirror must stay quiet for unreadable folders (inline error state, no dialog).
- Share the `Filter N items…` placeholder across all three view modes so List and Icons show the live item count too.

## Alternatives considered

- Right-arrow/Enter to enter folders works today but is slower than Finder's live mirror for keyboard navigation.
- Removing the count from Columns would unify placeholders the other way, but the count is useful when several panes with different counts are visible.

## Additional context

Finder behavior reference: in column view the right-hand column always reflects the current selection (folder → contents, file → preview column). Synchronous per-keystroke loading would be wasteful for rapid arrow presses, so the mirror should be debounced to the same 75 ms cadence already used for preview-follows-focus.

comments.body:
Implemented in #1188 (`714facee`), based on main `c43f1eed` including the separate lifecycle fix #1187. Only four production files changed; existing tests, fixtures, dependencies, and harnesses remain unchanged.

### Changes

- Cache directory counts; invalidate them on structural changes and key them by hidden-file visibility.
- Route full-sort metadata chunks through a temporary location index instead of scanning every entry per chunk. Release the index on sort completion/abandonment; preserve duplicate-location behavior.
- Replace quadratic selection retention with one directory pass and moved keys.
- Apply GTK selections atomically and update partial identity-map splices without recreating every object reference. Preserve repeated-object semantics.

Useful lazy row models and bounded thumbnail/preview/MIME/document caches are retained. Unicode comparison allocations, eager recursive-search metadata, and icon-cache history were investigated but are outside this bounded patch.

Shared navigation/collection impact justified the full pinned suites:

- `STRATA_CONTAINER_ENGINE=podman ./scripts/quality.sh test`: **2,299 passed, 20 existing ignores**.
- `STRATA_CONTAINER_ENGINE=podman ./scripts/e2e.sh`: **791 passed**.

- `STRATA_CONTAINER_ENGINE=podman ./scripts/e2e.sh tests/e2e/scenarios/test_monitor_selection.py tests/e2e/scenarios/test_selection.py tests/e2e/scenarios/test_view_switching.py tests/e2e/scenarios/test_search_filter_sort.py`: **97 passed**.
- `python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts -p 'test_*.py'` with inherited GUI/session-bus variables cleared: **206 passed**.
- Final pinned `./scripts/quality.sh fmt`, `./scripts/quality.sh clippy`, and `git diff --check`: passed.

Rootless Podman used session-owned state and private Xvfb/D-Bus. Pinned image `c3eeda033623f5f9426d1ab7167adb4e1c8a08d222dd68b590e9d33680e5fbb7`, Rust 1.98.1, GTK 4.22.5. Existing ignored manual/optional tests were not forced on. GitHub checks remain authoritative before merge.

A fresh-context read-only review found no evidence-backed P1/P2 regressions. Additional scratch-only probes checked duplicate metadata locations over multiple chunks and structural invalidation, repeated GTK identities across splices, and restored cached-pane rows/selection. No probe or evidence files were committed.

### Performance evidence

Medians of three final samples; synthetic in-memory fixtures on a Ryzen 9 9950X3D, same pinned environment and baseline. Strata package compiled with `profile.dev.package.strata.opt-level=3`; dependencies retained their test-profile settings. These measure isolated operations, **not whole-application latency, enumeration throughput, or RSS**.

| Operation | Main | Optimized |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 1,000 count reads, 100k entries, including first fill | 64.8 ms | 0.264 ms |
| 256 metadata chunks of 8, 100k entries, including index creation | 708 ms | 11.5 ms |
| Hide hidden files, 20k selected entries | 7,085 ms | 2.48 ms |
| Monitor removal, 18k selected entries | 5,735 ms | 3.11 ms |
| 32 middle-row replacements, 100k-item identity map | 143 ms | 11.4 ms |

author: JoeJoeflyn
body:
## Description

Sanitize parent-directory components at the shared archive extraction boundary instead of aborting on the first `..` member. ZIP no longer rejects those names before shared handling, while descriptor-relative writes, symlink refusal, absolute-path rejection, and conflict renaming remain intact.

## Why

Archive member paths are untrusted metadata. Naively joining a destination with `../escaped.txt` would resolve beside the selected folder; previously Strata prevented that escape by aborting the whole operation. The shared sanitizer now maps the member to `escaped.txt` inside the destination and continues extracting later members, while the descriptor-relative writer remains the final confinement boundary.

## Visual evidence

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/19f428c2-7c5c-4e64-b9e4-471531f23aad

## How to test

1. Create a ZIP containing `../escaped.txt` followed by `after.txt`.
2. Extract it into an empty directory with Strata.

**Expected result:** Both files are extracted inside the selected directory as `escaped.txt` and `after.txt`; no error popup appears and nothing is written beside the destination.

## Related issue

Closes #1189

issues.body:
### Strata version

Source build at commit `c43f1eed`.

### Installation method

Built from source.

### Linux distribution and desktop environment

Arch Linux, Hyprland/Wayland.

### What happened?

Extracting an otherwise valid archive aborts on the first member whose name contains a `..` component, and the UI shows an error popup. Safe members after that entry are never extracted. The current confinement is secure, but unnecessarily turns one parent-traversal name into a failure for the entire archive.

Finder-style archive extraction sanitizes unsafe member names and continues extracting all members within the selected destination.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create an archive with members `before.txt`, `../escaped.txt`, and `after.txt`.
2. Extract it with Strata.
3. Observe that `before.txt` may be extracted, extraction aborts at `../escaped.txt`, and `after.txt` is not extracted.

### Expected behavior

Resolve parent components without walking above the extraction root, extract the sanitized member within the selected destination, and continue through the archive. For example, `../escaped.txt` should extract as `escaped.txt`. Empty and absolute paths and Windows drive prefixes should remain invalid. Existing descriptor-relative confinement and conflict renaming must remain intact, and no file may be written outside the destination.

### Screenshots or video

N/A — filesystem assertions can demonstrate this non-visual behavior.

### Relevant logs

N/A.

### Additional context

`validated_archive_path` currently rejects parent components and `ExtractionSession::extract_member` propagates that error, stopping every decoder at the first such member. Add shared regression coverage so ZIP, TAR/TAR.GZ, 7z, and RAR all inherit the same parent-component sanitization policy through `ExtractionSession`.

author: wmfeht
body: ## Description Removable Unmount, Eject, and the unmount half of encrypted Lock flush the local mount with `syncfs` on a worker, then run the existing GIO call. The browser leaves that volume before the flush so directory monitors are dropped, and returns only if the release fails while the volume is still mounted. The drive stays in the sidebar, with a progress spinner, until the operation finishes. Hide, Close, and Escape dismiss only the overlay. Success says the drive can be unplugged only when it is removable or ejectable. A copy onto removable media shows “Writing to device…” and does not report success until `syncfs` returns. A cross-volume move, replace, merge, or undo syncs that filesystem after the copy and before the source is deleted. If the flush fails, the source stays in place. Cancelling or failing after bytes were written still flushes those roots, and a cancel does not report the transfer as finished. ## Visual evidence Large copy and move operations to devices such as USB sticks now show real progress bars instead of hiding progress after the data is accepted but a write is still underway: While writes are still finalizing, a modal displays the status correctly: If a write is pending to the drive not initiated by Strata and the device is ejected, a popup notifies the user: If dismissed, the device persists in the side bar with a spinner until operations are finalized: ## How to test 1. Mount a removable drive, copy a file onto it, and choose Unmount or Eject. 2. While the overlay is up, choose Hide and keep using the window. The drive row should keep spinning and should stay listed until the operation finishes. 3. If the overlay is still open when unmount or eject of a removable drive succeeds, it should retitle to “Safe to remove”. Lock, and unmount of a non-removable volume, should not use that title. 4. Copy a file onto the removable drive and watch the copy dialog. It should show “Writing to device…” before the copy is reported done. 5. Move a file from an internal disk onto the removable drive. The original should remain until the writing phase finishes, and should stay if that flush fails. **Expected result:** The drive is not dropped from the sidebar while writes are still flushing, Hide does not cancel the operation, a removable copy or move is not reported successful before `syncfs` returns, and a failed flush does not delete the only remaining copy. ## Related issue Closes #1182

issues.body:
### Strata version

0.19.0

### Installation method

Other

### Linux distribution and desktop environment

Omarchy 4.0.4 (Arch Linux), Hyprland 0.56.2, kernel 7.2.5. Package `strata 0.19.0-2` from the Omarchy repo.

### What happened?

I copied a ~310 MB folder to a USB 2.0 stick (NTFS, mounted by udisks with ntfs3). The copy dialog sat at 99 % for a while and then closed without any error. I clicked unmount in the sidebar, the device went away, and I pulled the stick.

The folder was not on the stick. I only found out at work. The volume was also left dirty, so ntfs3 refused to mount it until I ran `ntfsfix -d`.

Two things add up here:

1. The copy is reported as finished while the data is still in the page cache. I could not find an `fsync`/`syncfs` in the copy path. On a slow stick that is a minute or more of pending writes.
2. Unmount gives no sign that it is still flushing. The mount disappeared from the system 8 seconds before I unplugged, but udisks had not completed the unmount yet (it never logged the cleanup for that device until the USB disconnect). Nothing in the UI told me to wait.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Plug in a slow USB stick (USB 2.0 makes it obvious).
2. Copy a few hundred MB to it and wait for the dialog to close.
3. Unmount from the sidebar and remove the stick as soon as the device disappears.
4. Plug it back in: the copied folder is missing or incomplete, and an NTFS volume is marked dirty.

`grep -E 'Dirty|Writeback' /proc/meminfo` right after the dialog closes shows how much is still unwritten.

### Expected behavior

- The copy should not report success until the data is on the device, at least for removable destinations (`syncfs` on the destination before finishing, and let the progress dialog show that phase).
- While an unmount/eject is pending, keep the device in the sidebar with a "writing data, do not unplug" state until `unmount_with_operation` resolves, and then say it is safe to remove. GNOME Files does both.

### Screenshots or video

_No response_

### Relevant logs

```shell
17:02:59 systemd[1]: run-media-kike-OMARCHY_202609.mount: Deactivated successfully.
17:03:07 kernel: usb 3-4: USB disconnect, device number 8
17:03:07 kernel: device offline error, dev sda, sector 13143272 op 0x1:(WRITE) flags 0x4000 phys_seg 30 prio class 2
17:03:07 kernel: Buffer I/O error on dev sda1, logical block 786433, lost async page write
17:03:07 kernel: sda1: writeback error on inode 719, offset 0, sector 13140504
17:03:07 kernel: ntfs3(sda1): failed to read volume at offset 0x191143000
17:03:07 udisksd[2260]: Cleaning up mount point /run/media/kike/OMARCHY_202609 (device 8:1 no longer exists)
...
21:39:00 kernel: ntfs3(sda1): volume is dirty and "force" flag is not set!
```

A second stick (FAT, nothing written to it) unmounted at the same moment got its udisks cleanup line 2 seconds later, as expected.

### Additional context

Related to #1123 only in that both are copies to removable media that fail without the user noticing. Different cause.

## What and why
The Icons/List file-chooser swallowed single-click folder activation when folder clicks are set to single-click: the press was claimed with no action, so neither single- nor double-click descended into folders (keyboard Enter still worked). The main window and the Columns chooser already navigate on single-click per preference.

Now directories navigate per the saved click preference in the chooser too. Files still only select/preview on single click, so dialogs are never accepted accidentally, and double-click file accept is no longer blocked by the swallowed first press.

Fixes #1195.

## Reproduce / verify
1. Settings: set List (or Icons) folders to single-click.

author: l0gicgate
body:
## Description

The chooser backend previously held its D-Bus name indefinitely after the last dialog. Exit after two idle minutes, but keep active requests alive and prevent a new request from racing shutdown. In-app updates now stop and wait for older chooser/regular Strata processes from the same installation, then restart the updating window with the new executable. The updater uses pidfds to avoid signalling a reused PID and leaves helper processes and unrelated binaries alone. Manual installer and package-manager updates remain outside this in-app retirement path.

## Visual evidence

Pending: the automatic restart after an in-app update is user-visible. No authenticated release-update capture is available in this development session; owner upload of a sanitized before/after recording through the GitHub PR editor is needed before merge. No image is attached yet.

## How to test

1. Enable Strata as the system file chooser, open and close a portal-aware dialog, and watch `strata --portal` exit after two minutes; leave a chooser open longer than two minutes and confirm it remains functional.
2. Open two Strata instances plus a chooser, install an in-app update, and observe the old processes terminate and the updated Strata window relaunch automatically. Verify a separate Strata checkout remains running.

**Expected result:** No idle backend remains running; active dialogs are preserved; the update leaves no old regular or chooser instances for that installation.

## Related issue

Closes #1200

author: JoeJoeflyn
body:
## Description

Two unrelated UI fixes from one investigation session:

1. **Confirmation dialogs now focus the action button** (Closes #1204). Every confirm/cancel modal — permanently delete, empty trash, restore, replace, run action/program, forget password — previously opened with Cancel focused, so Enter cancelled instead of confirming. A shared `focus_button()` helper now drives all of them: Enter confirms, Escape cancels. Progress/loading dialogs still focus their single button.

2. **Path-completion dropdown no longer flashes** (Closes #1205). Location-editor exit paths restored the entry text while the entry was still visible; the `changed` signal re-opened the completion popover for a frame (close flash) and left it visible-but-unmapped so the next editor open re-mapped it with stale rows (open flash). The stack now switches to breadcrumbs before the text is reset.

## Visual evidence

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8010daa4-6a30-4729-b6f6-87986dda3ae3

## How to test

1. Select a file, press **Delete**, then **Enter** without touching anything else → the "Permanently delete" action confirms.
2. Open Empty Trash, a Replace/overwrite conflict, and "Forget saved password?" → the action button is focused in each; **Esc** still cancels.
3. Press **Ctrl+L**, type a path prefix so the completion dropdown appears, press **Esc**, then **Ctrl+L** again → no dropdown flash on close or reopen.

**Expected result:** Enter confirms destructive dialogs, Esc cancels; the completion dropdown never reappears stale.

issues.body:
### Strata version

commit b48e6f77 (0.19.0 dev)

### Installation method

Built from source

### Linux distribution and desktop environment

Omarchy (Arch Linux), Hyprland

### What happened?

The path-completion dropdown flashes once when the location editor closes and once when it reopens.

Every path that dismisses the editor restores the entry text **before** hiding it (`restore_location_text()` runs while the stack still shows the entry). `set_text` fires the entry's `changed` signal, which runs completion refresh while the editor is still considered active, so the popover re-opens for a frame and is then force-unmapped (the close flash). It also leaves the popover widget visible-but-unmapped, so the next time the editor opens GTK re-maps it showing stale rows for a frame before refresh rebuilds it (the open flash).

Affected paths: cancel (Esc), both `submit_location` error branches, mount-failure retry, retry-cancel, and `set_location` on navigation.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Press Ctrl+L to open the location editor and type a path prefix so the completion dropdown appears.
2. Press Esc, then Ctrl+L again and watch the dropdown region.

**Expected:** the dropdown disappears cleanly on close and only shows fresh rows on reopen.
**Actual:** a single-frame flash of the dropdown on close, and a stale-list flash on reopen.

author: guisilveira
body: ## Description Context-menu actions with different purposes reused icons and appeared together, making the menus harder to scan. Group regular-file, archive, folder, multi-selection, and folder-background actions by intent. Add dedicated Lucide icons for distinct actions; keep Compress in its own transform group, move Pin to sidebar into the organization/reference region, and group New Folder, New File, and Paste together. Permanent deletion uses CircleX and retains its danger styling. This changes menu presentation only. Existing action availability, capability checks, shortcuts, filesystem behavior, and the current archive extraction flow remain intact. ## Visual evidence Evidence pending upload through the GitHub editor. - **Regular file — before / after:** Edit, transfer, transform, reference, and destructive groups. Before: After: - **Archive — before / after:** Extract here and Extract to… retain their behavior and gain distinct icons. Before: After: - **Folder — before / after:** Pin to sidebar appears with organization/reference actions. Before: After: - **Multiple selection — before / after:** Shared actions follow the same semantic order. Before: After: - **Folder background — before / after:** Creation and Paste form the first group. Before: After: ## How to test 1. In a local folder, open the context menus for a regular file, an archive, a folder, multiple selected items, and empty folder space. Inspect action order, group boundaries, and icons. 2. Use Extract here and Extract to… on a supported archive, then check menu availability in Trash and Recent locations. **Expected result:** Actions appear in consistent semantic groups without empty separators. Permanent deletion retains its danger treatment. Extraction, conditional actions, shortcuts, and filesystem operations behave as before. ## Related issue Closes #1207

issues.body: ### Problem or use case Strata's context menus already use separators, but some actions are grouped in ways that do not clearly reflect the user's intent, and several semantically different actions reuse the same icon. On current `main`, examples include: - `Copy`, `Duplicate`, `Copy path`, `Copy name`, and `Copy to…` all using the Copy icon. - `Compress…`, `Extract here`, and `Extract to…` all using the FileArchive icon. - `Open` and `Open With…` sharing ExternalLink. - `Move to Trash` and `Permanently delete` sharing Trash, even though the latter is irreversible. - `Rename` being separated from Cut / Copy / Duplicate and grouped with Compress. - `Copy path` / `Copy name` sitting beside file-copy operations even though they copy textual information about the item rather than the item itself. - `Pin to sidebar` sitting inside the edit/clipboard block in the folder menu. - In the background menu, `Paste` is separated from `New Folder` / `New File` even though all three add content to the current directory. This makes the menus harder to scan than necessary. Icons should work as secondary visual landmarks. The text label remains the primary source of meaning, but when several adjacent actions share the same silhouette the icon contributes little additional information to visual scanning. The ordering has a similar effect. Stable semantic regions let users learn approximately where an action will be located even when the available actions differ between a regular file, archive, folder, multiple selection, or folder background. The goal is not to make every icon arbitrarily unique. Related operations should still look related, while semantically different operations should have distinguishable silhouettes and appear in predictable groups. ### Proposed solution Keep the current compact separator-based menus without adding visible section headings, but reorganize actions around a consistent internal model: `Open / View → Edit → Transfer → Transform → Organize / Reference / Inspect → Destructive` The categories above describe the information architecture and do not need to appear as visible labels in the UI. The same relative ordering should be preserved across contexts wherever possible so users can build spatial memory. The proposal below was also reviewed at Strata's 13 px menu-icon size. The icon choices listed here are the intended mappings rather than open alternatives. #### Regular file ```text Open Open With… Quick preview Open file location Print ──────── Cut Copy Duplicate Rename ──────── Move to… Copy to… ──────── Compress… ──────── Customize… Copy path Copy name Properties ──────── Move to Trash Permanently delete ``` `Open` and `Open With…` remain adjacent because the latter is a direct variation of the former. `Quick preview` follows them as another way of consuming the file without breaking that relationship. `Rename` moves into the direct-edit region with Cut / Copy / Duplicate rather than remaining grouped with Compress. `Copy path` and `Copy name` move away from filesystem-copy operations because they copy textual information about the selected item rather than the item itself. #### Archive ```text Open Open With… Open file location Extract here Extract to… ──────── Cut Copy Duplicate Rename ──────── Move to… Copy to… ──────── Compress… ──────── Customize… Copy path Copy name Properties ──────── Move to Trash Permanently delete ``` The common file actions remain first: ```text Open Open With… Open file location ``` Archive-specific actions follow: ```text Extract here Extract to… ``` This preserves relative ordering with regular files while still keeping extraction near the top of the menu. #### Folder ```text Open Open With… Open in Terminal ──────── Cut Copy Duplicate Rename ──────── Move to… Copy to… ──────── Compress… ──────── Pin to sidebar Customize… Copy path Copy name Properties ──────── Move to Trash Permanently delete ``` `Pin to sidebar` moves out of the edit/clipboard region because it changes how the folder is organized in Strata rather than modifying or transferring the filesystem object. #### Multiple selection ```text Open With… ──────── Cut Copy Duplicate ──────── Move to… Copy to… ──────── Compress… ──────── Copy paths Copy names Properties ──────── Move to Trash Permanently delete ``` `Copy paths`, `Copy names`, and `Properties` share the same compact reference/inspection region. Keeping them together avoids introducing a separate single-item `Properties` section and preserves the overall menu density. #### Folder background ```text New Folder New File Paste ──────── Open With… Open in Terminal ──────── Select All Refresh Show / Hide Hidden Files ──────── Customize… Properties ``` `New Folder`, `New File`, and `Paste` are grouped together because all three add content to the current directory. `Open With…` and `Open in Terminal` remain in a folder-targeted action region. Selection/view actions follow, with folder customization and inspection at the bottom. ### Icon semantics Use more specific bundled Lucide icons where the current icon does not sufficiently distinguish the action. Final mapping: | Action | Current | Proposed | | --- | --- | --- | | Open | ExternalLink | ExternalLink | | Open With… | ExternalLink | AppWindow | | Open file location | FolderOpen | FolderOpen | | Quick preview | Eye | Eye | | Print | Printer | Printer | | Open in Terminal | Terminal | Terminal | | Extract here | FileArchive | PackageOpen | | Extract to… | FileArchive | FolderArchive | | Cut | Scissors | Scissors | | Copy | Copy | Copy | | Duplicate | Copy | CopyPlus | | Copy path / Copy paths | Copy | Route | | Copy name / Copy names | Copy | FileType | | Move to… | Folder | FolderInput | | Copy to… | Copy | FolderOutput | | Rename | Pencil | Pencil | | Compress… | FileArchive | PackagePlus | | Pin to sidebar | Pin | Pin | | Customize… | Palette | Palette | | Properties | Info | Info | | Move to Trash | Trash | Trash | | Permanently delete | Trash | CircleX | | New Folder | FolderPlus | FolderPlus | | New File | FilePlus | FilePlus | | Paste | ClipboardPaste | ClipboardPaste | | Select All | ListChecks | ListChecks | | Refresh | Refresh | Refresh | | Show / Hide Hidden Files | Eye / EyeOff | Eye / EyeOff | The intended visual vocabulary is: - `Copy` for the base filesystem copy operation. - `CopyPlus` for creating another instance of the same item. - `Route` for filesystem paths. - `FileType` for an item's textual filename. - `FolderInput` for moving to another destination. - `FolderOutput` for copying to another destination. - `PackageOpen` for extracting an archive in place. - `FolderArchive` for extracting an archive to another destination. - `PackagePlus` for creating a compressed/archive result. - `Trash` for recoverable deletion. - `CircleX` for irreversible deletion. These mappings were compared at the 13 px size used by Strata's context menus. At that size, the icons should be treated as secondary cues rather than independent replacements for their labels. The goal is perceptual differentiation during menu scanning, not requiring users to infer the operation from the glyph alone. ### Destructive actions The destructive region remains at the bottom of applicable menus: ```text Move to Trash Permanently delete ``` `Move to Trash` keeps `Trash`, representing a recoverable deletion. `Permanently delete` uses `CircleX` and retains Strata's existing red/danger treatment for both text and icon. This provides multiple signals for the irreversible operation: - explicit `Permanently delete` label; - distinct `CircleX` silhouette; - red danger styling; - stable placement in the destructive region at the bottom of the menu. The distinction therefore does not depend on color alone. ### Compress remains a standalone region `Compress…` remains separated from both Edit and Transfer actions: ```text Move to… Copy to… ──────── Compress… ──────── Customize… ``` This introduces a small singleton section, but avoids grouping transformation with unrelated operations merely to remove a separator. Putting Compress beside Rename would recreate the current semantic mismatch, while placing it beside Move / Copy to would mix transformation with destination-based transfer operations. The extra separator is therefore intentional. ### Behavior and scope This should remain a presentation and information-architecture change. It should not change: - filesystem operation semantics; - keyboard accelerators; - visibility rules; - enabled/disabled conditions; - clipboard behavior; - conflict handling; - undo behavior; - destructive confirmation behavior; - selection behavior. Equivalent actions in single-selection and multi-selection menus should use the same icon vocabulary. Context-dependent actions may appear or disappear, but the relative position of shared operations should remain stable wherever practical. ### Why no visible section headings? Visible headings such as: ```text EDIT TRANSFER TRANSFORM INSPECT ``` would make the categorization explicit, but they would also increase the vertical size of menus that are already relatively long. The proposal instead communicates structure through: - semantic ordering; - proximity; - separators; - consistent relative placement; - differentiated icon silhouettes; - explicit text labels. The internal categories are therefore an information-architecture model rather than additional visible UI. ### Design rationale The proposal is intended to improve several related aspects of context-menu usability. #### Visual scanning Icons become useful landmarks instead of repeated decoration. For example, the current pattern: ```text Copy → Copy Duplicate → Copy Copy path → Copy Copy name → Copy Copy to… → Copy ``` becomes: ```text Copy → Copy Duplicate → CopyPlus Copy path → Route Copy name → FileType Copy to… → FolderOutput ``` The labels still carry the authoritative meaning, while the differing silhouettes make adjacent operations easier to distinguish during scanning. #### Semantic proximity Operations that act on the selected filesystem object are kept together: ```text Cut Copy Duplicate Rename ``` Operations that expose or copy information about the item appear later: ```text Copy path Copy name Properties ``` Transfer operations form another predictable region: ```text Move to… Copy to… ``` #### Cross-context consistency Shared actions retain similar relative positions across regular files, archives, folders, and multiple selections. For example: ```text Edit ↓ Transfer ↓ Compress ↓ Reference / Inspect ↓ Destructive ``` remains broadly stable even when context-specific actions disappear. This is preferred over independently optimizing each menu around assumed action frequency without usage data. #### Error prevention Recoverable and irreversible deletion no longer share the same silhouette. ```text Move to Trash → Trash Permanently delete → CircleX + danger styling ``` This gives the irreversible action redundant visual differentiation without relying exclusively on color. ### Alternatives considered - **Change only the icons.** This improves visual differentiation but leaves actions such as Rename, Copy path/name, Pin, and background Paste in unintuitive regions. - **Reorder the actions but keep the repeated icons.** This improves spatial predictability, but repeated icons still provide little information during visual scanning. - **Add visible headings such as Edit, Transfer, or Inspect.** The structure becomes explicit but at a significant vertical-density cost. Separators plus coherent ordering should provide sufficient grouping. - **Remove icons from context menus.** This eliminates misleading repetition but also removes useful secondary visual landmarks. - **Give every action a completely unrelated icon.** This maximizes differentiation at the cost of semantic consistency. Related actions should preserve some visual relationship. - **Use color as the main differentiator.** Color is appropriate for danger state, but shape and labels should carry the semantic distinction as well. - **Merge Compress into Edit or Transfer to reduce menu height.** This saves one separator but creates a semantically mixed group. Keeping Compress standalone is preferred. - **Give Properties its own section in multi-selection.** This creates a stricter distinction between reference and inspection but adds a single-item section and another separator. Keeping `Copy paths`, `Copy names`, and `Properties` together is more compact. ### Visual examples I will attach before/after captures for all five context-menu variants. The **Before** images show the current Strata menus. The **After** images are mockups generated from an interactive UI prototype representing the proposed ordering and iconography. The mockups were also used to compare ambiguous icon and ordering choices at Strata's 13 px menu-icon size. They are design references rather than screenshots of an implemented build. #### Regular file **Before:** **After:** #### Archive **Before:** **After:** #### Folder **Before:** **After:** #### Multiple selection **Before:** **After:** #### Folder background **Before:** **After:** ### Strata version `main` — commit `ae677e2d715daf30fc005388814cbf9bffe1bc78` ### Additional context The current mappings and ordering are defined directly in `src/ui/browser/context_menu.rs`, so the proposed work can remain focused on context-menu presentation and bundled icon assets rather than file-operation infrastructure. Strata already has the required theme-aware bundled-icon pipeline. New interface icons should continue to: - come from Lucide; - preserve Lucide geometry; - use the `strata-` namespace; - be included in the application resource bundle; - render through Strata's existing theme-aware primary/danger icon helpers. The new glyphs should be reviewed in the actual application at the standard 13 px menu size rather than judged only from enlarged Lucide previews. There is already precedent for assigning a dedicated icon to distinguish a context-menu action: #1040 uses `FolderOpen` for `Open file location`. `Send to…` may appear in some design mockups to demonstrate where that future action would naturally fit. The feature itself is already tracked separately in #1153 and is not part of this issue. If/when #1153 lands, its natural placement under this organization would be: ```text Move to… Copy to… Send to… ``` ### Acceptance criteria - [ ] Regular-file, archive, folder, multi-selection, and background menus use a consistent semantic ordering. - [ ] Existing context-specific visibility rules are preserved. - [ ] No visible group headings are added; separators remain the primary grouping mechanism. - [ ] Regular-file opening actions use the order `Open` → `Open With…` → `Quick preview` → `Open file location` → `Print`. - [ ] Archive common actions remain before archive-specific extraction actions. - [ ] `Rename` is grouped with the other direct edit actions. - [ ] `Copy path(s)` and `Copy name(s)` are separated from filesystem Copy/Duplicate operations. - [ ] `Pin to sidebar` is grouped with organization/inspection actions rather than edit actions. - [ ] Background `Paste` is grouped with `New Folder` and `New File`. - [ ] `Compress…` remains in its own section rather than being grouped with Edit or Transfer. - [ ] Multi-selection `Copy paths`, `Copy names`, and `Properties` share the same reference/inspection section. - [ ] Semantically different actions no longer unnecessarily share the same icon. - [ ] `Open With…` uses `AppWindow`. - [ ] `Extract here` uses `PackageOpen`. - [ ] `Extract to…` uses `FolderArchive`. - [ ] `Duplicate` uses `CopyPlus`. - [ ] `Copy path(s)` uses `Route`. - [ ] `Copy name(s)` uses `FileType`. - [ ] `Move to…` uses `FolderInput`. - [ ] `Copy to…` uses `FolderOutput`. - [ ] `Compress…` uses `PackagePlus`. - [ ] `Permanently delete` uses `CircleX`. - [ ] `Permanently delete` retains Strata's red/danger treatment for both text and icon. - [ ] Equivalent single- and multi-selection actions use the same icon vocabulary. - [ ] New icons remain visually distinguishable at Strata's standard 13 px context-menu size. - [ ] Existing keyboard shortcuts are unchanged. - [ ] Existing filesystem behavior is unchanged. - [ ] Disabled actions, such as Paste when the clipboard contains no supported content, remain disabled under the same conditions. - [ ] Before/after visual evidence covers regular file, archive, folder, multiple selection, and folder background menus.

## Description

Keep GTK's normal renderer as the default and add an opt-in Cairo fallback for small-text artifacts. Upstream [GTK issue #8395](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/gtk/-/work_items/8395) isolates a top-glyph-pixel loss in GL/Vulkan surface rendering; Cairo avoids it but does not fix GTK. Appearance → Rendering offers GTK default / Cairo with a full-width Restart now button when the saved choice differs from the startup choice. Explicit `GSK_RENDERER` overrides the saved choice, and a restart removes only an override Strata injected itself. Shared settings controls/styles and component-reuse guidance are documented.

## Visual evidence

Pending owner upload: before/after font rendering at 13px on Omarchy, and the Appearance → Rendering control before/after changing its value. Captures are not attached yet; GitHub's CLI cannot upload local images into the PR description.

## How to test

1. Launch Strata without `GSK_RENDERER`; Settings → Appearance → Rendering should show GTK default. At a display/text-size combination that produced broken glyphs, inspect the file list and sidebar.
2. Choose Cairo. The full-width Restart now button should appear below the full-width choice and show hover feedback. Click it; Strata should restart using Cairo and the button should disappear. Text should be legible. Select GTK default and restart to restore normal GTK rendering.
3. Launch with an explicit `GSK_RENDERER` value and confirm it takes precedence over the saved choice.

**Expected result:** GTK remains the default, Cairo is an optional workaround, and changes take effect after restart. Cairo can increase CPU use and may be inherited by applications started from Strata; desktop-wide rendering is unchanged.

## Related issue

Closes #1216

## Description

The location entry (Ctrl+L) only accepted directories: pasting a full file path like `/home/user/Documents/report.pdf` was rejected with `NotDirectory`, so opening a known file meant clicking through every directory level. Now, when validation reports `NotDirectory`, the parent is validated and navigated instead, and the named file is carried as a pending reveal:

- the loaded listing selects the file (works in the main window and the portal file chooser used for app Open dialogs / uploads)
- if the parent is already open, the file is selected in place or after a refresh
- a hidden target enables show-hidden so the selection is actually visible
- a file missing from the loaded parent shows an "Unable to select file" dialog

## Visual evidence

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7e0c7dc1-68dd-42ee-b217-78f811bec152

## How to test

1. Run `CHOOSER_CASE=single ./scripts/chooser-dev.sh` (or open the main window and press Ctrl+L)
2. Paste a full path to a file, e.g. `/tmp/some/dir/report.pdf`, and press Enter
3. Repeat with a path to a missing file, and with a hidden file like `~/.bashrc`

**Expected result:** the parent folder opens with the named file selected, ready to confirm; a missing file shows an error dialog; a hidden file reveals after enabling hidden files.

## Related issue

Closes #1139

issues.body:
When opening a file via Strata's "Open File" dialog (the one set as the system default file-open dialog), the location/path field only supports navigating into directories - there's no way to type or paste a direct path to a specific file and have it jump straight to that file (with it selected/highlighted).

## Current behavior:
The path/location field lets you type a directory path to navigate into it, but if you include a filename at the end, it doesn't resolve to that file.

## Requested behavior:
Typing or pasting a full path to a file (e.g. /home/user/Documents/report.pdf) into the location field should navigate to that file's parent directory and select/highlight the file, ready to confirm the "Open" action - similar to how GTK's/KDE's file chooser and most other file-open dialogs behave (e.g. via Ctrl+L path entry in GNOME/Nautilus-style pickers).

## Why this matters:
Without this, opening a specific file when you already know its exact path requires manually clicking through each directory level instead of just pasting the path, which is slow and inconvenient — especially for deeply nested paths.

author: JoeJoeflyn
body:
mise ~/.config/mise/config.toml tools: gh@2.98.0
## Description

SVG quick previews spawned a fresh bwrap helper per file and, once inside, fell through the pixbuf → glycin → ImageMagick → inkscape chain because `glycin-svg` could not run under the nested sandbox (measured ~2s per preview, text SVGs up to ~8s). Even after routing to resvg, the remaining ~100ms was process spawn + binary init, not rendering.

This change keeps every byte of untrusted input inside the existing sandbox while removing both costs:

- **resvg for SVG/SVGZ**: `preview-image`, `document-image`, list thumbnails, and media-metadata probes now content-sniff SVG (BOM/XML/DOCTYPE prologs, extensionless files, and gzip-compressed `.svgz` inflated under a bounded 8MB budget) and rasterize with the pure-Rust usvg/resvg renderer already used for document media. Malformed or oversized inputs still fall back to the existing pixbuf/ImageMagick/RAW chain.
- **Targeted fonts**: instead of `fontdb::load_system_fonts()` parsing all ~2400 system faces per render, SVGs containing `<text` resolve only the declared families via `fc-list` (the fontconfig cache is now bound into the sandbox); the full scan remains the fallback.
- **Persistent preview worker**: `PreviewImage`, `DocumentMermaid`, `DocumentMath`, and `DocumentMathInline` join the existing browser-worker wire protocol and run on a dedicated preview pool (separate from thumbnails, so Space previews cannot starve behind a scroll flood). Cache keys include the operation so a 256px thumbnail can never satisfy an 800px preview. Each job still executes in a fresh fork with namespaces, Landlock, seccomp, and rlimits — only the supervisor is reused — and the original one-shot bwrap path remains the fallback where Landlock ABI 3 is unavailable.
- **Document media concurrency**: embedded media renders now run four-at-a-time instead of strictly serial.

## Benchmark

Measured on this machine, Strata 0.20.1, release binaries, real bwrap sandbox per run (`elapsed_ms` covers in-worker fork + isolation + render + PNG return):

| Input | Before | New one-shot | New pooled (warm) |
|---|---|---|---|
| SVG (shapes) | 1885–2316ms | 94–99ms | — |
| SVG (text) | 2749–8065ms | 151–171ms | — |
| `.svgz` | 1536–1885ms | 86–104ms | — |
| PNG (control) | ~145ms | ~142ms | unchanged |

Pooled path, 12 real previews through the running app: first job on a cold worker 509ms, then median ~42ms, min 10ms (`queue_ms=0` throughout). Net: **~2s → ~42ms median (~45–50×)**.

## Visual evidence

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fbcab61d-743c-4835-a7b1-b04544397e19

## How to test

1. Put a folder containing `.svg`, `.svgz`, a text-heavy `.svg`, and a `.png` in a directory.
2. Select each file and press Space for quick preview; step through them rapidly with the arrow keys.
3. Optionally run with `RUST_LOG=strata::sandbox=debug` and watch `browser worker completed operation=PreviewImage elapsed_ms=…` lines; only one `browser sandbox started` should appear per worker.

**Expected result:** SVG/SVGZ previews appear in tens of milliseconds after the first render; PNG previews are unchanged; SVGs still render inside the sandbox (external resources remain disabled).

## Related issue

N/A — reported and verified interactively; no issue filed per owner request.
title: perf(preview): serve image and document renders from a pooled sandbox worker

author: JoeJoeflyn
body:
## Description

PDF quick previews rendered pages as static `gtk::Picture` images, so there was no text to click into, select, or copy. The sandboxed renderer now extracts Poppler's per-glyph layout alongside each page PNG (bounded `result.text` sidecar, same pattern as `result.meta`), and the UI draws a theme-accent selection overlay on top of each page.

The existing scroll pan gesture now routes per-press: drags starting on glyphs select, drags on margins or pages without a text layer (scanned PDFs) keep panning. Ctrl+A / Ctrl+C reuse the existing preview focus + keyboard dispatch, and copied text is reconstructed in page order including the document's own newlines.

Selection interactions match document viewers: drag-select, double-click for word, triple-click for line, word/line-granularity dragging, and shift-click extension across pages. Highlight bands hug the line box and trim below the baseline when a run has no descender glyphs, so they don't read as bottom-heavy.

## Visual evidence

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/35be0bc7-747a-45f2-ae39-3121ebc03cc6

## How to test

1. Put a text PDF in a folder (or use `tests/fixtures/documents/text.pdf`) and open its quick preview with Space.
2. Drag across a line of text, press Ctrl+C, and paste elsewhere — the selected text should arrive with line breaks intact.
3. Double-click a word, triple-click a line, shift-click to extend, and drag after a double-click to extend word-by-word.
4. Drag on the page margins or a scanned PDF — the view should pan instead of selecting.

**Expected result:** PDF preview text highlights on drag and copies to the clipboard; margins and text-free pages still pan; Ctrl+A selects all loaded pages.

## Related issue

Closes #1220

issues.body:
### Problem or use case

The Space quick preview renders PDF pages as images, so the preview pane cannot accept pointer input for text: clicking or dragging over a PDF does nothing, and there is no way to copy a quote, a command, or a URL out of a document without opening it in a full PDF viewer.

### Proposed solution

Give the PDF preview a real text layer, the same way document viewers do: extract each page's text and glyph bounds in the sandboxed renderer alongside the page image, then let the user drag to select text on the page, see the selection highlighted, and copy it with Ctrl+C (Ctrl+A for all loaded pages). Pages without a text layer (scanned documents, pure images) keep the existing pan behavior.

### Alternatives considered

- Open the document in an external PDF viewer: works, but defeats the purpose of a quick preview for a one-line copy.
- Rectangular (block) selection only: simpler, but copies text in visual order and behaves unlike every document viewer; flow selection matches what users expect.

### Visual examples

N/A

### Strata version

v0.20.1 (main)

### Additional context

macOS Quick Look offers the same capability behind a hidden setting; GNOME Sushi gets it by embedding Evince's document view. Strata renders PDFs in a sandbox, so the text layer needs to travel with the page render instead.
