author: pdwaldrop
body:
## Description

RAR was the one archive format whose decoding ran directly in the main process against attacker-controlled bytes: UnRAR's C parser, driven over FFI, with no process boundary in front of it. ZIP/7z/tar are pure-Rust decoders, and every other untrusted parser in the app (thumbnails, previews, archive *listing* for the other formats) already runs inside the bubblewrap sandbox — RAR extraction was the gap.

The existing mitigations this issue called out as already correct are untouched: `RAR_TEST` with null destination pointers (UnRAR never writes files itself), bounds-checked `UCM_PROCESSDATA` callback wrapped in `catch_unwind`, and destination writes confined through the hardened `ExtractionDestination` (`openat2` + `RESOLVE_IN_ROOT` + per-component `NOFOLLOW` + `O_EXCL`). The residual risk this closes is a memory-corruption bug inside UnRAR's own parsing code before any of that applies.

**What changed:**

- The UnRAR FFI code moved entirely into a new sandboxed helper operation, `--preview-helper extract-rar` (`src/sandbox_helper/archive_rar.rs`). It opens the archive **read-only** inside bubblewrap, with **no filesystem write access of any kind** (no `/output` bind at all, `prlimit --fsize=0`) — the only way bytes leave the child is over its own stdout pipe.
- A small wire protocol (`src/rar_extraction.rs`) frames each member: directory/file header, then (for files) the declared byte count, then a per-member success/failure trailer, matching UnRAR's own error timing (it only signals failure after finishing whatever bytes it emits for that member).
- The parent (`src/sandbox/archive.rs`) spawns the sandboxed child and drives the **existing, unchanged** `ExtractionSession` exactly the way ZIP/7z/tar already do — `MemberContent::File(reader, Some(size))` over a bounded `Take<R>` — so every real destination write still goes through the same hardened confinement code, untouched by this PR.
- Cancellation is enforced by the parent killing the sandboxed child (matching how every other sandboxed helper here already works); the child has no cooperative cancellation path since it has no way to observe the parent's cancellation flag across the process boundary.
- Resource limits: same address-space cap as other sandboxed operations, but a larger CPU budget (120s vs. the shared 10s preview limit) since bulk archive extraction is a fundamentally bigger job than rendering a thumbnail.

## Visual evidence

N/A — pending. Captured a screenshot of the app's file listing after extracting a real `.rar` through "Extract here" (showing both the original archive and the real extracted `VERSION` file it decoded through the sandboxed helper), but no authenticated upload route is available from this session right now. Will follow up with the image attached directly through the PR comment editor.

## How to test

1. Place a `.rar` archive in a folder, right-click it, choose **Extract here** (or **Extract to…**)
2. Expected: the archive extracts correctly, identical to before this change
3. To see the sandbox boundary directly: `ps aux | grep bwrap` while an extraction is running shows a `bwrap` child running `--preview-helper extract-rar`; it exits cleanly once extraction finishes, with no leftover process
4. Password-protected and encrypted-header RAR archives, and a deliberately corrupt archive, are covered by the automated tests below (real fixture files, real UnRAR decode, run in-process without needing bwrap)

## Related issue

Closes #1046

---

Review update: pinned Podman quality formatting, Clippy, and full Rust tests (1805 passed), plus the canonical E2E suite (839 passed), completed successfully on the merged PR head. The password-retry and real RAR activation scenarios also passed after the wire-protocol fix.

A real end-to-end sandboxed spawn (bwrap invoking the built binary with `--preview-helper extract-rar`) cannot run inside `cargo test`'s own test-harness binary — the harness replaces the crate's real `main()`, so a spawned child re-exec would hit the test runner's argument parser, not the app's. This matches the existing convention in this codebase: no test here calls `crate::sandbox::parse` (the equivalent for every other sandboxed operation) end-to-end either; sandboxed dispatch is unit-tested via command-argument assertions instead. Given the added scope, this PR's tests are layered:

- `src/rar_extraction/tests.rs` (9 tests): the wire protocol round-trips, and rejects malformed/oversized/non-UTF-8 records.
- `src/sandbox_helper/archive_rar/tests.rs` (8 tests): the real UnRAR FFI path, run in-process (no spawn needed to call the function directly) against real fixture archives — a plain archive, a corrupt one, and a password-protected one (missing password, wrong password, correct password), asserting the exact wire bytes produced.
- `src/sandbox/archive/tests.rs` (7 tests): the parent's record-dispatch logic against a fake in-memory wire stream (directory/file dispatch, a top-level error record, a per-member trailer failure, an `on_member` failure mid-stream), plus the sandboxed command's constructed arguments (read-only archive bind, no writable bind at all, password never appears on argv).
- `src/adapters/local_operations/archive/decoders/rar/tests.rs` (2 tests): the parent's cancelled-vs-failed error mapping.
- The rest of the archive module's existing suite (157 tests) still passes; two pre-existing tests that called RAR's old in-process `extract_rar` directly (which now always spawns) were adjusted to exclude the RAR case from their generic loops, with the real-UnRAR coverage they lost now covered by the fixture tests above instead.

On top of that, I extracted the real sandboxed pipeline manually: built the binary, ran `./target/debug/strata --preview-helper extract-rar <archive>` directly and confirmed the exact expected wire bytes, then drove the actual app end-to-end (right-click → Extract here on a real `.rar`) and confirmed the correct file was extracted with no leftover sandboxed process afterward — shown above.

issues.body:
## Summary

RAR extraction drives the UnRAR C library over FFI (`src/adapters/local_operations/archive/decoders/rar.rs`) on a `gio::spawn_blocking` worker (`src/adapters/local_operations/archive.rs:240,276`) — that is, inside Strata's own address space. Every other untrusted-parser path in the project is isolated in the bubblewrap helper per #6, and ZIP/7z/tar are pure-Rust decoders. RAR is the one format where attacker-controlled bytes reach a memory-unsafe parser with no process boundary in front of it.

The existing mitigations in that module are genuinely good and this issue is not a report that they are missing:

- `RARProcessFile` is called with `RAR_TEST` and null destination pointers (`rar.rs:239-247`), so UnRAR never writes files itself. This is what makes the CVE-2022-30333 class of traversal inapplicable here, and it is the right design.
- The `UCM_PROCESSDATA` callback bounds-checks the library's buffer before constructing a slice, rejects negative and inconsistent lengths, and wraps the whole callback in `catch_unwind` (`rar.rs:57-72`).
- Extracted bytes are streamed into the hardened `ExtractionDestination` (`openat2` with `RESOLVE_IN_ROOT | NO_MAGICLINKS`, per-component `NOFOLLOW`, `O_EXCL`), so destination writes are confined regardless of what the decoder reports.
- The `unsafe` surface is confined to this one module and documented per project policy.

The residual risk is narrower than that list: a memory-corruption bug **inside UnRAR's own parsing code**, before any of the above applies, compromises the file-manager process — which holds the user's session, Secret Service access for volume passwords, and (on opted-in installs) the portal file-chooser backend.

## Severity

Lower than it first looks, and worth stating plainly:

- RAR parsing is **only** reachable through explicit user-initiated extraction. `extract_rar` is the sole entry point (`archive.rs:276`); there is no passive listing, preview, or thumbnail path that opens a RAR. Merely browsing a folder containing a hostile `.rar` parses nothing.
- RAR compression is not supported, so there is no write-side exposure.
- `unrar_sys` 0.5.8 bundles a current UnRAR (the module notes 7.01), so this is about future unknown bugs, not a known outstanding CVE.

## Proposed fix

Route RAR decoding through the existing preview-helper sandbox, reusing the `sandbox_command` infrastructure in `src/sandbox.rs`:

1. Add a helper operation that opens the archive read-only inside bubblewrap and streams member bytes and metadata back over stdout, keeping the `RAR_TEST` + callback-sink design as-is.
2. Keep destination writes in the parent process through `ExtractionDestination`, so the sandboxed side never needs a writable bind of the destination and the confinement guarantees do not change.
3. Preserve cancellation and progress by framing the existing per-member reporting over the pipe.

The wall-clock, address-space and CPU limits already applied to preview parsing would then also bound pathological RAR archives, which is a secondary benefit.

If a full sandbox move is more than the format warrants, a smaller step would be capping declared member sizes and entry counts before the FFI call, though that does not address memory safety.

## Relationship to existing issues

Follows the precedent set by #6 (sandbox thumbnail and preview parsing of untrusted files) and extends it to the one remaining native parser. #832 and #816 added and fixed RAR support but did not address isolation. #516 (persistent sandbox workers) may be a useful vehicle if that work lands first, since a reusable worker would make per-archive sandbox startup cost less relevant.

author: JoeJoeflyn
body:
## Description

Fixes a bug where completing any file move (drag, Move to…) wiped the system clipboard, so text copied beforehand — e.g. a copied filename — could no longer be pasted. `complete_cut_transfer` now returns early unless tracked cut entries were actually consumed, and only rewrites the clipboard when the app still owns the relevant file-list payload.

Also bundles the columns/list interaction work from the same branch:

- Slow-click rename now only arms on the rendered filename text (List/Columns) or the caption band (Icons); clicking icons, padding, other columns, or chevrons no longer triggers rename — matching Finder.
- A normal-speed double-click opens as before; a pending slow-click rename is cancelled by the second press.
- Columns: re-clicking an already-open folder's name arms rename instead of collapsing the child column; clicking empty column space clears selection and closes deeper columns; header clicks remain focus-only.
- Background (non-revealing) moves no longer steal column focus: moved sources don't trigger select-next in the origin column, and focus returns to the source column after the transfer completes.
- Drop-destination highlight only paints while the pointer's action is acceptable, and re-evaluates on modifier changes.
- Columns now mark the open-folder path: the immediate parent of the active column gets a stronger accent fill (`active-parent`) than older ancestors, plus a short pulse when a child column opens. Unfocused selections were softened so the marker stays distinct.
- Quattro-derived themes now map `highlight` to the selection color.

## Visual evidence

Pending owner upload — local captures available:

- `tests/e2e/baselines/gtk-4.22/columns-overflow.png` (regenerated) shows the path marker: `release` with the strong immediate-parent accent fill, `projects` with the fainter ancestor marker.

## How to test

1. Copy a file's name (or any text) to the clipboard, then drag-move an unrelated file into a folder. Paste somewhere — the copied text survives.
2. Ctrl+X a file, Ctrl+V into a folder — cut-paste still moves and consumes normally.
3. In List view, click a selected file's icon or size column twice slowly — no rename; slow-click on the name text still renames. Click then quickly double-click — the item opens.
4. Columns view: open a folder, re-click its name — rename editor opens instead of collapsing. Click empty space in a column — selection clears and deeper columns close.
5. Drag a file onto a folder in an earlier column with "open folder after drop" off — after the move, focus stays/returns to the source column rather than jumping to the destination.
6. Columns view: the row of the folder whose column is active shows a strong accent fill; ancestors show a faint one; opening a child pulses the parent row.

**Expected result:** clipboard contents survive unrelated moves; rename only arms on name text; open-path rows are visibly marked without conflicting with real selection.

## Related issue

N/A — reported interactively.

## Validation notes

- `quality.sh fmt`, `clippy`: pass (post-merge).

author: JoeJoeflyn
body:
## Description

Keeps large selections and file operations responsive while preserving operation safety:

- represents Select All symbolically and reduces per-entry allocation during 100k-item browsing
- batches live directory publication and monitor reconciliation without blank/loading reloads
- uses storage-aware bounded workers for copy, delete, and restore while retaining cancellation, conflict, symlink, staging, FAT32, and removable-device safeguards
- drains every started batch before reporting cancellation or errors and retains every completed path for undo
- preserves sampled byte progress for large copies and Unicode case-folded collision detection without slowing high-count small-file copies
- starts Trash and Restore feedback only after progress fully closes; outbound restores keep the pre-restore listing frozen until the flight lands
- leaves Permanent Delete immediately actionable while calculating its size summary asynchronously and about 5× faster on the 100k mixed fixture

## Visual evidence

Existing large-selection capture:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/226af438-c06b-41c6-a363-f21c099a0183

Updated Trash/Restore animation capture is pending owner upload.

## How to test

1. Open a folder containing 100,000 mixed files and press Ctrl+A.
2. Copy the selection, including a symlink and a one-file directory, then cancel a second copy partway through.
3. Exercise a case-only destination-name collision.
4. Move a smaller selection to Trash and restore it with Undo.
5. Permanently delete a disposable folder and click the confirmation while its size summary is still calculating.

**Expected result:** selection and browsing remain responsive; all started work settles before cancellation/error completion; copy conflicts preserve source semantics; Trash and restore update the listing without blank reloads; progress fully closes before animation starts; restored rows appear when the outbound flight lands; and Permanent Delete is immediately clickable.

## Related issue

N/A — the owner explicitly requested no issue for this task.

author: wmfeht
body:
## Description

Adds the saved entry point for 10xer mode ([#1233](https://github.com/lgse/strata/issues/1233), part of [#1152](https://github.com/lgse/strata/issues/1152)) and the target product specification in `docs/10xer-mode.md`.

`tenxer_mode` is off by default and saved in `settings.toml`. A saved `true` applies before Settings opens, including a second window and lazily created Columns, Icons, and List views. **Settings → General → Browsing → 10xer mode** and **Ctrl+Shift+M** change the same preference and update every open window immediately.

While the mode is on:

- Window Search and pane Close, filter, refresh, and sort chrome hide. Window Close, chooser Accept/Cancel, and clickable List headings stay.
- **Type to search**, **Keep arrows in file list**, and **Mirror columns selection** stay saved and editable, and those rows show **Not used in 10xer mode.** Their saved values apply again after leaving.
- The footer shows **10X** immediately before the item count. The accessible name and tooltip are **10xer mode**.

**q** leaves the mode and does not close the window. **Q** closes only the current window, through the normal close path, so an in-progress custom-action job on the last window still blocks the close. Turning the mode on hides an open pane filter with the other reduced chrome. Turning it off brings that filter back.

The mode control is titled **10xer mode**. Its subtitle does not call the feature experimental, and leaving does not show a footer flash. `docs/10xer-mode.md` is the target keymap contract for later stories; this change only installs the toggle, **q**, and **Q**.

## Visual evidence

- Settings → General → Browsing, with the **10xer mode** row off and on (including a **Not used in 10xer mode.** subtitle).
- A browser with the mode on: Search and pane chrome hidden, **10X** immediately before the item count.
- The same browser after **q**: chrome restored, **10X** gone, window still open.


Updated visual evidence pending owner upload; the earlier capture predates the 10xer rename.



## How to test

1. Launch with no `tenxer_mode` in `settings.toml`. Confirm the default chrome and keymap are unchanged, and that Settings has no experimental label on **10xer mode**.
2. Turn the mode on from Settings in one window, then with **Ctrl+Shift+M** in a second window. Both windows should hide Search and pane Close/filter/refresh/sort immediately, show **10X** before the count, and keep window Close.
3. Quit and relaunch. The saved choice should already be applied before Settings opens. Switch Columns, Icons, and List and confirm the reduced chrome still applies, including a newly opened column.
4. With the mode on, confirm **Type to search**, **Keep arrows in file list**, and **Mirror columns selection** still toggle in Settings but show **Not used in 10xer mode.** Leave with **q** and confirm those saved values work again, both windows restore chrome, and neither window closed. Press **Q** and confirm only that window closes.
5. With a pane filter open, turn the mode on. The filter and the other reduced chrome should hide. Turn the mode off and the filter should return.

**Expected result:** The preference, both toggles, reduced chrome, the **10X** footer tag, and **q** / **Q** behave as above across two windows, a restart, and a view rebuild. The rest of the Yazi-style map in the specification is not active yet.

## Related issue

Closes #1233

### Problem or use case

As a keyboard-first user, I can opt into Omastrata and return to the
default interface without losing my existing preferences.

### Proposed solution

A saved, off-by-default mode with Settings and keyboard toggles,
experimental labeling, and live browser chrome changes.

**Blocked by:** None. **Decision blockers:** None; chooser integration is OMA-29.

#### Acceptance criteria

1. With no saved setting, the default map and chrome remain unchanged. A saved
   `omastrata_mode = true` applies before Settings is opened, including new
   windows and lazily created Columns, Icons, and List views.
2. Settings → General → Browsing and `Ctrl+Shift+M` change the same preference.
   Two open browser windows update immediately. Restart preserves the choice.
3. Enabled mode hides window Search and pane Close/filter/refresh/sort controls;
   window Close and clickable List headings remain. Leaving restores the controls
   according to their normal state. Verify operability, not pixel positions.
4. `q` disables the mode without closing a window and flashes
   `Left Omastrata mode — Ctrl+Shift+M returns`; `Q` requests closing only the
   current window and respects existing guards such as running custom-action jobs.
5. Type to search, Keep arrows in file list, and Mirror columns selection remain
   saved and editable but show `Not used in Omastrata mode.` Their saved values
   take effect again on exit. The mode control and footer tag identify the
   experimental feature.
6. Initial disabled binding does not steal focus, dismiss an existing interaction,

## Description

While Omastrata mode is on, a key in the file list no longer runs the default map as well. Home-row letters, type-to-search, and the shortcuts the mode leaves unbound (Ctrl+D, Ctrl+F, Ctrl+B, Ctrl+R, Ctrl+Shift+K, Ctrl+T, and Ctrl+\) are consumed before the existing command chain. The shortcuts that stay bound still perform their current actions. Text fields, modal dialogs, native menus, and the open shortcut reference keep their own input. Ctrl+Shift+M still toggles from a browser text field and does not override a modal. Ctrl+, still opens Settings.

The conflicting application accelerators follow the saved mode. Turning the mode on removes them for every window, closing one window does not put them back, and turning the mode off restores the default set. Repeating the same mode value does not stack accelerators.

The replacement Yazi verbs are not implemented here. Those keys are only stopped.

## Visual evidence

N/A. This change is input routing only. No chrome, copy, or layout changed.

## How to test

1. Turn Omastrata mode on with Ctrl+Shift+M or Settings → General → Browsing.
2. Focus the file list. Press h/j/k/l, a letter such as s, Space, Ctrl+D, Ctrl+F, Ctrl+B, Ctrl+R, Ctrl+Shift+K, Ctrl+T, and Ctrl+\. The selection, files, filter, sidebar, and rename state stay as they were. q leaves the mode without closing the window. Q closes only the current window.

author: adamcbrewer
body: ## Description Add quick previews for local printable models. STL gets a fixed-angle, theme-tinted render. 3MF uses an embedded thumbnail only when there is exactly one usable candidate; multiple usable thumbnails or no usable thumbnail fall back to rendering. Corrupt candidates do not hide a single usable image, and candidate inspection has byte/pixel/work limits. FreeCAD files show their embedded thumbnail without requiring FreeCAD. Multiple objects within one model part can render; assemblies split across model parts show “Multipart model detected. Unable to render preview.” when rendering is needed. A single usable thumbnail can still preview those assemblies. Shows actual worker stages alongside the spinner: “Reading model…”, “Rendering 1.2M triangles…” and “Finishing preview…”, plus thumbnail-specific text. No estimated percentage or artificial delay. Rendering stays inside the bounded preview sandbox, with palette-aware in-memory caching and live theme updates. Inputs remain limited to 128 MiB and meshes to 2 million triangles, with centralized constants for future tuning. **128 MiB is an input-file limit, not a RAM limit**; unpacked 3MF XML has a separate 128 MiB limit. Component budgets are enforced before expansion, and two-pass rendering avoids retaining a second projected mesh. Limit failures explain why the preview is unavailable. Browser thumbnails now extract a single usable embedded PNG from local 3MF/FreeCAD files through the existing persistent workers and caches. They never render geometry; STL and missing/ambiguous embedded images keep the normal file icon. No new pool or dependencies. Heavy Quick Previews still share one permit with PDFs/documents; format and palette travel explicitly with the request. ## Visual evidence https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ff5f6e53-d19c-499a-9dcf-a135cf72c760 ## How to test 1. Select a local ASCII or binary STL and open Quick preview. For a larger model, watch the loading text, then change the active theme while the preview is open. Switch files during rendering to check that old progress does not appear on the new selection. 2. Preview 3MF files with one, multiple and no usable embedded thumbnails, including one valid image plus a corrupt candidate. Try a `.3mf` symlink to an extensionless target. Check multiple objects and transforms within one model part, then an assembly split across model parts. 3. Preview an FCStd file with a saved thumbnail, then one without. FreeCAD does not need to be installed. 4. Try a model larger than 128 MiB or an STL exceeding 2 million triangles. 5. In filtered List results, select a nested result using the keyboard, open its context menu, choose Properties, then close the dialog. Double-click a file and confirm it launches only once. 6. Browse a folder containing 3MF/FCStd files with embedded PNGs in Columns, List and Icons, then navigate away and back. Files without a usable image should retain the normal icon; no geometry should be rendered for browser thumbnails. **Expected result:** Models render at the fitted three-quarter angle and follow theme changes. Loading text reflects actual worker stages; fast previews may finish before every stage is visible. One usable 3MF thumbnail is displayed in its original colours; multiple usable thumbnails trigger rendering only in Quick Preview. Unsupported multipart rendering, missing FreeCAD thumbnails and exceeded limits produce specific messages. Filtered results retain their selection after the context menu and Properties close. ## Related issue Closes #1225 ## NOTES The filtered-result selection fix remains separate. A follow-up fixes its duplicate double-click dispatch while preserving keyboard activation and selection after Properties closes. Resource behavior and limits are documented in `docs/preview-sandbox.md`. The input/triangle limits are retained; memory amplification is reduced instead. Three-run medians in the pinned environment: a two-million-triangle STL used 288.5 → 207.5 MiB peak helper RSS (CPU 1.68 → 1.78 s, identical PNG); excessive-component 3MF rejection used 309.3 → 107.7 MiB and 4.65 → 0.43 s. These are helper measurements, not total application RAM or release-performance guarantees.

issues.body: ## Problem or use case STL and 3MF files have no visual quick preview in Strata. When browsing printable models, it would help to recognise the shape without opening a slicer or CAD application. The shaded model preview on Printables is a good example and should inheri the active OS theme. ## Proposed solution - Start with local STL (binary and ASCII) and 3MF files. Show a fitted, shaded still image in the existing quick-preview pane when the file is selected. - Tint the model from the active theme accent and use theme surface/background colours. Update an open preview when the theme changes, including when following Omarchy. For the initial 3MF preview, use the same theme-tinted appearance rather than material colours. - Proposed architecture: detect these extensions in the preview provider; parse and render the mesh inside the existing bounded preview sandbox; return a size-limited image to the GTK pane. Keep mesh input, triangle counts, output size and render time bounded, with cancellation on selection change. If images are cached, include the theme palette in the cache key or redraw on theme change. - Frame the complete model (including 3MF objects and their transforms) at a useful fixed angle. author: JoeJoeflyn
body:
## Description

Large images (> ~134 MP, such as 18354 × 23598 px scans) exceed the 512 MiB sandbox `RLIMIT_FSIZE` when decoders allocate an uncompressed decoded pixel buffer (`width × height × 4 bytes`), causing the kernel to kill the decoder with `SIGXFSZ`.

- Check image dimensions from headers before initiating a full-resolution raster decode.
- Implement fast SOF0 (JPEG), IHDR (PNG), and GIF dimension sniffers to avoid slow `Pixbuf::file_info` hangs.
- When an image exceeds `FILE_SIZE_LIMIT_BYTES` (~134 MP), check for an embedded EXIF thumbnail in `IFD1` via `kamadak-exif`. If present, render the thumbnail and preview using the embedded thumbnail (with an ImageMagick fallback to handle nested Glycin/Bubblewrap sandboxing).
- If an oversized image has no EXIF thumbnail, safely return an empty result so Strata displays the generic fallback icon without crashing or killing sandbox processes.
- Normal images (≤ 134 MP) continue to use full-quality raster decoding.

## Visual evidence

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9ea2009b-9f60-45ea-9d58-56d5192ad3d2

## How to test

1. Place an oversized JPEG with an embedded EXIF thumbnail (e.g. > 134 MP scan) and an oversized JPEG without EXIF in a directory.
2. Open Strata and navigate to that directory.
3. Observe that the image with an EXIF thumbnail renders its thumbnail and preview pane cleanly.
4. Observe that the oversized image without EXIF displays a generic icon without any `SIGXFSZ` crashes in `coredumpctl list`.

**Expected result:**
Oversized images render safely without killing sandboxed decoder processes with `SIGXFSZ`.

## Related issue

Closes #1202

issues.body:
### Strata version

0.18.0 (the limits involved are unchanged on `main` as of 9c60c0b / v0.19.0)

### Installation method

GitHub release archive

### Linux distribution and desktop environment

Arch Linux (Omarchy 4.0.4), Hyprland 0.56.2 — glycin 2.1.5, gdk-pixbuf2 2.44.7, bubblewrap 0.12.0

### What happened?

Opening a folder that contains a very large JPEG (18354 × 23598 px, ~433 MP, 22 MB on disk) in the Strata file chooser (portal backend) kills the sandboxed glycin loader with **SIGXFSZ**, and systemd-coredump records a crash. It happens every time that folder is shown: two loader crashes per open, about half a second apart. I saw it on two separate days, four cores in total, all identical. The file gets no thumbnail, and on desktops that turn coredumps into notifications, the user gets a "process crashed" alert each time.

The cause is the sandbox's `RLIMIT_FSIZE`. glycin decodes at full resolution and sizes a memfd to `width × height × channels` before scaling down. For this image that is 18354 × 23598 × 3 = **1,299,353,076 bytes**, well past `FILE_SIZE_LIMIT_BYTES` (512 MiB). Going past `RLIMIT_FSIZE` makes the kernel send SIGXFSZ, which by default terminates the process, so glycin never reaches its own error path ("Failed to set memfd size").

The code already expects this: `file_size_limit_holds_a_full_resolution_decoded_frame` in `src/sandbox/tests.rs` notes that exceeding the limit "kills the loader with SIGXFSZ rather than surfacing an error", and sizes the limit for images up to 50 MP. Nothing stops larger images from being decoded, though. Any image over ~179 MP (RGB) or ~134 MP (RGBA) reaches the decoder and kills it.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a large JPEG, e.g. `magick -size 18000x18000 xc:gray big.jpg` (324 MP → ~972 MB decoded RGB; I have not run this exact command, my reproduction used a real 433 MP scan)
2. Open a file dialog in any app with Strata as the FileChooser portal backend, and navigate to that folder
3. `coredumpctl list glycin-image-rs` shows new SIGXFSZ entries

### Expected behavior

Oversized images are skipped: they get a generic icon (or a "too large to preview" state), and no sandboxed process is killed. Two possible fixes:

- Check the image's dimensions before decoding. `gdk_pixbuf::Pixbuf::file_info` already returns width/height cheaply from the header (the RAW path in `sandbox_helper.rs` uses it). Refusing to decode when `width × height × 4` exceeds the file-size budget would turn the crash into an ordinary error.
- Alternatively, set SIGXFSZ to `SIG_IGN` in the sandbox helper before glycin spawns its loaders. An ignored disposition survives `execve`, so `ftruncate` would return `EFBIG` and glycin would report an error instead of dying. I have not checked whether bwrap or glycin's spawn path resets signal dispositions, so this one needs verifying.

### Relevant logs

```shell
# coredumpctl info (one of four identical cores)
Signal: 25 (XFSZ) si_code: SI_USER
Command Line: /usr/lib/glycin-loaders/2+/glycin-image-rs --dbus-fd 8
User Unit: dbus-:1.1-org.freedesktop.impl.portal.desktop.strata@0.service

# /proc/<pid>/limits of the crashed loader, as recorded by systemd-coredump
Max cpu time              10                   10                   seconds
Max file size             536870912            536870912            bytes
Max address space         2147483648           2147483648           bytes

# crashing thread, symbolized via debuginfod.archlinux.org
#0  __ftruncate64 (fd=6, length=1299353076)
#1  nix::unistd::ftruncate (len=1299353076)            nix-0.30.1/src/unistd.rs:1531
#2  glycin_common::shared_memory::SharedMemory::new (size=1299353076)   glycin-common/src/shared_memory.rs:20
#3  glycin_utils::image_rs::Handler::frame<image::codecs::jpeg::decoder::JpegDecoder<...>>   glycin-utils/src/image_rs.rs:59
#4  glycin_image_rs::ImageRsFormat<...>::frame          glycin-loaders/glycin-image-rs/src/main.rs:451
```

### Additional context

It is deterministic: all four cores request exactly the same 1,299,353,076-byte buffer. I haven't traced which caller makes the second decode attempt in each pair; it may be the thumbnail plus the single-click preview (`single_click_previews = true` here).

The 2 GiB `RLIMIT_AS` would also stop an image this size even if the file-size limit were raised, so raising the limits alone won't fix it.

body: ## Description Adds a **Send to** context-menu submenu for copying files and folders to mounted removable devices. Destinations include the drive root, up to three recent folders, and **Choose folder…**. Device targets are re-resolved at activation so stale mounts fail closed; copies do not navigate away from the source. Transfers now show files copied, the current file, bytes, speed, and estimated time. FAT32 copies preflight the 4 GiB per-file limit; native new copies stage files so a failed or cancelled copy does not publish a partial file. If cancellation waits on a nonresponsive device, the dialog explains the risk, allows a return to the browser with a persistent warning, and blocks new file operations in that browser until the pending transfer resolves. A failed flush is reported, not treated as a safe cancellation. **Stopping Strata's writes does not make earlier writes safe to unplug.** A physical exFAT USB transfer stalled with kernel USB write/read errors during manual testing. The cause of that device-level failure remains undiagnosed; this PR does not guarantee recovery from stalled kernel I/O. A successful physical-drive retest remains outstanding. ## Visual evidence Before: After: Transfer progress (simulated GTK fixture, not a physical USB copy): ![Progress showing files, bytes and speed](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9fe8006e-fcc0-417d-b604-7f2bf448cb66) Stalled cancellation (simulated GTK fixture): ![Device not responding and safe-eject warning](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b225bf5f-327b-4b53-bdff-3c2805fb839c) ## How to test 1. On a healthy mounted removable device, select files/folders and use **Send to → Drive root** or **Choose folder…**. Confirm sources remain unchanged, the browser does not navigate away, and destinations appear in recents. 2. Copy a large file and check that files copied, bytes, current file, and speed update. Cancel: an incomplete final file should not appear. If the device is unresponsive, the warning must remain until the transfer resolves; returning to the browser must not imply safe removal. 3. Try a file over 4 GiB on FAT32 (including inside a selected folder): it should fail before copying. exFAT must not receive the FAT32 size rejection. 4. Disconnect or unmount an idle device before selecting its stale Send to destination; it should fail closed. **Do not intentionally disconnect an active transfer.** **Expected result:** Only mounted local writable removable devices appear, transfers provide accurate feedback, and errors/cancellation never claim a drive is safe to unplug until the OS confirms safe eject. ## Related issue Closes #1153

issues.body:
### Problem or use case

Copying a folder to a USB stick today means: copy, navigate to the device (sidebar or another pane/tab), then paste. I do this daily — copying an Academia folder onto a pendrive before going out to teach — and the navigation is the slow part, especially when the current location is deep in the tree and I would rather not leave it.

Windows Explorer covers this with "Send to": right-click a folder, pick a removable drive, and the copy starts immediately without moving away from the current folder. Windows copies to the drive root and never prompts for a destination.

### Proposed solution

Add a **Send to** submenu to the file/folder context menu listing the removable devices currently mounted — the same ones Strata already surfaces under Devices in the sidebar. Each device opens its own submenu whose first row copies to the drive root, using the existing copy path with the normal progress reporting, conflict handling, and undo behavior:

```
Send to ▸
  ┌─────────────────┐
  │ Kingston 32GB ▸ │──┬──────────────────────┐
  │ SanDisk Ultra ▸ │  │ Drive root           │
  └─────────────────┘  │ /Teaching   (recent) │
                       │ ──────────────────── │
                       │ Choose folder…       │
                       └──────────────────────┘
```

Activating the device row directly would be the shortest path to the root, but a `GMenuModel` item carries either an action or a submenu link and never both, so **Drive root** is an explicit first row instead. Everything below that row is optional (see below); with it dropped, each device submenu holds a single item.

Points worth deciding:

- Multi-selection behaves the same as copy/paste.
- When no removable device is mounted, hide the submenu or show a single insensitive row.
- Scope the list to removable local volumes. Internal drives and GVfs/network mounts probably should not appear by default; a setting could widen it later.
- Exclude or disable read-only mounts.
- Copies should go through the same FAT/exFAT name handling addressed in #1123.

#### Optional, beyond Windows parity

Windows offers no destination prompt, so treat these as separable and drop them if they are not wanted: a **Choose folder…** row reusing the existing chooser rooted at that device, and remembered recent destinations per device, so a repeated weekly copy into the same subfolder stays a two-click path rather than a chooser round trip. **Drive root** should land first and stand on its own.

### Alternatives considered

- **Copy, then paste with the device open in another pane or tab.** Works today; it is exactly the navigation this request removes.
- **Pinning the device.** Pins are per path and mount points move, so this still ends in navigating.
- **Dragging onto the device in the sidebar.** Where that works, it still needs a precise drag across the window, which is awkward with a touchpad or a long selection.
- **User-defined context-menu actions (#1050).** A script could express the copy, but a built-in submenu can enumerate live mounts, which a static user-defined action cannot.
- **A flat device list with one shared "Choose folder…" row.** Keeps the root copy at one click, but the chooser then has to cover device selection as well, and per-device recent destinations no longer have a place to live.
- **Custom popover rows via `gtk_popover_menu_add_child()`,** splitting name and arrow into separate hit targets so the root copy stays one click. Rejected here as non-standard for the menu system and more work for keyboard and accessibility, but it is the only layout that gets both.

### Visual examples

ASCII sketch above; no screenshot yet.

### Strata version

0.19.0

### Additional context

Related issues: #295 (sidebar eject/unmount), #441 (mounted USB drives in the sidebar), #1067 (removable drives in the portal sidebar), #1123 (FAT/exFAT copy name handling), #1050 (user-defined context-menu actions).

author: JoeJoeflyn
body:
## Description

Adds a Name field to file-open portal choosers: type an existing local filename or paste a direct HTTP(S) file URL, then click Open or press Enter. Remote files download to a temporary local path returned to the requesting application.

A compact circular download indicator and cancellation live in the bottom-left action bar. Unknown-size downloads show a spinner and bytes received. Name-field validation, local lookup, and URL download errors appear there as plain error text without adding a row or a box. The address bar remains navigation-only; global Ctrl+V does not start downloads. Folder, SaveFile, and SaveFiles requests do not support remote downloads. Credentialed URLs and automatic redirects are rejected.

This revises the original interaction per the owner's request. Local filename selection preserves filters, multiple selections, and keyboard file actions.

## Visual evidence

Original implementation, before the Name-field/action-bar redesign:
https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/530536b3-a58e-44eb-8789-6ed9712b0cbc

Updated captures are retained locally; owner upload through the GitHub editor is pending because the available tooling cannot upload GitHub image attachments. The original clip does not show the revised interface.

## How to test

1. Launch this build with `python3 scripts/portal-test.py single --binary target/debug/strata`, or trigger a file-open portal request routed to it.
2. Type `notes.txt` in Name and click Open: the response should select that existing local file.
3. Open another request, paste a direct HTTP(S) file URL into Name, and click Open or press Enter. Progress appears at the bottom-left; completion returns a local `file://` URI under a `strata-download-*` temporary folder.
4. During a download, press Escape or its cancel button: the chooser remains usable, and another filename or URL can be submitted.
5. Entering a web URL in the address bar still fails as an unsupported location. Folder and Save requests must not download URLs.

issues.body:
### Problem or use case

On Windows, pasting a direct file URL into the File name field of an Open/Save dialog makes the shell download the file to a temporary location and hand the application a local path. This lets you use remote files without manually downloading them first.

Strata's portal file chooser currently rejects `https://` input in the location bar (Ctrl+L) with an unsupported-scheme error, and the Save dialog's Name field rejects it as an invalid basename. There is no way to pick a remote file for an application that requested an Open dialog.

### Proposed solution

When the chooser receives an `http(s)` URL — in the location entry for Open requests, or in the Name field for SaveFile requests — download the file to a temporary directory with a progress indicator and a Cancel option, then complete the request with the local `file://` path. Directory and multi-destination (SaveFiles) requests should keep rejecting URLs with a clear message.

Filename resolution: Content-Disposition `filename`/`filename*` when present, else the URL path basename (percent-decoded), else a generic fallback. Downloads go to a unique `strata-download-*` directory under the system temp dir; stale directories are pruned on subsequent runs.

### Alternatives considered

- GVFS `http://` mounts: the GVfs HTTP backend is read-only WebDAV-era code, often absent, and cannot be mapped to a native path the portal can return.
- Navigating into the downloaded temp folder instead of completing the request: possible follow-up, but the Windows behavior completes the dialog directly.
- Returning the file under a stable name in a shared downloads cache: rejected — unique temp dirs avoid collisions and cleanup policy stays simple.

### Visual examples

N/A — behavior mirrors the Windows common file dialog.

### Strata version

0.19.0 (main @ c43f1eed)

### Additional context

Changes `docs/portal-file-chooser.md` behavior ("entering a remote URI shows an unsupported-location error") for the http/https schemes only. smb/sftp and other URI schemes remain unsupported in the chooser.

author: JoeJoeflyn
body:
## Description

Fixes directory scheduler starvation in global search when indexing trees with multiple sibling repositories or subdirectories (e.g. `~/Project`).

Key changes:
- Prioritize shallower depths during directory scheduling when virtual work is equal so parent listings discover immediate sibling folders before subtrees are traversed.
- Separate structural directory batching from regular file batch limits to prevent parent directory listings from repeatedly pausing, restarting, and re-scanning from index 0.
- Precompile glob overrides once per root instead of repeatedly rebuilding regex sets on every directory slice.
- Omit redundant `stat` syscalls on directory entries and reuse walker metadata for files.
- Add cache exclusions for `go/pkg/mod/` and `__pycache__/`.
- Extend generated-cache pruning coverage for Go modules and Python bytecode caches.

### Benchmark
Real filesystem search on a home directory with 30+ repositories (searching for `rune` located at entry #32 in `~/Project`):
- **Before:** Timed out at 20,000ms (`search index partial entries=59731 elapsed_ms=20026`) and failed to reach sibling folders later in directory order.
- **After:** `~/Project/rune` is discovered, indexed, and returned as the top match in **277ms** (<0.3s).

## Visual evidence

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b6082b0b-894a-4187-8c44-f70071f30331

## How to test

1. Open Strata in a home directory containing multiple subprojects or repositories (e.g. `~/Project`).
2. Press `Ctrl+F` to open the search bar.
3. Type the name of a folder located further down alphabetically (e.g. `rune`).

**Expected result:**
The folder match appears immediately in the search results within milliseconds, without spinning or timing out with partial search coverage.

## Related issue

Closes #1286

issues.body:
### Strata version
0.20.1

### Installation method
Built from source

### Linux distribution and desktop environment
Linux, Hyprland

### What happened?
Global search gets stuck descending deep into preceding subdirectories when indexing large trees (such as ~/Project with multiple repositories), causing shallow sibling folders to be starved and omitted before the indexing budget expires. Furthermore, regex overrides are repeatedly recompiled on every directory slice.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Have a directory with multiple sibling subdirectories (e.g. ~/Project with 30+ repositories).
2. Search for a folder located later in directory order (e.g. 'rune').
3. Observe that search times out and fails to find the folder.

### Expected behavior
Shallow sibling folders should be discovered quickly before deep subtrees are traversed, and search should find matching folders within milliseconds.

### Additional context
Pruning large generated caches like go/pkg/mod/ and __pycache__/, precompiling glob overrides once per root, and giving shallow depths priority during directory scheduling resolves the starvation.

author: JoeJoeflyn
body:
## Description

Audio files now open in a now-playing view instead of a blank video surface:

- **Artwork:** embedded art, falling back to a `cover`/`folder`/`front`/`album` image in the same folder. Without art, a theme-colored record spins in its place.
- **Track changes:** existing art stays put while details load. Only different artwork triggers tuck → crossfade → slide-out; identical album art is reused. Between art and no art, the record and the art fade separately, so they never blend.
- **Details:** title, artist and album come from tags. The track number comes from tags, otherwise the file's position among the folder's audio files ("3 of 12 in folder"), or visible filtered audio results ("3 of 12 in results"). Every row keeps its space while tags load, so switching tracks never shifts the layout.
- **Spectrum analyzer:** Winamp-style. Bars rise instantly and fall fast, and peak caps hold, then drop under gravity. The bars follow what is actually being heard and move the same at any refresh rate.
- **Waveform scrubber:** playback starts immediately on a plain progress line. A waveform overview then grows in from that line, decoded in the background at low priority after 50 ms of stable selection. Hovering previews the target time and clicking seeks. Overviews are cached, selections replaced within that delay never decode, and failures keep the plain line.
- **Layout:** art beside the controls when the pane is wider than tall, art on top otherwise. When space runs short, the spectrum goes first, then the art.
- **Previous/next:**
  - Buttons step through the folder's audio files, or visible filtered results including subfolders, and keep playing. Playlists and MIDI are excluded.
  - In 10xer, `<`/`>` do the same, from the listing while an audio preview is open or from inside the preview.
  - In default mode, use `Ctrl+Alt+<`/`>`.
  - All are listed in F1.
- **Errors:** a broken track keeps its audio view, a visible error, and previous/next controls. Broken or oversized covers cannot block audio; multiple embedded pictures prefer the front cover. Tracks never advance automatically.
- **Restarting:** songs always start from the beginning. Video previews still resume where they were closed, as in `main`.

Performance:
- Songs play through an audio-only session, so artwork is no longer decoded into a frame re-sent 30 times a second, and resizing the pane no longer restarts audio.
- The record and covers are rendered once at display size. Resizing scales those cached textures and regenerates them after 120 ms at a stable size.
- Uncached tags and artwork wait 50 ms too; cache hits stay immediate. Folder artwork is reused across tracks, and failed lookups can retry.
- The record only spins when it is visible, and nothing ticks while paused.

The sandbox gains `preview-audio`, `audio-tags`, `audio-cover` and `audio-peaks` operations; see the new "Audio previews" section in `docs/preview-sandbox.md`. Embedded tags are sanitized before display.

## Visual evidence

Pending: the owner will upload recordings through the GitHub editor. Before/after captures of playback-error recovery and a resize recording are retained locally; the review-fix comment identifies the files. No attachments have been uploaded.

## How to test

1. Open a folder containing:
   - an MP3 with embedded art
   - a FLAC next to `cover.jpg`
   - an untagged Opus or Ogg file with no art
   - a text file
2. Preview the text file, then move to the MP3 and press play.
3. Drag the divider to make the pane wider than tall, then narrower.
4. Hover and click the waveform. Click next and previous while playing, crossing between songs with and without art.
5. Turn on 10xer mode (`Ctrl+Shift+M`), press `i` on a song, then use `>` / `<` from the listing. Press `l` and use `>`, `<`, Space and `←`/`→` inside the preview.
6. Press F1 and check the "Preview media" section.
7. Add an undecodable `.wav`, playlists/MIDI, and a second track using the same folder cover. Step rapidly while playing; use mute/volume during loading, then step past the broken track.
8. Filter for audio files including subfolders and use previous/next in Columns, List, and Icons.
9. Preview a video saved with an `.ogg` audio extension and an MP3 containing front/back covers.

**Expected result:**
- The art fades in on its own when coming from the text file, then the record slides out once playing.
- Tags and the track caption appear without the layout moving.
- The bars jump with the music and fall quickly, while the peak caps linger.
- The waveform grows in shortly after selection, and seeking works.
- The layout switches between side-by-side and stacked.
- Previous/next and `<`/`>` skip non-audio files, keep playing, and restart each song from the beginning.
- In the listing, the cursor ring follows `<`/`>`; inside the preview, the keys stay in the preview.
- Track changes never show the record through translucent art; identical art does not animate into itself.
- Errors keep navigation usable, rapid steps preserve playback, and closing or cancelling a load cannot cause a later surprise autoplay.
- Filtered stepping stays within visible audio results. The `.ogg` retains its video picture; the multi-cover MP3 shows its front cover.

## Related issue

Closes #1288

### Problem or use case
Audio file previews currently show the generic video surface with no visual indication of the audio content or playback energy.

### Proposed solution
Render a SoundCloud-style live spectrum visualization in the preview pane for audio files: a 24-band FFT computed from the decoded PCM stream, resampled into thin animated bars themed with the accent color. Clicking the waveform toggles play/pause.

### Alternatives considered
Static waveform overview (no live spectrum), or keeping the video widget for audio.

author: wmfeht
body:
## Description

In 10xer mode a file preview has its own keyboard owner, so keys held by the drawer cannot launch, move, rename, delete, paste, or select listing items.

**i** toggles a file's preview and leaves focus in the listing, so **j** / **k** keep moving the cursor and the preview follows it. On a directory, **i** is still the unfocused Miller column or the folder peek. In List and Columns, **l** / **→** on a previewable file opens the drawer if needed and moves the keys into it. A further **l** / **→** or **Enter** does not open the file. **h** / **←** or **Shift+Tab** returns to the same cursor without closing the drawer or going to the parent; the next **h** is ordinary parent navigation. **Esc** and **i** close the drawer and hand the keys back. An unpreviewable file flashes `Nothing to preview`.

While the drawer owns the keys, an accent bar runs across the top of its header. Document motion and paging scroll the document. An archive tree stays read-only: member navigation never extracts or opens a listing file, and the directory cursor and fill stay put. A password field takes typed text and editing shortcuts. Media controls keep play/pause, seek, volume, and mute. **J** / **K** scroll an open preview without taking focus. Leaving the mode, clicking the listing, or closing the drawer releases ownership. With 10xer mode off, archive and media keys stay on the default map.

## Visual evidence


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e1d8eff2-3f7d-46b0-ae11-5591b38405ed



## How to test

1. Turn on 10xer mode and open a folder of text files in List view.
2. Focus a long text file and press **i**. The preview opens and the cursor stays on that file. Press **j**. The cursor moves and the preview follows. Press **i** again. The preview closes.
3. Focus the long file and press **l**. The accent bar moves to the preview header. Press **j**, **End**, and **Page Down**. The document scrolls and the listing does not move or launch the file.
4. Press **h**. Focus returns to the same file, the preview stays open, and the folder does not change. Press **h** again. The parent folder opens.
5. Press **l** to re-enter the preview, then **Esc**. The drawer closes and the file is focused again.
6. Focus a file Strata cannot preview and press **l**. The footer says `Nothing to preview`.
7. Open a password-protected archive with **l**, type the password (letters such as **h** and **j** stay in the field), unlock it, and move through members with **j** / **k**. Nothing is extracted. **h** at the archive root returns to the listing. **Esc** closes the drawer.
8. Turn 10xer mode off and open an archive preview. Arrow keys, **Enter**, and **Esc** behave as they did before.

**Expected result:** Preview keys scroll or operate that preview. They do not change the listing selection, location, or files on disk. Returning to the listing keeps the drawer open; closing it returns the keys to the same cursor.

## Related issue

https://github.com/wmfeht/strata/issues/43
https://github.com/wmfeht/strata/issues/44

body: ## Description 10xer mode can now arm a two-key `g` chord. The footer shows `g-` and the valid second keys, and the sidebar shows keycaps for Home, Downloads, Documents, Pictures, Videos, Trash, Network, Recent, and the visible PINNED rows. The next key completes only that chord. `g g` moves to the first item. `g h` opens Home, `g c` opens `~/.config`, and `g d`, `g t`, `g n`, `g r`, `g k`, `g p`, and `g v` open Downloads, Trash, Network, Recent, Documents, Pictures, and Videos. `g 1`–`g 9` follow visible pin order, skipping bookmarks that are already standard places. A missing user folder reports `No Downloads folder`, `No Documents folder`, `No Pictures folder`, or `No Videos folder`. A missing pin reports `No pin N` and stays put. Escape cancels. Any other second key cancels with `Unknown chord`. While a document or archive preview owns the keys, `g g` goes to the top of that preview instead of changing the listing. Settings, leaving 10xer mode, and closing the window drop a pending chord. Sort, copy, custom-action, and typed-path chords stay for their own stories; this change is the shared armed-chord interaction they will use. ## Visual evidence Shortcut reference refresh: after screenshot pending owner upload through GitHub editor (the existing capture above predates the refresh). The F1 reference now has a centered panel with the same dimmed, blurred backdrop and glow as global search, a themed search input, category sidebar, two-column action list, shortcut badges, counts, and a footer. Filtering preserves the panel height; search matches actions and keys, and category selection narrows the list. The wider sidebar does not move when a category is selected. The footer now lists dialog-only navigation: Ctrl+B for categories, Ctrl+F for search, Ctrl+L for results, arrows or j/k to move, Tab to cycle, and Escape to close. Focus stays inside while open. At narrower window sizes, the header, tightly packed wrapping library-style category pills, and single-column results stack vertically, keeping the reference within the window; resizing while open updates the layout. Tab repeatedly focuses the active category button, not the sidebar scroller; only that button gains a focus border, without tinting the sidebar or results background. In wide mode, category rows remain near their natural height instead of stretching to fill the sidebar, including after resizing from compact mode. A faint theme-accent background marks the focused results list. ## How to test 1. Resize the window below and above ~1480 px, open F1 shortcuts, and confirm the panel stays inside the window and changes between stacked and two-column layouts. Tab through search, the active category pill, and results in both sizes; use arrows/hjkl to select any pill and scroll the pill strip when it overflows. Then open F1 shortcuts. Search for an action and a key, choose a category, scroll with arrows/Page Down, close with F1 or Escape, and confirm browsing focus returns. Repeat with 10xer mode off and on. 2. Turn on 10xer mode and open a folder that contains several files. 2. Press `g`. The footer shows `g-` and the place hints, and the sidebar shows keycaps on the standard places and visible pins. 3. Press `Escape`, then `d`. The chord is gone and the listing does not jump to Downloads. 4. Press `g` then `z`. The footer reports `Unknown chord` and the folder does not change. 5. Press `g g` and confirm the cursor is on the first item. Press `g h`, `g c`, `g d`, `g t`, `g n`, `g r`, `g k`, `g p`, and `g v` and confirm each destination. With Documents or Videos missing, the matching `No … folder` message appears and the current folder stays. 6. Pin two folders, with a standard place such as Downloads stored between them in the bookmark file. Press `g 1` and `g 2` and confirm they follow the visible PINNED order. Press `g 3` and confirm `No pin 3` without navigating. 7. Open a long text preview with `l`, press `g g`, and confirm the preview scrolls to the top. Press `g` then `h` and confirm the listing does not go Home. 8. Press `g`, then open Settings with `Ctrl+,`, turn 10xer mode off, or close the window. The chord is cancelled. **Expected result:** Each second key does only the place or cancel action above. A cancelled chord does not leave a key that later acts on its own. ## Related issue https://github.com/wmfeht/strata/issues/45

author: wmfeht
body:
## Description

10xer mode can search names under the current folder from the footer without changing the saved Include subfolders preference or dropping an earlier `f` filter.

`s` opens a `search:` prompt and searches the current folder tree, including when Include subfolders is off. It does not search other indexed roots, search file contents, or bind `S`. At most 100 hits are shown. The footer keeps `search: …` and the displayed hit count, including zero, and shows the hit under the cursor as a path relative to the searched folder. A folder with no local path, such as Network, reports `Nothing to search`.

Enter applies the query, closes the prompt, and returns focus to the hits, on the first hit when there is one. It does not open that hit. A following Enter opens it through ordinary activation. Escape from a nonempty prompt keeps the hits. Escape from an empty prompt cancels. Dismissing the search restores the previous `f` filter, or the ordinary listing when there was none. Pressing `s` again while hits are showing pre-fills that query. A newer query, navigation, leaving the mode, or closing the window drops a slower previous result stream. Changing view keeps the search.

While hits are showing, List and Columns move through those hits. Icons move among the result icons. `g g` and `G` reach the first and last hit. `g f` opens the folder that holds the focused hit, selects it there, and ends the search so the item stays visible. `i` opens an unfocused column or folder peek for a directory hit, and toggles preview for a file hit, without taking preview ownership. In List and Columns, `h` dismisses the search unless a preview owns the keys.

## Visual evidence

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c8c7af28-555e-4083-b82a-90e505747b8b


## How to test

1. Turn on 10xer mode. Turn Include subfolders off. Open a folder that contains a nested file whose name does not appear in the current directory, and commit an `f` filter that hides that nested file.
2. Press `s`, type part of the nested file's name, and press Enter. The footer shows `search:` and the hit count, the nested file is listed, and it is focused but not opened.
3. Press Enter again and confirm the focused hit opens through the normal open action.
4. Search again, press Escape from the prompt while it still has text, and confirm the hits stay. Press Escape from the listing and confirm the earlier `f` filter returns.
5. Press `s` and Escape with an empty prompt. The search does not stay, and the earlier filter is unchanged.
6. With hits showing, move with `j` and `k` (and the icon direction keys in Icons). Press `g g`, `G`, and `g f`. `g f` opens the hit's folder with that item selected and clears the search.
7. Open Network or another location with no local path and press `s`. The footer reports `Nothing to search`.

**Expected result:** Search stays inside the current folder tree, caps the visible hits, restores the previous filter on dismiss, and keyboard motion acts on the hits rather than the hidden directory.

## Related issue

https://github.com/wmfeht/strata/issues/48

https://github.com/wmfeht/strata/issues/49
title: feat(tenxer): search the current folder tree from the footer

## Description

Adds an "Always use for this file type" checkbox to the Open With dialog, as requested in the issue (Nautilus-style, footer-left of the action row, unchecked by default).

When checked, the selected application is registered via `AppInfo::set_as_default_for_type` for each of the selection's content types before it launches. Unchecked behavior is unchanged.

Details:

- Shown in all Open With paths: item context menu, multi-select, the folder background menu (`inode/directory`), and the activation-fallback chooser when no default exists.
- A multi-type selection records the default for each distinct content type.
- A failed `mimeapps.list` write logs a warning; the file still opens.

2. The file opens in the chosen application, and `~/.config/mimeapps.list` gains `<type>=<app>.desktop` under `[Default Applications]`.

author: wmfeht
body:
## Description

In 10xer mode, `g Space` now opens a footer `go ›` prompt for a known destination. Before, it toggled the selection.

Typing never navigates. Enter submits through the same navigation as the location bar (Ctrl+L). A path can be absolute, start with `~`, or be relative to the open local folder, with `.` and `..` handled like `cd`. A path that names a file opens its folder with the file selected. URIs are submitted unchanged, except that a password typed in the URI moves into the mount operation and does not stay in the location. A missing or unreachable destination shows the location bar's existing error and keeps the current folder open. Esc cancels without navigating. Clicking a listing row ends the prompt and keeps that selection. The entry is cleared on submit, Esc, focus loss, a replacing prompt, and mode exit. It keeps no undo history, so reopening the prompt or opening another window cannot bring back typed credentials.

Tab and Shift+Tab cycle forward and backward through folders (never files) that match the typed prefix. With no slash, matches come from the current listing. After a slash they come from the parent folder, and `~` means home. Matching ignores case. Hidden folders appear when the listing shows them or when the prefix starts with `.`. Each completion keeps the typed form and ends in `/`, so the next Tab descends. The footer shows the position in the cycle (`2 of 5`) or why nothing changed.

Enumeration outside the current listing runs as cancellable background GIO work and shows `Listing folders…` while it runs. Editing, cancelling, submitting, leaving the mode, or closing the window drops pending work, and a late answer never changes the text. Enumeration stops at 16,384 entries or 1,024 matching folders. A read error or an exceeded limit leaves the text unchanged and shows a hint. URI-like input (a scheme, `//host`, `\\host`, or `user@host:`) is never completed, mounted, or probed.

## Visual evidence


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bb695c04-cb82-4158-81e5-9fdec840540d



## How to test

1. Turn on 10xer mode and open a local folder that has a few subfolders with a shared prefix, for example `alpha`, `alps`, and `beta`.
2. Press `g Space`. The footer shows `go ›` and the selection does not change.
3. Type `al` and press Tab several times, then Shift+Tab. The text cycles through `alpha/` and `alps/` in both directions and the footer shows `1 of 2` / `2 of 2`.
4. Type `~/` and press Tab. Home folders are offered. Type a prefix that matches nothing and press Tab. The text stays and the footer shows `No matching folders`.
5. Enter `..` or a relative subfolder and press Enter. That folder opens. Enter a path to a file and confirm its folder opens with the file selected.
6. Enter a path that does not exist. The location error dialog appears and the current folder stays open.
7. Type `sftp://user:secret@example.invalid/` and press Tab. The footer shows `URIs are not completed` and nothing is mounted. Press Esc, reopen with `g Space`, and confirm the prompt is empty. Try the same with focus loss and with leaving 10xer mode.

**Expected result:** `go ›` only navigates on Enter. Tab completes folders without blocking or changing text late, and typed text, including credentials, is never kept after the prompt closes.

## Related issue

https://github.com/wmfeht/strata/issues/50

https://github.com/wmfeht/strata/issues/51
title: feat(tenxer): navigate typed paths from the footer with folder completion

author: wmfeht
body:
## Description

In 10xer mode, **z** opens a footer `jump ›` prompt and **Z** opens `recent ›`. Both pick a folder from Strata's own saved navigation history (the same history as the default map's Ctrl+Shift+K), not a zoxide database.

**z** ranks by name match first, then by how often and how recently each folder was opened. **Z** keeps matching folders in last-visit order. The folder already open is left out. Candidates list above the footer for any input, including empty, with the first one chosen. Up/Down choose another row (wrapping) while the entry keeps focus, and Enter or a click opens the chosen folder once. Editing the text lists fresh candidates and chooses the first again. A miss shows `No matching folders`, and Enter then leaves the prompt open without navigating. Esc, focus loss, a replacing prompt, and leaving the mode close the prompt without opening a candidate.

The candidate list reuses the location bar's completion popover styling. That popover's glow now follows **Settings → Appearance → Effects → Element glow**, which also fixes the location bar completion popover ignoring it.

A few visual tweaks ride along. An armed chord now shows a `g-` pill with a panel over it that lists each valid second key as a keycap beside its action, replacing the inline line of hints. The panel never takes focus, so the next key still completes the chord. The **10X** pill moves to the footer's far right corner, with the `g-` pill beside it. In 10xer mode, List and Icons no longer show their pane header (back, forward, and up buttons with the folder title); the top bar breadcrumb already names the folder, and List keeps its column headings. **Ctrl+N** now shows or hides the sidebar in 10xer mode (Ctrl+B stays full page up), including while the preview owns the keys.

## Visual evidence


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e49629f5-c498-4c44-aba4-ca19dfca1980



## How to test

1. Turn on 10xer mode. Open a few different folders, some of them more than once, and finish in a folder you visited earlier.
2. Press **z**. The footer shows `jump ›` and a list of visited folders appears above it, without the folder you are in. The most-used folders come first.
3. Press **Down** and **Up**. The chosen row moves and wraps, the footer shows its position (`2 of 5`), and typing still edits the prompt.
4. Type part of a folder name. The list narrows, a name match comes first, and the first row is chosen again. Press **Enter**. That folder opens.
5. Press **Shift+Z**. The footer shows `recent ›` and the list is ordered by last visit.
6. Type text that matches nothing. The list disappears and the footer shows `No matching folders`. Press **Enter**. Nothing navigates and the prompt stays open.
7. Press **Esc**, reopen with **z**, press **Down**, then click a listing row. The prompt closes and the chosen folder does not open. Try the same by leaving 10xer mode (**q**).
8. Turn off **Element glow** in Settings with the prompt's list showing. The accent glow around the list goes away.
9. With the listing focused, look at the footer: **10X** sits in the far right corner. Press **g**. A `g-` pill appears with a panel over it listing keys such as `h` Home and `Space` Type a path. Press **h** to go Home, or **Esc** to cancel; either way the panel closes.
10. Switch to List (**Ctrl+3**) and Icons (**Ctrl+2**). Neither shows the back/forward/up header; List keeps its column headings. Leave 10xer mode (**q**) and the header returns.
11. In 10xer mode press **Ctrl+N**. The sidebar hides and focus stays in the files; press it again and the sidebar returns. **Ctrl+B** still pages up.

**Expected result:** `z` / `Z` open a visited folder only on Enter or a click, in frecency / last-visit order, and never act on a candidate from an earlier query or a dismissed prompt. An armed `g` chord lists its keys in a panel over the `g-` pill until it completes or is cancelled.

## Related issue

https://github.com/wmfeht/strata/issues/52
title: feat(tenxer): jump to visited folders with z and Z

body:
Follows up on the rail mechanism from #1181.

What changed and why: in Columns view with the preview open, dragging a column's resize edge across the width threshold collapsed and restored the sidebar rail every frame (216px <-> 44px, several transitions per drag). The rail block now freezes engage/restore while the resize gesture is active, measures against the parent width with a restore margin covering the reclaimed sidebar width, and bases rail demand on standard column widths so user-widened columns scroll instead of collapsing the sidebar. author: wmfeht
body:
## Description

10xer mode gets its file verbs.

- **y** / **x** yank or cut the focused pane's fill, or its cursor item when nothing is filled, including on **f** / **s** results. Hovered rows, parent folders, and a Miller column's open-path marker are never targets. Empty folders flash `Nothing to yank` / `Nothing to cut`.
- Copied items now show the copy icon in place of their thumbnail (scissors still win for cut) in Columns, List, Icons, and search results, across windows. **Ctrl+C** / **Ctrl+X** keep their default behavior and set the same marks. Marks go away when another application takes the clipboard.
- **Y** / **X** clear the marks and release the clipboard only while Strata still owns it.
- **c c** / **c n** copy paths / names through a new `c-` chord with its own key panel. **Y** no longer copies a path in 10xer mode.
- **p** pastes with Keep Both focused on conflicts when it is offered (copies only); otherwise Replace is focused. **P** and **Ctrl+V** focus Replace. Pasting uses the same destination as **Ctrl+V** and does not change pointer/keyboard ownership. An empty clipboard flashes `Nothing to paste`.
- **d** / **Delete** now ask before moving to Trash. **D** / **Shift+Delete** (and **d** inside Trash) show the permanent-delete confirmation with Cancel focused, and finishing the size calculation no longer moves focus to the delete button. Empty folders flash `Nothing to delete`.
- **a** opens `create ›`. Enter creates an empty file with the exact name typed (spaces and Unicode kept), or a folder when the name ends in `/`. Invalid or taken names (including broken links) keep the prompt open with the reason; nothing is renumbered, replaced, or followed. Esc, focus loss, a clicked row, another prompt, and leaving the mode discard it. **Ctrl+Shift+N** is unchanged.

Context-menu hints, the F1 reference, and Settings → Keybindings list the new keys.

## Visual evidence

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/884e01f1-4bcd-4e33-bd07-2b13d35b787c

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5a9004ba-93e2-4a63-b21d-ece16651bd19


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/667c0ed9-a0f4-4105-b27e-2b84a9722d32



## How to test

1. Turn on 10xer mode in a folder with a few disposable files and a subfolder that already contains one of them.
2. With nothing selected, press **y** on a file: its thumbnail becomes the copy icon. Press **Space** on two other files, move the cursor elsewhere, and press **x**: only the two filled files show scissors. Open a second window on the same folder; it shows the same marks.
3. Press **Y**: the marks and the **Files on clipboard** pill disappear. Yank again, copy some text in another application, and confirm the marks disappear and **X** does not clear that text.
4. Press **c**: a `c-` pill lists `c` Copy path and `n` Copy name. **c c** / **c n** put the path / name on the clipboard.
5. Yank the conflicting file, enter the subfolder, and press **p**: the conflict dialog opens with **Keep Both** focused. Close it and nothing changes. **P** and **Ctrl+V** open it with **Replace** focused. Cut a conflicting file and press **p**: Keep Both is not offered and Replace is focused.
6. Cut a non-conflicting file and paste it elsewhere with **p**: it moves only then, and its mark disappears. **Ctrl+Z** moves it back.
7. Press **d**: a Move to Trash confirmation opens; Esc keeps the file, and confirming trashes it. **Ctrl+Z** restores it. Press **D**: Cancel is focused and **Enter** cancels.
8. Press **a**, type `notes.txt`, and press **Enter**: an empty file is created. Try `sub/` (folder), an existing name, `..`, and `a/b`: invalid or taken names keep the prompt open with the reason. Type a name and click a row, or press **Esc**: nothing is created.

**Expected result:** file verbs act only on the filled selection or the cursor item, confirm before deleting, never overwrite or renumber without a choice, and clipboard marks match what Strata actually holds.

author: wmfeht
body:
## Description

In 10xer mode, each **Esc** press now ends exactly one interaction, in the order the Escape precedence spec lists.

- One precedence chain now handles every listing Escape. Dialogs, the shortcut reference, text fields (including inline rename and new-folder entries), autoscroll, footer prompts, armed chords, and preview key ownership still get Escape first, as before.
- An open folder peek now closes **before** any filter, search, highlight, visual, or preview step. Before this change it closed only after all of those.
- Ordinary listing and **f** results: a visual range over the **f** results (keeps the fill) → filter → find highlights → visual (keeps the fill) → preview → selection.
- Recursive **s** results: visual (keeps the fill) → find highlights → preview → results. Dismissing the results restores the earlier **f** filter, and that same press doesn't clear it.
- Esc from the sidebar or a header control takes the same steps. Clearing a filter or closing the preview from there returns focus to the file list.
- When nothing is left to dismiss, **Esc** does nothing. It no longer closes the deepest Miller column (for example, one opened with **i**), and it never closes the window.

`docs/10xer-mode.md` now says that Escape does nothing once nothing is left to dismiss, and that the sidebar and header controls take the same steps.

## Visual evidence

Pending: no recording has been captured yet. The owner will attach a short recording through the GitHub editor.

## How to test

1. Turn on 10xer mode in a folder with a few files and a subfolder.
2. Press **Space** on a file, then **f**, type part of another file's name, **Enter**, then **i** to preview it. Press **Esc** repeatedly: the filter clears first, then the preview closes, then the fill clears. Each press ends one thing.
3. Press **/**, type a name, **Enter** (highlights), then **v**, then **i** on a file. **Esc** removes the highlights, then leaves visual mode (the fill stays), then closes the preview, then clears the fill.
4. Commit an **f** filter, then run an **s** search that finds a nested file. Press **i**, then **v**, then **Esc** four times: visual ends, the preview closes, the search results go away and the **f** filter comes back, and then the filter clears.
5. In List or Icons, set up a filter and press **i** on a folder to open the peek. **Esc** closes only the peek, and the filter stays.
6. Commit an **f** filter that shows several files, move to one, and press **v**. **Esc** leaves visual mode and the filter stays. The next **Esc** clears the filter.
7. In Columns, press **i** on a folder to open the next column. Keep pressing **Esc**: the fill clears, and after that the column stays open and the window stays open.

**Expected result:** each **Esc** removes exactly the next state in the list above. Nothing else changes, and focus stays in the file list.

## Related issue

https://github.com/wmfeht/strata/issues/61
title: feat(tenxer): end exactly one interaction per Escape press
